From the very start, this team built more than a robot - they built a teamwide MACHINE fueled by purpose, precision, and HEART. With a bold splash of GREEN and a spirit as strong as a SHAMROCK, this team shows that when preparation meets passion, magic follows.

These competitors have been building something special from the GROUND UP. Following a significant drop in membership, they “rebuilt” their team into a thriving community, empowering new members, developing future leaders, and creating a welcoming space where every student contributes. Rising from the BASEMENT to new heights, this team truly earns their place among the stars.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team builds with engineering rigor, where sustainability is designed in from the START, Through modular reuse, process discipline, and structure across every PART They create resilient systems that adapt, recover, and SCALE, Delivering long-term impact through engineering that will not FAIL.

Spirit is not just about being loud. This award goes to a small team where everyone cares about each other. They embrace their neurodivergence and were candid with the judges about how things stay tight-knit despite the occasional struggle. The team spirit award goes to the shifting brains of 10339 – Brain Shift

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Engineering is more than what you build, it’s also how you build it. With comprehensive documentation and complete student ownership, they can explain the entire robots, from NOSE to PRE-HENSILE TAIL Engineering with precision, personality, and a little bit of FUNK

In a program where competition is fierce, this “A”-mazing team proves that kindness and collaboration are just as powerful as any robot on the field. This team lifts others as they climb—helping a fellow team design sweaters to fund their Championship journey. This winning team also hosts mock competitions where teams don’t just learn—they compete, grow, and have a ROARING good time. With a supportive BEAR spirit, they don’t just build robots—they build a legacy.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team roams the field, making defense look like a walk in the JURASSIC park. What they created was a fuel deflector that “REX” the plans of every shooter trying to score. Their creative solution makes this competition feel like DINO-mite.

This team’s robot is a masterclass in industrial execution, pairing elegant design with the relentless reliability required to withstand the rigors of the field. Their commitment to technical excellence is evident on every part, ensuring a robot that performs with surgical precision match after match. Always BLUE, always BOLD, and always BUILDING to a higher standard

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Control excellence was everywhere on this field, but one team pushed their vision system a step further. When every millisecond matters, they made sure their robot never blinked, with a student-designed camera PCB delivering low-latency, high-rate updates to power their advanced controls

This team uses autonomy to create symbiosis between the human and robot. Their reliable, zone-based state machine handles details like automatically retracting the hood so the driver can stay focused. Their operator can trim the turret on the fly so the robot can shoot accurately. Working together, both robot and human perform with EAGLE-like precision

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team left us pondering an alternative reality. ROBOT, INTAKE, HOPPER, SHOOTER -- They showed how their MACHINE was IN LINE to score BUCKETS of “kernels” With a buttery Team Update and a cart that makes them POP, We'll always come back, WADDLING for more.

This team has truly set the standard -- demonstrating exceptional enthusiasm for outreach and for spreading the FIRST mission. They have worked tirelessly to break down barriers, both within their local communities and across the globe. As one of the largest teams here, they have delivered impact on an equally large scale. Their professionalism and dedication in ensuring that people from all backgrounds have access to STEM opportunities is nothing short of inspiring. By TURNING SUCCESS INTO ACTION, they have strengthened engagement in the robotics community close to home. And their efforts in doing so are second to none. So, to add a little more GOLD to their PURPLE AND GOLD...

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Through STEAM fairs and summer camps, this team GROWS the next generation of engineers. They bring back what they LEARN through internships with their sponsors, reinvesting in their community. After 15 years of COLLABORATION, this team is “TRUVY” an inspiration to us all.
This team took a spin on their robot design. Their beveled bumpers built a beefy barricade for the boxy bot. Turning the tides of competition.
Late nights in a garage, creating robots with might, They honor women scientists who inspired the fight. A small team, full of positivity and cheer — Watch them fly to new heights this year.
These rising stars reused old parts, proving that innovation doesn’t always start new. Sometimes it’s rediscovered - they revived a robotics program with PREHISTORIC roots.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This scrappy team may be young, but they’re already forging a powerful impact in their community. They collaborate with other teams while HAMMERING out opportunities for students everywhere. With a drive that’s anything but rusty, they continue to weld together innovation, outreach, and opportunity. You might know them for their solid as steel grant list or their wildly popular estimation jar game, these MANIACS really know how to stir up excitement! They prove that a little madness and a lot of metal can build something truly extraordinary.
This team in red rotates positions to uplift their kin. A pride that cheered for every team with a grin. These LIONS roared loud above the din.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The judges agree that this team’s design process allowed their subsystems to work seamlessly. Each design choice reflected clear priorities, testing, a strong iteration in mechanical and software, and a commitment to growing “CUBS”. This was a true KODIAK moment in engineering excellence!
Scouting for teams who are parched from the heat of competition; These ace veterans use their knowledge and skill to help keep other teams afloat. ORANGE you glad that you can CITRUS-T them?

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was looking for new solutions from the JUMP. Careful choice of material for their many 3D prints and a unique wire spool let them LEAP ahead of the competition.

In this high contact and collision game, this team built to withstand the competition. Boasting a high accuracy in pit, their match performance lived up to it. This small team CLAWED their way to perfect aim, sending fuel pouncing to the hub with precision.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The best control systems are the ones you almost don't notice — because everything simply works. This team created an intuitive roadmap to every electrical component, making troubleshooting fast, precise, and impossible to miss. With color coded zip ties marking every path, finding the right connection is always just a MATTER OF TIME.
Shooting a stream of fuel, their robot uses a sonar to see the hub while simultaneously SWIMMING through the seas of competition. We’re E-E-E-EXCITED to say…

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You can’t miss this brave defender in their pit or on the field. Their detailed artwork and creative pit displays shine brighter than polished armor. By bringing myth to metal they forged a legendary look in BRONZE and creativity.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: With the spark of innovation, this team rolled up their robotic sleeves to bring STEM directly into the hearts of their underserved community- creating and executing hands-on experiences that attract young, magnetic minds. They’ve made learning an adventure, even in their local fields and farms where STEM opportunities are few and far. Their impact isn’t just felt - it’s measured. Every event, every workshop, every initiative is designed to make a close and personal difference, planting seeds of curiosity that bloom into lasting STEM engagement. And through these hands-on programs that are fully supported by local organizations, they’re growing something even bigger: a sustainable orchard that ensures the next generation of innovators is ready join their team’s journey. This red, white, and blue inspiration is shaping the STEM future of their community through FLL teams, Girl Scouts, children’s museums, and summer camps. This team is forging more than just robots - they’re forging futures and proving what it means to be strong, committed, and forged for greatness.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Planting seeds of STEM at local farmers markets, this student-led team cultivates curiosity wherever they go. By weaving personal passion projects into their outreach, they’ve not only inspired their community, they’ve also built a robust mentorship program that ensures their rookies flourish in the world of engineering. They actively mentor FIRST teams from their own backyard to across the globe. And when school policies forced them into a garage workspace, they didn't just adapt; they thrived. The Engineering Inspiration award goes to team 2854, The Prototypes.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: This team's robot is so smart it basically does its own math homework. This winning design uses advanced vision control and filtering to make autonomous decisions that put most human eyesight to shame. Their COOL-LOOKING BOT is more than just a pretty face—it's a masterclass in redundancy and efficiency that literally unfurls success right on the field. Shining brighter than a new set of gears and moving fast, the Industrial Design Award goes to Team #604, Quixilver!

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: With a team made up of neurodivergent students, any task can become a struggle. But on this small, tight-knit team, snacks and basketball breaks are the key to making progress and having fun. Their robot helps out by recruiting for them, driving into classrooms with invitations to spark interest. The award for getting their BRAINS SHIFTED into gear goes to

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: From a tight-knit and hardworking community, this Rookie team stepped up the challenge. With prior robotics experience, they didn’t stay set in their ways. In a season about rebuilding, they took what they knew and pushed forward into something bigger. They adapt fast and keep raising the bar. For boldly taking on the next level, the Rookie All-Star Award goes to Team 11247, Alisal High School Robotics Team.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: This team has already taken their BYTE-sized rookie steps and is ready to continue their time here in FRC. Donating technology to those who need it most and starting FLL teams in their area, they have taken PRIDE in reaching out in the community. When it comes to rising to the top, this team is PURRR-fect.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has shown a lot of METTLE in their practices and they don’t let anything go to waste - even their METAL shavings. Their positivity has helped them to rise from tough losses, and become a sustainable team that’s here to stay.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: FIRST is more than just robots, and spirit is more than just cheering. This team shows DEEP passion for their agricultural community - meeting people where they are even if they don't study STEM. It's also where WE celebrate today, because the Team Spirit Award winner is our host

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: These engineers reached for the stars by pairing thoughtful design with exceptional system integration. Through purposeful prototyping, clear documentation, streamlined subsystem unit testing, advanced vision tracking, and a portable calibration rig, these cookies baked up a SUPERNOVA of engineering excellence.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: Contrary to their name, this team has exhibited not FURY but GRACE and GENEROSITY. Be it giving away spares or helping a fellow team with a stylus, this team has traded all of their WRATH for FINESSE.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's performance on the field has been so intense it threatens to BLOW A CIRCUIT! They managed to belt out a hybrid indexer design and a launcher so "FLIPPING" cool that it can fire from either side of the field without losing its cool. For a design that truly breaks the mold without blowing a fuse, the creativity award goes to Team 6059, System Overload!

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: When this hound is on the hunt, it noses out fuel cells like treats. Once the fuel in its clenches, no bot shoots them out faster. They sink their teeth into every detail of their robot with the same relentless energy. When they compete on the field, their performance is on FIRE

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Before each match, every motor runs its CHECK. Slow subsystems caught before they WRECK. One button knows the period, the position, the PLAY. Built by the driver who designed it their own WAY. Some teams build in garages, some in schools down the HALL. The most innovative control this year came from an abandoned MALL.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.script: Others brought cameras and turrets GALORE. This team brought math, odometry, and settled the SCORE. Good wasn’t enough, so they tore it APART. Rebuilt in two weeks with a shooter and HEART. A solver so sharp it made turrets look SLOW. Eiko Squared just knew where the fuel had to GO.

records.eventName: CA District Pinnacles Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The pit, cart and robot all match their theme. This team has gone all-in on their rebrand and found whatever materials they can to decorate with, like Pool noodles, Coral, and Algae. So stop by their pit and you will definitely “C” some OTTERS.

This team is impactful as an asteroid. It may be a dinosaur, but it is not extinct. It makes an impact on its community by ensuring everyone can afford to be part of a LEGO league, and offers its resources to help its community.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Engineering inspiration needs student determination with mentoring and with community events. Following their STEM trail, their butterfly system depicts the metamorphosis from caterpillar to cocoon to butterfly. This team took their machine "La Ball James" to the largest FTC kickoff.

For a solid robot design, teams need to both have good ideas, but also have the ability to track the many pieces and bring them into one harmonious whole. This team brought together pieces from its community and joined it to their design aesthetic. The resulting hail of fuel let them bring the fires of the underworld to the west with their robot, Cerberus.

The judges award captures an aspect of a team that is not captured elsewhere. This team was in the trenches helping other teams who were in distress, from failing software to other team’s impact presentation equipment. Their presence was as comforting and nourishing as a bite from a fresh bagel on a Sunday morning.
Their roster turned over one year, But quitting? That's not their frontier. They logged on and learned, New members they earned— All hail the team that rose with the sun!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Like birds preparing to leave the nest, this team nurtures ideas until they hatch and take flight. They have built a program where students grow, leadership spreads, and their program will keep them flying for years to come.
Their passion just can't be contained New FTC teams they have trained, Sensory packs flow, To statehouses they go, And their Phoenix makes sure spirit's sustained!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: A well-engineered robot should perform well on the field, but what happens in the pits is just as important. Maintainability and system checks between matches helped ensure this team's sustained performance. This alloy of capabilities allowed this giant robot to keep stomping on the competition.

Here at FIRST, we believe you can compete like crazy while still treating others with respect, kindness, and generosity. This award celebrates a team that demonstrated outstanding respect, teamwork, and a strong spirit of Coopertition — always willing to help others while giving their best on the field. Their actions throughout the event showed what Gracious Professionalism truly looks like in our community.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Good engineering mixes technical knowledge with creativity. Sometimes we need to sail out to the edge of the known world to try out a new idea, as this team did. Their turret design was a low-wire act that a hundred minions could not improve upon.

This simple but refined robot created a buzz both on and off the field. Their innovative indexer had fuel racing to feed their robot. For a build that is truly strong as steel, the quality award goes to Team 9425 the Steel Stingers.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Robots can sometimes seem to have a mind of their own, and teams hope that the robot performs the way they intended. This team took it a step farther and had a turret that thought that the world should revolve around it. The flurry of fuel into the hopper verified their approach. To really make this work and be one with their robot, a team has to be a cat from the next universe.
This robot was fast, strong, and was one of the few teams that even took to the air. It navigated around the field as if it had X-ray vision. It's a bird! It's a plane! It's SUPER-NURDS!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team didn't just build a robot; they curated an entire tropical experience. They hit Hueneme with a wave of spirit, and their competitors can still be seen wearing those colorful leis all over the stands! They are the very image of a Mechanical Paradise.

This team has answered the call by bringing STEM directly to those who need it most. Their mission is clear: representation matters and access should never depend on gender, race, or wealth. They've built alliances, mentored teams, and secured lasting support across their district, ensuring FIRST is not just a program but a movement. Because when outreach is intentional, data-driven, and led by students, it can be more than a program - it can be a force that transforms a community. Guided by their Engineering Design Process, this team has SES-tamatically eliminated obstacles and isn't just making robots - they are making an impact

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team treats engineering as loud, hands on, and a little contagious to help turn their community into a workshop of possibility. From running summer camps to mentoring FLL teams, they prove pipelines of talent are laid early. For building more than robots and scaling up a culture of making, the Engineering Inspiration award is presented to team 4698, Raider Robotics.

This team kneads only a few seconds to rise and make the hub hot as an oven. Their robot never goes stale. Even after their intake was toasted by a collision. Opposing teams will feel a little sourdough when this team bags up the match.
This team has a sense of style. They exhibit co-opertition with an app that turns the world purple. It's time to tip our hats.

This tam proving that passion and determination matter more than resources. With a robot built from passed-down parts from partner team and adapting an FTC camera for vision, they take on every challenge. Full of energy. fearless thinking, and unstoppable curiosity - this is true WARRIOR power!

This team doesn't just build robots here at FIRST, they FORGE legends. Despite being a young team, they are well oiled, creating strong bonds with other FRC teams and hosting a summer camp with LEGO robots. Starting with a SPARK we beliece they will grow into a raging inferno.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team shows that the best ENGINEERING practices create something that endures. Growing their team from 10 members to over 80, they have nested strong systems for future members to grown in. For this team, sustainability is nothing to SQUAK about.

This team has a way of bringing people together — and their spirit always comes full circle. Their boundless enthusiasm made every interaction feel like a celebration - and through exceptional partnerships, they carried the mission of FIRST far beyond the competition floor. When it comes to packing big spirit into every byte, this team proved that even a small team can leave a big mark.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team SOARED above the rest in both machine design and fabrication. a FORCE to be reckoned with, their robot excelled at both intake and fuel delivery. This bot was engineered to spread its WINGS and fly.

This team’s enthusiasm to collaborate SOARS high. Their dedication to inclusivity and working together consistently takes FLIGHT. They collaborate with various teams throughout the season for technical and outreach events. Their sportsmanship takes FLIGHT on the field through communication and planning in advance. There is no holding back on sharing their passion and robot for any members approaching their purple wings.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's PRESENTATION of the robot wowed the judges with its unique design solutions and well-articulated engineering design process. They showed how creative thinking can lead to easy servicing and functional results. Their ideas stops fuel cells from invading into their electrical systems.

Building the robot is only part of their success and the judges recognize them as a quality example to others. Through their robust design configurations and their custom gearboxes, this team ensures their robot withstands the rigor of competition like the stallion it is.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team proudly waves their flags. With a turret loyal to making shots, this team establishes a unique approach to their adjustable hood. When it comes to control, this team is PATRIOTIC.

This team JUICED every fuel it saw in autos. Their robot put up a rock solid counter reaction to any defensive measures against it. When it comes to scoring triple digits, you always want them as your partner in LIME.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From their bold colored machines to their signature shirts, this team doesn’t just show up - they show out, with a style that is anything but ordinary. Their commitment to visual identity is total - every robot, every shirt, every dolly, and even the way they hand out pins tells the same unmistakable story. When it comes to packing personality into every rivet, this team proved that their brand of funk is in a class of its own.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Growing their community means everything to this team. Their year-round outreach effort not only includes volunteering but also hosting FIRST competitions and finding new partners. Their professionalism and eagerness to help make them the go-to team. The judges were GREEN with envy when they heard about the team’s 15 NEW THINGS.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: The animal kingdom is well represented in FIRST. Summer camps, FLL mentoring, exploring engineering in the community are just a few things they do. With strategically located FRIENDS, they have reached a new height. We can hardly wait to see what RARE BIRDS can solve with their integrated product teams.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: In a community where access to STEM opportunities can be limited, this team saw not a barrier, but a responsibility. They identified the gap and got to work, bringing meaningful STEM experiences directly to underserved students and families. They don’t just run programs, they build pathways. By hosting STEM fairs and inviting sponsors to participate, they create a visible journey of opportunity, showing young learners what their future in STEM can look like and how to get there. Whether they’re sharing STEM in classrooms or riding the rhythm of “Music in the Park,” this team meets their community where they are, making learning accessible, engaging, and fun. You might think they’re just a group of block heads… …but we think they’re building something extraordinary.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Good industrial design is a mix of an overarching vision and an attention to many details. This robot really turned the judges’ heads all the way around with their slick integration of many creative components to maximize fuel capacity. They truly created an EPIC robot.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Sometimes a team invents something and the judges realize it is so unusual that there is no existing award that fits it. That was true for this team, which created automation software running off the robot to benefit not just themselves, but other teams as well. This project definitely gave teams a Vector to better alliance selection.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: While most rookies are mere sparks, this team has ignited with a luminosity that outshines a galaxy of stars. By engineering a "central engine" of sustainability, they have triggered an explosive debut responsible for scattering FIRST Core Values and forging technical excellence across the region. When it comes to a massive collapse of boundaries and a brilliant release of professional power, this team is a total blast.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Robots are not the only things this team builds. They also build confidence and community. They may not have started with an abundance of resources, But they are FLYING to new heights with a BUZZING group of mentors and shared documentation. This SWARM OF HORNETS surely have a bright future!

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team demonstrates that long-term success is built through discipline, with detailed documentation and systems designed to last beyond a single season. Their well-structured procurement program ensures resources are managed with foresight and accountability, creating stability for the future. They are clad in blue and embodying the precision of the sword.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Dressed in Macedonian blue, this team can be heard from the pits to the Aegean sea. Their enthusiasm and team inclusivity embody the meaning of team spirit. They galvanize a wave of excitement that can't be contained.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Building a FIRST robot requires planning and discipline. This team took that to another level with detailed tracking of parts and was able to predict, based on data, when a part should be replaced. This diligence was reflected in their placement in the competition. When the judges saw all this, the only thing they could say was, ‘Holy Cow”!

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: From their daily greetings, and smiling faces to the apprehension from so many other teams and assistance they give to other teams, this team leaps above the Waves to launch everyone into Outer Space.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's design is as bold as their coloration. Their interleaved shooter and unique conveyor let them move fuel so fast, you'd think they are in two places at once. All together now: when I say twenty-one, you say (oh two)!

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team has embedded processes throughout their engineering lifecycle to ensure a robust robot. From tracking part fabrication and verification to stress testing and color-coding their wires, quality is built in. This team's process has proved extremely FRUITful, allowing them to SURF their way to success.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team's holistic design combined a large hopper with a compact turret. They made a splash on the field with a constant stream of fuel, washing over the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: At this level of competition we expect that robots will have excellent ability to operate autonomously. This team took it to the next level by incorporating physics simulations to make it faster to turn around their updates of autonomous routines and to optimize their power usage. Their software process allows for adaptability, and, as they say in their documentation, “Greyt designs are never finished.”

records.eventName: FIRST California Southern State Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: FIRST teams love to show their colors. Sometimes a team we thought we knew will take rebranding to the next level by defining font, colors, and even adding a squid. In their pits, on their robot, and on their t-shirts, it's all orange and blue.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: When this team sees a problem, they fix it and share the solution. They developed and shared numerous published resources to support the FIRST community. Their hands-on outreach activities through Girl Scouts and sponsor partners grow the herd of future STEM professionals, MOOving students to make a lasting difference.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team turns awareness into action and opportunity into reality. They spark curiosity and expand access to education, hosting a walk-a-thon that highlights students who travel miles to learn, refurbishing and donating 3D printers across the globe, and promoting literacy in their community. They elevate opportunity, inspire respect for learning, and show how engineering can change lives. This team keeps the GEARS OF PROGRESS turning.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team focused on integrating its design to make a high functioning robot. Their tower electronics and spindexer are elegant and functional. Like the Star Trek’s USS Cerritos, this team is EPIC.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team works on the cutting edge of materials and technology. For robustness, they use kevlar embedded carbon fiber. Due to the diminishing supply base, they designed and fabricated their own hall effect sensor. The judges were very impressed with this ROBOT ALLIANCE FROM THE WEST.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team turned a season of change into a full on REBUILT glow-up. Powered by grassroots hustle and a whole lot of community magic, they turned uncertainty into opportunity. In every sense of the word, this team is truly a UNICORN.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team takes sustainability to the next level. Partnering with clubs in their school and serving their community gets their gears turning. It did not take a large JUMP for the judges to recognize these travelers for the energy they’ve put into improving the planet.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: In the stands and in the pits, raising funds and spirits, these WARRIORS hold strong. With bold colors and a powerful voice, they inspire both spectators and players alike. Motivating one another, building robots and community, they do whatever it takes.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team demonstrated outstanding engineering through iterative prototyping and collaborations with programming for simulations. Their dedication and resilience are reflected in their robot design. As agile as a PARROT and as strong as an OX, this team didn’t just check boxes, they engineered a machine that can soar and power through any challenge.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team shared their practice field and CNC with other FRC teams. They had collaborative conversations and feedback with other teams for design. As the only FRC team in their school district, they GEARED UP to mentor 6 FLL teams. Their positive attitude is seen on and off the field, creating a sense of community and even having time for the bus ride home.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team made a sharp point with an intentional and creative design solution leading to success on the field. Creativity is ingrained in this team with all they design. Their robot’s shooter utilized a unique top roller to control for distance and accuracy, which kept them from getting the BLUES. No problem is too TITANIC for this team to overcome.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team MARCHED through the season to design and build a reliable quality machine. The rigor of this BATTLEfield is no match for their easily swappable spares. No one can turn a blind eye to their endless volleys of fuels that BEARLY ever miss.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team knows that great control requires constantly knowing exactly where you are. They hunt for their target on the move using their NADIR proof turret and veneer encoders. This tribe is on a quest for success.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.script: This team’s robust vision system ensured very reliable auto performance. They’re electronics respond in realtime, never missing a beat during autonomous operation. With software so responsive they could pass a medical exam, this team delivered a LIFE SAVING performance.

records.eventName: CA District San Gabriel Valley Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s inclusive identity showed a strong message of unity. They are dreamers embodying passion and resilience by working together to bring STEM to their community. They rise like ROSES from between the cracks in the sidewalk.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: The FIRST Impact Award is presented to the team judged to have the most significant measurable impact of its partnerships among its participants and community over a sustained period, not just a single build season. The winner is able to demonstrate progress towards FIRST’s mission of transforming our culture. The recipient team will be invited to the District Championship where it will compete for the FIRST Impact Award against winners from other qualifying events and compete with their robot. This team’s activities and engagements are the perfect embodiment of Impact. They started with a multi-year plan to cultivate interest and engagement in their community and those efforts are starting to bear fruit. For their community, STEM and Robotics were not even on the radar until this team came along. They may be a small team, but they punch well above their weight – their impact extends from elementary to college students. They have built a sustainable program. They Seeded, They Fielded, They Grew – and now they get to harvest the Impact Award. We hope they never change their stripes!

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: If you are looking for inspiration, just talk with anybody from this team. They have made the FIRST mission their own. Not just passionate about engineering excellence, they have carefully developed plans to inspire that passion with their peers, their community, and the world. They share resources and knowledge freely and openly, bringing along as many teams as possible for the journey. Their creations are like those of a 3-star Michelin Chef, but are made available to everyone. They are always running at 110%. They are here, They are there, They are everywhere!

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Sometimes an elegant yet simple design approach yields the most effective solution. A 3-D printed base provided leverage for easy access, configuration, and repair. This team built a beautiful robot that buzzed around the field and became quite the pea shooter.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Judges' Award for Keeping Humans Relevant: This team has laser vision, throwing coconuts and making countless 3-pointers onto what seemed like a distant island. When their robot struggled some, these human players found a way to shoot their way to the winning score, proving that it takes more than just a robot to win a match.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Given a short runway, this team built, rebuilt, and were able to take off and land on the playing field. By overcoming the extreme build time crunch and through strong partnerships, collaborations and cooperations, this team is an inspiration to their school and community, implementing the Mission of FIRST to advance science and technology. With wings of a SAINT, qualifying to compete for the Rookie All-Star Award at the District Championship, we congratulate:

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team took the “Rebuilt” challenge to a new level. After facing significant mentor and team member losses, this team re-invigorated itself by developing new engineering pathways and incorporating FIRST and STEM more deeply into their curriculum. We applaud their commitment to “rise once again.”

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: All teams build robots, but this team has built something far bigger – a living pipeline of future teammates, engineers, and leaders which grows stronger every year. Dedicated sub teams and a program built specifically to champion women in STEM, ensure that every member finds a place to belong and learn. Clear plans for each team member cultivate the next generation of captains and mentors, long before their graduation day. This is not a team that simply hopes for the future, this is a team that engineers it.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Their energy was impossible to miss – bright, bold, and infectious. They lit up the stands with their enthusiasm and spirit which truly embodies FIRST’s mission. With flags flying and cheers that never let up, their presence made every match more thrilling. They gave us the kind of energy we would replay just to see bright pink again.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team engineered a clean, highly effective design that excels at collecting large volumes of fuel balls while delivering rapid, precise shots from anywhere on the field. Built for resilience, their robot withstands the gameplay rigors and enables quick, efficient repairs. Their robot is a joy to watch, their performance truly speaks for itself – smooth, controlled, and remarkably fluid, gliding across the field with the grace and confidence of cetaceans.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Embracing FIRST’s core values drove this team to advocate for expanding STEM, special education, and FIRST at elementary schools in their community. They will drop everything to help each other and other teams by fixing mechanical issues and providing resources to learn new skills. By creating a database of grants, they expanded the financial resources available to all teams because they are Maniacs when it comes to Gracious Professionalism.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took a different spin when designing their shooting mechanism. Their colorful approach let them swivel without limits and not get wrapped up by those pesky, annoying wires. A completely untangled longship was deployed.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team clearly identified key operational requirements early on and developed a robust hardware and software system to meet the challenges of the game. Their robot incorporates innovative solutions across all aspects, and their execution looks stunning. They introduced a creative solution to take the zap out of static electricity. Like modern explorers navigating the digital world of robotics, they pursue excellence by focusing on details that clearly elevated their bot.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team simulated everything before they built anything, then calibrated it all with interpolation tables. Mechanical energy storage devices took the drama out of shooting, and a custom controller paired with a visual signaling system means that the operators barely have to think. They didn’t just write clever code; they built a comprehensive “control eco-system,” from simulation to operator eyeballs.

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Picking the best mode for the situation can be challenging, but these metalworkers can show us how. One, two, three shooters for the win!

records.eventName: CA District San Diego Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team integrates many diverse students under one consistent marketing theme. Their branding standards and team identity provide a creative twist for their host school. It’s no “wookie” mistake – please use your applause to send this team to hyperspace!

Some teams climb the mountain. This team carved a path so others could climb it, too. When they saw barriers to FIRST participation in the Bay, they did not wait for the fog to lift. They cleared it. They built common ground; a shared home where teams could practice, collaborate, and grow. They proved the vision, forged the partnerships, raised the support, and turned an idea into something lasting. These leaders knew that a true clan only prospers when they help their neighbors rise. They shared their secret scrolls of scouting strategy and their digital training manuals with every team in the land, ensuring that as they grew, they pulled the whole community up with them. Like the old names carried by their machines, their story feels legendary. But their real magic is simple: they make more people believe they belong. The FIRST Impact Award goes to Team 8033!

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has SET the bar for inspiring their community and beyond. Their outreach efforts start in the community, mentoring FLL and making specialized mobility karts for toddlers. However, they haven't stopped there. They've advocated for STEM at a government level meeting with Assembly and Congress members. Their extensive work educating and promoting STEM has reached across the seas to places like India, Mexico, and Kenya. They are truly making a splash everywhere they go.

Something in the pits has been turning heads and breaking expectations. Their three-wide shooter with inertia flywheels creates high throughput in different locations. Design optimization with SRPP panels show off their strategic manufacturing. With inseparable form and function, you’ll never catch this bot breaking.

This small and scrappy team has been quietly empowering the competition. Their eagerness to share their ambitious designs really made us take notice. Their codebase deployed with Docker would impress a seasoned software engineer. When it comes to passion for engineering, this team is already powered up.

This rookie team’s accomplishments are the result of more than just luck. Building a team of 30 enthusiastic students, forging a partnership with a cross-town rival, and reaching out to local schools to spread the joy of STEAM are all projects that exemplify the spirit of FIRST. When it comes to community and heart, this team is a star.

These East Bay competitors started with nothing but drive and went looking for the rest, one teacher at a time. They knocked on every door and made their case for a space, built in a library, spilled into a parking lot, and still showed up to SF Districts ready to compete. This team proves that the biggest obstacles are no match for the right amount of determination.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has built a strong pipeline of future innovators through an FLL recruiting pathway and ensures continuity through leadership transition training. They extend STEM learning to the community through a printer dissection workshop, and show environmental stewardship by partnering with biology clubs for beach cleanups. They also creatively repurpose spare parts from STEM kits for charity events, giving materials a second life. Through community engagement, leadership development, and environmental responsibility, this team demonstrates what sustainability in FIRST truly looks like.

When it comes to Team Spirit, this team proves that great ideas don’t need to be trashed; instead, they can recycle, refine, and rebuild. This student-led team has perfectly sorted sub-groups: mechanical, programming, outreach… working together like a well-oiled ecosystem. This team isn’t just building an excellent robot; they’re building a sustainable future. Their enthusiasm is contagious, their teamwork is efficient, and their spirit leaves a small carbon footprint but makes a big impact. So when it comes to inspiration, tune your antennas and give it up for… Eco Robotics!!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: With precision, purpose, and heart on display, this team set themselves apart by helping others along the way. Their shooter was refined through iteration after iteration, paired with a clever corkscrew indexer and a 3D map of the field that elevated their execution. With a mechanism that twists like a double helix, their engineering is clearly in their DNA.

This San Francisco team doesn’t just build robots, they build community. With a robust history of mentoring and launching teams across the Bay Area, this team makes sure no one feels excluded or underappreciated. And when a team flew in from abroad without a battery and a robot in pieces, they opened their workshop and got them on the field. These birds fly in red, and always bring the whole flock with them.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This next team tends to provoke a reaction. They built their entire vision pipeline in Rust from scratch — no libraries, pure math. Their gearbox? 3D printed by design, outperforming traditional aluminum in resilience and stability.

This team’s robot was nothing short of crazy. Their shooting looked like a stream of water, and even through every bump, hit, and bit of madness on the field, they stayed strong. Match after match, they showed the kind of consistency and durability that defines true quality. With a clean, dependable design, they brought lasting quality to town.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Auto adjusting their turret to find the goal from anywhere on the field? Check Dynamically adjusting shooter speed to score from any distance? Check Using pre-loaded coordinates of obstacles on the field from an offline 3d model to adjust their robot on the fly? Check If you ask the judges, that's quite a control system.

High above the competition, one robot showed what it means to hunt with precision. It soared across the field completing cycle after cycle with perfect accuracy. With the awareness of a bird’s-eye view, it always knew exactly where it was on the field. Using machine learning to spot its prey, it tracked and hunted game pieces with pinpoint accuracy. Even when defenders tried to disrupt its flight, this robot stayed locked on target and never missed its mark. Built to soar… and ready to strike. The winner is… Team 114, Eaglestrike!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is sweet by design. Their cute and playful, bright-blue branding sets the standard and attracts aspiring, young students interested in STEAM. Their media workshops help teams capture their FIRST experiences and share them with the world. When it comes to imagery, this team bubbles to the top.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: In a region where STEM opportunities are limited and FIRST teams are scarce, one team has transformed their community. Their outreach has introduced more than 10,000 students to STEM and FIRST. Their comprehensive K through 12 pathway has resulted in additional FLL and FTC teams and expanded competition opportunities. This team’s impact doesn’t stop with them; it ripples outwards. They embody Co-opertition by sharing their knowledge and best practices around fundraising, logistics, and outreach thus enabling other teams to carry forward their own impact. The vast scope and scale of their volunteering is shown through more than 7000 volunteer hours over 3 years, making them the largest FIRST volunteer force in their area. When asked for assistance, they invariably respond, “Sure, we can find a way to help.” Most recently, that help has solved critical problems in NorCal FIRST, such as providing a venue for a key competition, volunteer staffing, and frictionless discounted access to LiveScan. Like the FIRST bird flying in a V-formation, this team is leading others to soaring success.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team really impressed the judges with their well-rounded outreach and dedication to FIRST ethos. They’ve been focusing on making measurable change through corporate and team partnerships, robot demos, FLL outreach, and BAKING female empowerment that’s out of this world. Their JAR of wonders has SWEET-TALKED the judges and helped numerous teams within this competition. They SERVE as a prime example and an INSPIRATION to all teams. Congratulations Team 1868: The Space Cookies

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: From a meticulous schedule to a polished MACHINE, this garage-built robot is brilliantly CLEAN. Using high-speed video to fix hopper JAMS, they added a crash bar to survive heavy SLAMS. Ready to force a system reboot and BRING THE HEAT, the Industrial Design Award goes to Team 9470, Ctrl Alt Defeat!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: This year’s Judges’ Award recognizes a GOLDEN STATE team that turned a ‘sophomore” slump into a “sophomore” bump. With only two members returning, this season’s roster “checked” into the game and started dropping hints. They’ve created pathways through FLL spread STEM in the community. And lowered team entry costs to turn this “rebound” into a “fast break” . We’re glad this group has taken their talents to FIRST and built a robot that shoots 3-Pointers. Congratulations team 10644 the West Coast Warriors.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: This winning team has flourished a lot the past few seasons. They have doubled in size each year for the last three years. They started a sibling team to support freshmen. They’ve become stewards of STEM at their schools They made a lasting impact on the judges with their candidness about their past struggles and their experiences of the team have changed them for the better. So, thank you for doing the difficult work to change your culture and we’re ready to see your future all start success!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Some teams talk about sustainability—this team lives it; from the way they build their robot to the way they show up for their community. Every part has a second life, every scrap finds a purpose. Even materials from neighboring clubs get pulled back into the cycle rather than thrown away. When a team turns POOL NOODLES into decorations, last year’s game pieces into life preservers, and scrap into buttons, you know the environment is in good hands---the Team Sustainability Award belongs to 6665 C-Otters.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: Some teams compete on the field – this team makes sure the entire building knows a competition is happening. From organized stands packed with noise to enthusiastic outreach, their CAN-DO attitude turns every opportunity into a moment worth showing up for. LOUD, PROUD, and TIED together in every sense of the word The team spirit award belongs to Team 1967 the Jankster!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: With a top-down design from the very START, Their full architecture is a work of ART. A packaged intake and a fifty ball-hopped, Feed four wide lanes to secure the win. When the shooters spin up, the fuel goes POOF! The Excellence in Engineering Award goes to the Cheesy Poofs!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: This team is growing a pipeline to feed their program and others. Instead of HIBERNATING during the off season, they hold a competition that helps prepare new FRC students. Helping teams in and outside of their territory, this team’s gracious professionalism is MAAW-velous. PAAWS for effect, the gracious professionalism award goes to Team 766!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their two-way shooter is just the start of this team’s creativity. Color coding, custom bumper locks, and let’s not forget about their choice of materials. On a budget, they reused past game pieces and SYSTEMATICALLY OVERLOADED their robot with 3D printing.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: While beautiful robots fill the field, this winning team spins with quality. A clear view is provided into their core mechanism. One gear feeds the next, in a cascade of clean design. The Quality Award goes to—Team 972 Iron Claw.

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Hierarchical states keep every subsystem in LINE, Kalman filters fuse sensors so navigation stays FINE, Drivers change intent-yet control is maintained by DESIGN!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.script: From trench to bump, their auto finds the WAY, With vision and state machines that guide the PLAY, Align, intake, and score—the Bulldogs lead the DAY!

records.eventName: CA District Silicon Valley Event presented by Apple
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: One team made sure you knew exactly who they were the moment they walked in the room Two years ago, they REBUILT their identity from the group up, and the result is a robot, a uniform, and a presence that move together as one unmistakable package. In a night sky full of competitors, one star burns brighter than the rest

This team makes FIRST soar in their community and beyond. They spread STEM by mentoring MANY FLL teams, brought STEM to special education students, and hosted community events. Their sustainable programs and team spirit ensures that their wingspan reaches far across Southern California.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: They built up a pipeline with care, A JV squad feeding the share. They host every age, Put girls on the stage, And their outreach graph climbs through the air. Three programs, all seasons, all year, Their volunteers always appear. New chapters revived, Old missions still thrive— The Robot Dolphins are here!

records.teamName: Jaguar Robotics Sponsored By Feit Electric
records.script: Clean, elegant, and clearly built with purpose, this robot showed what happens when great engineering meets thoughtful design. Its sleek system efficiently handled up to 100 fuel with no dead zones, and it arrived competition-ready. Their design showed a balanced form, function, and style!
This team is well-rounded and full of heart. From robots to community, they prove you don't need a wand to create something extraordinary. They bring pure magic to everything they do.

In space, rare stellar explosions release incredible energy and light across the universe. This team brought that same spark and momentum to their robotics program. Facing the pressure of the six-week build season, this team rallied their community and raised an incredible $35,000 to power their program and expand opportunities in STEM. .

This team has shown resilience in the face of uncertainty They were on the verge of slithering off into the sunset, but were able to make a trace to reconnect their circuit. This team is our rising all-star 6060 Circuit Serpent

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has blessed the FIRST Community by hosting FLL tournaments to further the pipeline. Their impact is black and white. They developed cow-munity resources that support many teams in their operations.
This team is a sea of red in the stands. They bring energy and spirit to all they do. You can hear them chant loudly for their alliances. OOIE OOHIE OTCHA their Grrrrr-eat!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Some robots just seem to understand the game. With top notch design, a laser-accurate shooting turret, and six cameras constantly reading the field this robot showed true engineering excellence and a deep understanding of the game.

Teams and communities call this team when they need help. Their work with others is always gracious and professional. Their passion for helping others and forwarding STEM in the community spreads like wildfire. Get an extinguisher because this team is on FIRE!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team engineered a feeder as cool as an icemaker. Their 3D-printed orange screw launches fuel soaring toward the hub. Let congratulations roar through the field!
The subsystem design of this robot was outstanding. With military precision, they minimized unique parts and championed simplicity. This brave team has true warriors of quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team rode the wave of excellence by developing a web app to train their automation, and successfully used this training to put points on the board. Their interface allowed rotation and mirroring for teaching, no matter where they start the match. By turning complex math into a user-friendly tool, they avoided rip currents on the field.

In teleop, this team’s automation is worthy of lore With one button, their driver can pass and score Their code can both diagnose a jam and prescribe a solution This team with white coats will win evolution.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Each season this team proudly raises their colors and builds an identity that cannot be missed. Through thoughtful design, a consistent theme, and a presence that reflects who they are, they truly forge their brand to be seen.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: These students are playing an instrumental role in breaking down obstacles to STEM for their communities. Their outreach is creating lasting, meaningful, and positive impacts locally and across the region. Embodying the mission of FIRST, they are increasing STEM access to many underserved communities, including the neurodivergent population. With a brave “YES, AND!” attitude, these DRAGONS are soaring to new heights.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: These kids went out of their way to promote STEM knowledge in a community with diverse interests From advancing societal well-being through STEM applications to a commitment to inclusivity and equal representation. With determination and purpose, these CUBS all ROAR: ROBOTICS FOR ALL

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team STICKS together and always answers the call to build a connection Their outreach and sustainability go a long way to complete this CIRCUIT Don’t get in their way, or you might meet their TREBUCHET.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team CRAFTED a monumental robot this season. They traveled into the depths, spiraling through the BLUE. They SQUARED up to the competition and came out unstoppable.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team flew down to the depths to pick up our Judges’ Award. Through designing an underwater ROV to monitor Oyster reefs, this team used undersea exploration as a vehicle to educate and inspire middle schoolers and other members of their community. From the sky to the sea, these HAWKS have boundless inspiration.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: These students have already accomplished so much on their path They are creating positive changes in their community through workshops, summer camps, and mentoring. The judges are excited to set this team FREE to compete at the next level!

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team is rising through the ranks and growing in numbers. They hosted an FLL tournament on their own and even advocated for STEM funds at both the state and federal levels. This WILD HORSE of a team is creating a STAMPEDE.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has a buddy system for training new members and a METAL CLAD budget. From kickoff to competition, they ensure every voice is heard. By bringing FIRST to schools across their community, they will keep their HIVE open for years to come.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team showed a spirited attitude that was truly VENOMOUS. Their ability to get students, their families, and sponsors involved and excited was STRIKING. These SNAKES showed incredible spirit through and through.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The judges loved how this team SWARMED the field. Their highly mature design process produced an efficient machine that performed seamlessly and reliably. Excellence comes to this team like a BEE to HONEY.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team believes that STEM literacy is for ALL. They communicate in multiple languages to support PASSENGERS of all ages. The CRAZY TRAIN for gracious professionalism departs from their maker space.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team went an ASTRONOMICAL distance to ensure the effectiveness of their robot’s design. They crossed multiple state lines to source custom bearings for their robot, building their relationship into a long-term sponsorship. Their solution SHINED in the pits and truly EXPLODED our minds with their creativity.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: This team’s detailed checklist ensures they tension their belts for precision and accuracy. In just 8 minutes, they can replace anything -- with time and parts to spare. Their strategic approach allows them to SUSHI ROLL and score maximum points on the field.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is leading the HEARD in control. Using their finely-tuned encoder to mitigate movement over the bump, they LOCK-IN to their position. Their bold vision and mastery of control ensure that ANGUS KHAN redefines what’s possible in FIRST.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.script: Throughout the match, this team SWOOPS and scores. This FLOCK has fine-tuned their autonomous routine to consistently outscore the competition. These BIRDS certainly have a reason to show their FEATHERS.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by C-CAM, VSU, Go Tec, and NASA
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team paints a picture of consistency, weaving bold colors and sharp design into every detail of their program. From pit to robot, their identity never FADES TO BLACK, always staying bright and unmistakable. With branding this vibrant and vision this sharp, it's clear this team always keeps a WATCHFUL EYE on excellence.

This team personifies the total package of FIRST on a global scale. They consistently expand and adapt their outreach to new heights. They maximize the impact and accessibility of the FIRST mission around the world by pairing STEM engagement with food security. Their GEM and LAPIS programs engage and empower girls through hands-on STEM experiences. They came, they saw, they KILT.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: A model FIRST team, inspiring near and far, this team lifts their community, school, and state with an unstoppable commitment to engineering excellence! Impacting thousands each year and spanning three continents, they pounce on “social problematics” for every challenge they encounter. The future of innovation is louder, bolder, and more inspired because of their prowess and roar.

Scoring fuel from anywhere on the field, their dual roller caught the judges’ eyes. Their design flows smoothly on the rails with clean appearance, function, and performance. With full steam ahead, this team can really fly.
This small team has helped grow a much larger community. They plant the seeds to grow STEM across a variety of environments and cultures. We are grateful that palm trees grow in Northern Arizona.

Rising from the ashes of the pandemic, this team has redefined themselves multiple times. Doubling their previous year’s size, they created a safe space and a scholarship fund for their robotics team. Living up to their name, this international team rammed their way across the map on a 20-hour bus-ride to join us.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Rooted in people, prosperity, and planet, their roar for change echoes far beyond the field! Fueled by the spirit of caring for the land, this team has created a movement. Striking with the force of nature and the heart of the planet, they are built for the future and dedicated to sustainability.

The drive to host and recruit FIRST’s message in the streets and across the world is infectious and inspiring. This robot’s strong vertebrae shined through with their consistent compassion and good nature across FIRST. This team has a pulse on the welfare and prosperity of FIRST values for their team and others.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: They maximized scoring efficiency, iterated with purpose and achieved an impressive accuracy. This team showed an animal-like focus, steadily pursuing a one clear goal to dominate scoring on the field. They really clawed their way to the top, scaling simultaneously like bears in the forest.

This team has reached around the world to lend support to teams far and near. Mentoring rookie teams by sharing grant writing support, shop access, and education resources, they help grow engineers and spread FIRST values. Their students’ selflessness and positive attitudes are like tentacles, spreading Gracious Professionalism everywhere they go.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team traveled far to clear the path for their alliance. They “drifted” away from typical designs and got inspiration from cooler climates. This team proved their snowblower-bot can handle a “flurry” on the field with aloha spirit.

While others spun their wheels, this team had their flywheel locked in at 2.5 times the competition. They mapped the game, engineered for reliability, verified their models, and built a protected design that was simply out of this world. When quality is the standard, these are the TecDroids you are looking for!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The best control systems don’t react to the field - they read it! They prepared for the field with two turrets, custom path finder software and seven lanes. Houston, we have a clear winner.

This award winner has been in the forefront of streamed autonomous flow. Their use of clocked measurement on the move and april tag monitoring allowed them to fly autonomously around the rest. Forget being Up-A-Creek without a paddle - this crew has their bearings from the moment a match starts.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their message is woven into the fabric of their identity, sparking curiosity for future generations. Driving their robots to remote communities, they help children reach for the stars. This team harmonizes FIRST values to orchestrate the leaders of tomorrow.

This team has blazed a new trail for the FIRST pipeline in their state. Their school may sound prickly, but they bring people together and expand FIRST to disenfranchised and underrepresented students. Their off-season robotics event has rebuilt and strengthened FIRST in their home state.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team’s dedication to sharing STEM and mentoring blew us all away. Their impact crosses borders – Ecuador, India, Brazil are all at play. Books, kits, and training the trainer are their tools. And their programs promoting women in STEM are a jewel. Their passion and jot for outreach are hard to find.

This team crosses the finish line with their elegant design. They fire on both cylinders using design principles to develop a machine that is both integrated and sleek. This red and black pit crew drives their precision machine towards victory.

This team has a small town feel with a “big city” perspective on recruiting. They will literally go the extra mile to promote FIRST as ambassadors of outreach. From playing charades to picking fruit at the farmer’s market, the whole community salutes this ‘bot.

This small but mighty team forged an alliance with other teams for outreach before they ever built their first bot. Their enthusiasm for FIRST and excitement to compete are infectious and will surely spread among their subjects. As their dragon stands guard, this kingdom survived their trial by fire.

This young team has spread their wings far beyond the competition floor, reaching classrooms across borders to share the gift of knowledge. Their precision is sharp on the field; their shooting is so accurate that it rivals the best compass. When it comes to the future of FIRST, keep your eyes on these night hunters – their talons are just getting sharp.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In a place where STEM must fight for every inch, this team has learned to waste nothing – not a single part, not a single student. From reusing last year’s robot to mentoring the next generation of engineers, they build a legacy as carefully and they build their machines. Like the champions of old, they have forged something enduring from limited resources.

Ascending as a team on the “incline”, this team unites in problem solving and co-opertition. Their summer camps and science nights raise the STEM platform for our elementary school future engineers. Their team spirit elevates everyone to the summit.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team had a purrrfect solution for success, combining their approach with a favorite carnival ride. After viewing their bot, the judges went wild for their civic design. Their endgame was a MARVEL, hanging upside down like “Spidey”.

Some competitors build for themselves, but this team builds for everyone. They opened their doors and their field, giving other teams a place to grow and a helping paw. Whether guiding a team from the ground up or stepping in at a moment's notice when others were in need, they never hesitate. In the spirit of FIRST, this team proof that the biggest claws can also have the biggest heart.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Outside-the-box thinking led them to go to the edge of the limits. Their innovative approach to expand the frame, bumped hopper capacity and shot volume. This helped them charge up Pikes Peak in style.

The quality of their materials combined with the configuration of their pit rivals an “F1 Team”. This team was able to sting the competition with an innovative intake. Their design and fabrication “DENIM”-strated they are more than a fashion statement.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Their control system really carried the water and proved its “ok” to be flying blind. This team’s “bit” is so much more than a computer “byte”. Mastering the hat-trick of power management, state mechanisms, and blind coding, this team controlled the field.

This robot glides under the bar to score. It’s brain was built for ball physics and path planning as a winning strategy. Their design is not Jurassic, rather modern with a bite! This robot has a mind of its own.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s spirit, colors, and love for competition are integrated throughout their visual theme and robot. Their vision of inclusion is evident by the drawing on the back of their shirts. While their distinctive mascot does not breathe fire, it guards their pit with its large tail!

Whether mentoring multiple FLL teams or hosting summer camps, this team does it all.
