From a food drive that collected more than 70 pounds of food to multiple robot demos that reached over 30 thousand people, they set a strong example for others. Known for hosting both the FLL and the FRC state Championships, they are guarding a legacy that will endure for years to come.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: ENFORCING the core values of FIRST, this team’s commitment to INSPIRING the youth and community continues strong. Even Isaac Newton couldn’t stop them.

This teams design shook the judges to their core with their sleek robot. From their custom built shooter to their unique agitator this team is constantly iterating on their robot and continuously pushing their limits. You know their robot is the complete package because they didn’t forget the net.
This team treats robotics like it's real life. They emphasize STEAM over STEM. Their skills were inspired and developed thanks to Dr. Poly!

This year, excitement filled the air as this team achieved a major milestone—a working robot. Though they may be young, their passion and commitment are undeniable. They are not afraid to put in the work, and this is only the beginning of what promises to be an incredible journey in the years to come.
This team was quick to impress. It is amazing how high they have risen in just 2 years. You would know them by their zip code.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Their hats make this team easy to spot in a crowd. They have all 3 P’s of Sustainability covered. They create a buzz where they go, but NOT because they are bees.
This team is forever young, formed so that all can participate. Everyone is eager to talk about their team and they are proud of exposing their belly pan in every match.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s robot blew the judges away, with a clean, mean, and accurate machine. From their electrical wiring, to the maximization of hopper volume, the thoughtfulness they put in every aspect of their robot shows in their performance. They’re wired, not tired, and Biggie Cheese is the pinnacle of excellent engineering.
Everyone does anything on this team. They are not only mentors but mentees. Their squad inspires from here to Fiji.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This award recognizes a team that showed incredible ingenuity in perfecting their fuel flow. You'll have no reason to complain about this team's performance, with their smooth indexing and aggressive intake design. This team puts the grit in the gears and built on the backbone of steel.

This team exemplifies use of data in their design and build quality. They substantially improved their shooting accuracy with their auto-adjusting dual shooters and hoods. This team has Quality in their blood.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s robot provided consistent, reliable performance all weekend long. Their code combined autonomous functions with manual controls to allow the drive team to adjust on the fly. When knocked off target this robot automatically readjusts to get back to snowblowing fuel with ease.

This team’s robot knows where it is on the field at all times. Their auto aiming and integrated intake/hopper design allowed them to achieve their goal of maximizing their fuel scoring potential. This robot “shakes and bakes”.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s logo evolves each year to reflect the theme of the game. It brings the concept to life through its visual imagery. The cup and coin on their shirts symbolizes the team’s history and tradition, paying homage to the legacy of the game.

This team has deep roots that has allowed them to spread their impact throughout their state and beyond. Helping support rookie teams through a rookie workshop and providing assistance to teams in the pits, this team is a friendly face to FIRST teams that need support. They have a strong FIRST pipeline, mentoring and supporting multiple FIRST teams in their area. This team is the strong trunk of OpenAlliance, reaching over 200+ FRC and FTC teams. Their branches continue to grow, intertwining with their community. Partnering with the Society of Women Engineers Next club and creating "Robots on Fire", their focus on bringing STEM and FIRST to all was clear. We hope to see this tree continuing to grow.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team is united and resilient and they know robotics is more than just the competition. From STEM nights, to global presentations about FIRST, the team’s dedication to their outreach is clear. They have even donated over one thousand dollars of LEGOs to their local school team. This team shows the FIRST community that it is not the size of the herd that matters but the heart of the ram.

This team has an elegant and robust design from drive base to their wiring. With their 360 degree turret they can hit their target wherever they need. This robot was an impressive project from this team as they prowled through the field.

When it comes to this team’s good qualities the judges had no shortage of praise. With extensive outreach, clear team pride and plans for the future, they truly are examples of what FIRST is all about. Small but strong, this team is like a mini fridge, and the cold didn’t bother this squad anyways.

This team has recently blasted into the scene. They have managed to accomplish what more experienced teams do by converting passion into action. With enthusiasm abound and a vision for the future. We look forward to seeing them grow when they Return next year.

When it comes to prospects for the future, this team has it all planned out. Just as belts hold together essential parts of a robot, they bind together and are already on their way to expand STEAM in their community. We’re calling all the monsters to rise among the stars.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: How do you overcome losing longtime mentors and build for the future? This team decided a student-led team was the best way to ensure sustainability. From finding new sponsors to pre-season workshops and tool training to ensure knowledge transfer, this team has gone a long way to secure their team's future. Make sure to stop by and sign their belly pan.

Team spirit isn’t just about cheering, it is about bringing unique ideas together. From what’s in our heads to what we create with our hands. Like cards for the cause that we decorate. Thank you Roxanne for embodying this team’s spirit.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The judges would like to recognize a team with an outstanding engineering design and process. A team that began with defined functional requirements and followed through with intentional design decisions, collaboration, and verification. Their thorough documentation, consistent testing, and disciplined workflow were a true constitution for their success.

This team doesn’t treat Gracious Professionalism as a school project. They are willing to share parts, their space and their time. They exemplify coopertition in everything they do. Thank you to this team for helping make this event successful.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has approached the game’s challenge with creativity and practicality. Their robot exemplified versatility through its design of a unique shooting mechanism. This team is ready to unleash their talons and pivot towards their goal.

This award goes to a robot built with robustness in design. Their reliability and controlled failure points allowed them to score under any emotion. They brought in a furious storm raining fuel from above.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With their cameras at the ready this team really knows where its at. The control system knows where and when to paint the depot with fuel. With a dashboard display, robot lights and haptic feedback this robot shoots for the sky

This team excelled in software integration, maximizing their simples, COTS-based robot to achieve their number one priority: points. With a turret that constantly repositions according to the match state and extensive data collection to support shoot-on-the-move, this team successfully paired a mechanical body with a powerful brain.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's visual presence is an absolute standout. Draped in brilliant yellow and blue, their branding catches your eye. If the match is on the line and you're feeling a tug, just look to the field for their trusty robot, Doug!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.awardName: Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This squadron is on the move, growing from 9 to 350 members across all levels of FIRST. Their medics have aided nearly 90 teams across five competitions with spare parts and programming assistance. NEXT, they have hosted initiatives for young women to connect, learn, imagine, make, and become future STEM leaders. If you ever need assistance, the judges recommend you call these mercenaries.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: The only thing that looks better than this robot is how it performs. This certified dumper rained fuel into the hub. Its gold snake skin protects the wire harness complementing its black and gold shield

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: This team prides itself in making use of local materials. Their STEM outreach is BUILT on a foundation made of cardboard. Using a robot with self-made wheels, this team has a tighter grip on their future than an Octopus.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: A group of students realized their part of the county didn’t have a FIRST team, so they figured they were free to start one. In their first year, they’ve advocated to pass state funding legislation, worked on coding camps, and have partnered with a local CTE program. NASA might have helped to launch them, but this team is well on their way to All-Star status

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: This team is smart like a pet. This team serves a role model for local communities, helping people in need and rescuing animals. Curiosity didn’t kill the cat, it made it smarter.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When it comes to sustainability, this team isn’t telling tales. From laptop donation, to recreating soda bottles into robot mounts, to food drives, to a creative booster program, they are fabricating ways to protect people and the planet while prospering. They’re free to land atop the sustainability podium.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: This flock of students really knocked over the judges. Rarely butting heads, these students have formed lasting relationships in their pursuit of knowledge. One could say they’ve really RAMMED through all barriers.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team excels in iterative design processes with constant team collaborations. Their data and scouting is out of this world. They are swimming in engineering documentation and processes

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.script: This team wanted to share their workspace and remove barriers to STEAM learning. They shared their STEM Center with other FRC teams and created a website with programming resources. This team makes a difference. Their work has real impact and genuinely MATTERS

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.teamName: Galaxia in memory of David Zohar

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Curie Division presented by The Argosy Foundation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
