Their branding is exacting down to the thought level they celebrate their match victories with shield stickers, and their color scheme flows from their machine back to the controller. The judges probably could have found 1K of examples to nominate the Kil-A-bytes

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has truly made a difference in moving STEM initiatives forward in their community and beyond. From week zero warm-ups to advocacy, STEM kits and monthly workshops, there is no off-season for them. Their earnest commitment is: “FIRST is for everyone”

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their beautiful design and robust fabrication. From their self correcting auto to their carefully constructed electrical board – this blue machine ran circles around the field. This team drove the competition MAD with their performance.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This team paved the way for people across the globe, no matter how young or how old. Their food drives help to supply needed food for many years to come. From the plains of South Africa to the Jersey shore, they serve a never ending slice of Pi.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: Being a rooikie does not mean you don’t understand the values of FIRST. Reaching out to the extended community is part of their D.N.A. This Baltic state team is the first letter of the Greek Alphabet

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: In just one year, this team showed up to the event ready to play. With potential on the HORIZON, they brought a game of their own – built from scratch – to lead the way.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This Team’s efforts focused on the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals. Their use of horse shoe crabs grew their team and the ocean, encouraging everyone to “Do The Best”

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This team knows the importance of team unity and makes sure to share it with their community. You might have seen them around the pits clipping clothespins with words of encouragement This Canadian team encourages inclusion through their stem workshops for neurodivergent and visually impaired students. Please join me in congratulating team 7712, Team Umoja

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s design process demonstrated their commitment to deliver a beautiful machine. They flooded the field with their fuel and code, overwhelming the competition with their rip current.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This New Jersey team, models for all FIRST teams what GP is all about. From helping scores of teams at home, to helping lending a hand at competitions, they do their best to make sure “no one gets left behind” Congratulations, team 316, Lunatecs.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is diligent in mitigating risks with unique systems of checking. By redesigning the hardware in the loop, they can isolate and test on the fly. Look out as this team comes buzzing by.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a well documented and clearly executed plan, building a bold yellow robot backed by strong design, strong electrical and strong programming practices. They integrated an omega symbol to show this is not the ending, just simply the beginning.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team demonstrated exceptional innovation by extending the boundaries of how robotic systems are designed, tested and validated. By developing a model within an existing simulation, they showed a efficient approach to improving real-world performance. Sometimes the best way to win in the real world is to first win in a fake one.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.script: This east coast team spun around the field. Staying on target, they played all their cards right. Their three of a kind autonomous routine is all aces!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Daly Division presented by BAE Systems, Inc.
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s brand pierced through their progression of FLL, FTC and outreach. You can pick them out from the crowd with their Holy Hand Grenades Don’t forget to bring carrots for Dynamite!

This team digs through their past to find new ways to advocate, improve, and engage. They spark excitement for engineering around the globe. We are sure that the stands will explode with excitement for

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: These goggle wearing engineers are inspiring the next generation. From custom inventions to putting roofs over heads. These steam powered philanthropists are building up their community one cap at a time.
Industrial design is like charting through unknown territory. This robot followed a clear path through the design morass and emerged from the Swamp.
Fairy Godparent Award These fairy godparents know how to rock! From Jamaica to all the Boys and Girls they sprinkle their dust. Building a golden chain of teams...
This team is making waves and cleaning oceans. Coming in like a storm ready to shake up their community. They have recycled plastic and rebuilt to create a better future.

These student's can't reign in their enthusiasm for changing the culture in their country. They are hosting monthly STEM camps in impoverished schools and harnessing FIRST-time government funding for classroom technology. They may only be colts, but this team is already running wild.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has created a powerful engine for a bright future. Their enthusiasm and vitality only grew as they galloped from facility to facility. After 6 long years, this team is now super charged with a million dollar workshop.

records.teamName: The Gadgeteers of St. Johns County
records.script: This team made anyone who came to their pit feel like they fit in. They kept the gears of passion grinding within their team, with their sponsors and at the competition Their team spirit shines like gold.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: These students did a ‘super’ job clearly explaining a design process that combines physical components and sensor feedback to achieve their goals. A unique implementation of a LIDAR sensor ensures fuel reliably gets to their ‘halo’ turret. This ‘caped crusader’ makes a delicious recipe.
GP is embedded in this team's code. By sharing their booty both on and off the field, they’ve proven everyone belongs in STEM. The FIRST Core Values are the wind in their sails.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Most teams stop at a single system for every component, this robot is able to stoop down with redundant talons and an advanced targeting system to shoot its shot!
This team didn’t fall into any traps with their maintenance. Their robot organization and documentation was out of this world! The judges loved the paint job that matched their starbursts.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has shown their control over power. Their cameras give a clear view of the sandy terrain. The judges were electrified by their ability to record their varmint.

A gold standard when it comes to autonomous features. Charging forward with hundreds of points per match, their canon-like turret blasts them to victory. This overseas team, along with their golden AI, horn-leads the way for autonomy.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to imagery, they didn't take a chance. Their style isn't just luck. They went all in and hit the jackpot.

Redefining what it takes to make a lasting impact. Their students enthusiasm and dedicated work energize their community and build a powerful pipeline where learners become leaders! Every effort sparks curiosity and builds futures. This role model team turns classrooms, camps, and community events into launchpads for the next generation of innovators! All of that energy leads to one question… which way’s the beach!

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: All throughout their community, this team brings fashionable energy. Uniting languages and opportunities they clearly have synergy. These boys and girls are proof that any Mohawk can truly rock out.
This vibrant team has a sleek and visually appealing robot. It was no accident that their robot was practical on and off the field. They dominated with their design.

Closing the resource gap across an entire robotics community is tough. They united teams, educators, and industry professionals across borders. For strengthening their robotics community on a shocking scale, the award for industry collaboration goes to Team 7130 Future Shock.
Every great vision starts with a chance. Bring in your friends and see it advance. These stars have perfected their next battle plans.

Leading the way is not always about speed After receiving vital help their first year, they returned to pay it forward and supported another first year team. While many teams focus on the speed of their robot, this team has proven that setting the right PACE is their team focus.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In everything they do, this team has a plan, from inspiring their Superintendent, school clubs, and recycling their robot, they clearly have a plan. We are proud to grant permission to land.

You would never describe this team as an old nag. Their relentless enthusiasm resulted in fun challenges, new facilities, and supported teams in their area. With a culture that is truly unbridled, they have shown everyone that they have the horsepower to lead the charge.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their design process. Their bot works flawlessly as one mechanism. Their bold play on the field has us sold.
They poured encouragement, teamwork, and kindness over every challenge, making the whole event better for everyone around them. This team didn’t just bring the sauce, they were the gravy on top.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their approach to feeding their intake did not leave them"BEACHED". They did not horse around when it came to the creative approach of their bot. WHEN I SAY 54 THIS TEAMS SAYS .....
This team takes an "EDGY" approach to building a quality bot. Their Flashy colors make other teams blush. They turn every trap into a triumph.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This robot's control system demonstrates forethought in approach. They definitely caught the fire of innovation as they designed and built their robot. By integrating many sensors, drivers only need to get close to the goal to puff fuel into the hub.
Their robot's turret redefines a complete circle. Autonomous Mode features a ghost in the machine. They "fuse" programming and play into one.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The energy of this team generates enough steam to really turn people's heads. Their cohesive visual identity meshs with public figures, making the community tick. Their dedication to winding up the world shows that even the smallest gear makes a watch tell time.

This team has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to advancing STEM education and the mission of FIRST. With a diverse team representing global backgrounds, they have achieved remarkable local, community, and global impact through mentoring teams, running sustainable outreach programs that reach hundreds of students weekly, and launching initiatives that combine engineering skills with meaningful societal contributions. Their dedication to diversity, innovation, and community engagement truly stands out. Congratulations, Team 5557

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: In nature, some of the most powerful creatures move around quietly and deliberately — focused, yet radiating a brilliance that electrifies everything around them. This team embodies that same force, channeling their energy into a community impact so far-reaching and genuine that it has become the very definition of what the Engineering Inspiration Award was created to recognize. They championed STEM in a country who's public school system has yet to emphasize it - including training other schools during their weekends and going as far to spread RoboJam to other countries. It is with immense pride that we present this honor to Team 7403, the Lightning Blue Lizards!

This team sailed the ocean to South Florida bringing with them a robot design with a simple, clear and retractable spring solution, strong enough to deliver the consistent performance while guided by a singled eye sailor. For the simple and effective industrial design, the award goes… Team 8817

This team has opened their resources to the world and lit the spark of FIRST in places it had never reached before ensuring that the student who walks through their door today will one day come back to hold the door open for the next one. Today, we honor a team that does not just participate in the FIRST community they are the reason it grows. Please join me in congratulating Team 2383, the Ninjineers.

Crossing oceans and boundaries, this rookie team brought global collaboration and fresh energy to the competition, quickly becoming a standout presence both on and off the field. Through strong teamwork, rapid technical growth, and a commitment to the mission of FIRST Robotics Competition, they inspired others while building a solid foundation for future success. The Rookie All-Star Award goes to FRC Team 11138 TEKNOROB.

The Rising All-Star Award celebrates a team that has persevered through challenges despite the difficulties of being young. This team overcame a complete overhaul, expanded FIRST to new shores abroad, opened doors of access to students who never thought robotics was within their reach, and excelled in the face of extraordinary adversity. It has not been since 333 BC that an impact on Cyprus has been made this significant. Put your hands together and congratulate your 2026 South Florida Regional Rising All-Star Award winners, Team #8859, Bora Robotics!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Bringing juniors and sponsors with them, They can find their way out of any labyrinth No bull, just minotaurs Congratulations Team 1369
From the south to the north On the floor, the pit or the arena They dance to victory Congratulation, Team Merengue

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: They engineered unique approaches and fired every fuel with precision. This team has prowled the field with precision and power for over thirty years. These cats don’t just build robots, they engineer solutions - welding, wiring, coding. Congratulations Team 108 SigmaCats
This team fostered the spirit of FIRST through their kindness towards other teams, and respect fforging a positive environment at this year's event. Congratulations Team 9404

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team showed exceptional creativity in every part of their design. They weren’t afraid to get a little dirty turning challenges into clever solutions. Their innovative approach set them apart. Congratulations Team 3932

These builders rose out of the swamp with a machine as tough as gator hide and smooth as still water. They delivered precision, durability, and clean design at every level, executing each task with control and consistency. For unmatched craftsmanship and performance, the Quality Award goes to Children of the Swamp.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The judges saw that when a technology shifts from being just a tool to becoming an identity, something truly special happens. This family team united engineering knowing exactly where to look, aim, and strike. This robot was already scoring, spinning, tracking, and executing with such precision that the impossible seemed like second nature in every match. For the unique integration the award for innovation in control goes… Team 59 Jesus and Charisse

This team showed exceptional precision and consistency throughout the competition. Their programming and strategy set them apart from the rest of the field, showing they truly had their “ducks in a row.” Congratulations Team 180.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Precision cuts, crisp code, seamless teamwork every byte counted. The team that made us hungry every time we looked at them. Raise a slice to Pizza Byte

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Some machines — and some ships — are so powerful, their impact isn’t fully understood until you dig a little deeper. This team built the pipeline — mentoring 5 FLL and 3 FTC teams that feed directly into their roster, unearthing the next generation of innovators long before the rest of the world knows their names. When it comes to teams that boot up the future one student at a time, please welcome Team 6919, The Commodores.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Going boldly beyond, this team’s initiatives engage both young and old, sparking curiosity and creating lasting pathways into STEM for those who may have never imagined themselves in the field. Through inclusive programming, hands-on experiences, and a steadfast commitment to mentorship, they support the ever-moving military family, empower FLL coaches, and inspire programs like Build Brave Girls. This Award goes to Team #4188, Columbus Space Program

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Whether they’re hunting in golden plains or in the state of Georgia, this machine was King in distinguishing itself with pride. This team made sure their jungle cat bot could stalk prey with an elegant and sleek design. Roar loudly for the winner of the Industrial Design Award, Team 1261 the Robo Lions

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Well, you can tell by the way that they walk, that this team is Stayin' Alive. Fielding a full team of rookies, they have been relentless in pursuit of competition performance. Strutting through a challenging season, this team has built on a continued legacy to pass down as they rise again. The Judges are thrilled to present our Stayin' Alive Award to Team 3901, the 100 Scholars.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Loss of your maker space… No power in your new facilities… Loss of more than half of the members of an already small team.. NO PROBLEM! This team managed to “spin” into action! When a series of setbacks for this rebuilding team could have led them to become as extinct as the “dinosaurs,” this team instead got to work rebuilding their shop, expanding their team, retraining new members to know something about - everything - assuring the continuity of their program and their team. This team discovered the strength of community by building an alliance of schools that have come together to build one remarkable robot. Please congratulate Team 8736, The Mechanisms of Marietta and their robot - Spin-a-Saugus!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When it comes to sustaining people, prosperity and the planet, this team really sank its claws into all three challenges by training and cross-training members, actively and proactively seeking sponsorships, and reusing every single part possible when building and rebuilding their robots. You could say, that when this team faces a challenge, they swoop in “talons first,” ensuring the continuity of both team and planet through a relentless focus on preserving resources, growing their sponsorship base, and mentoring future generations of robotics professionals. You might even say they’ve been tough as “steel” when it comes to their program’s impacts, both within their school and on planet earth. Please congratulate Team 6910, the Steel Talons of Mill Creek high school!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: More than meets the eye, this team showed up for battle to face any mega-challenges of the day. Optimizing their community through outreach and mentorship of local elementary students, they fought off any Decepticons and showed great representation of the First Robotics principles. Hitting the field with Optimus Trek, the Team Spirit Award is awarded to Team 4240, the TroTek Warriors.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Engineering Work Process is a continual loop of failure and progress to innovate design and performance. This team unearthed this mindset and created a business-worthy plan documenting research, strategy, planning, design, testing, and building of their robot and components. Uncovering the innovative design elements through this robust process, they found the Pachyderm that they were looking for. The Excellence in Engineering Award therefore goes to Team 8866 - Innovation Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: This team is bound by a code of honor, kindness, and an unshakable sense of community. They consistently demonstrate that success is measured not just by wins, but by how you treat others. And while their robot Zips around the field, it is clear that they are held together by far more than zip ties, they are bound by true brotherhood.. This award goes to Team #7104, The Bot Brothers

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Behold the Spin-dexer—where chaos meets precision, turning scattered game pieces into perfectly timed performance. With a spin, a sort, and a spark of ingenuity, this bot transforms motion into strategy like never before. This isn’t just a mechanism—it’s creativity in motion.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: This team demonstrates true quality through its unwavering attention to detail in everything it does. Clad in purple and every gear in sync, this team reflects strength, reliability, and a commitment to doing the essentials exceptionally well. Though the team is new, their foundation is strong. Like a well-known bridge every connection is built to last. This Award goes to Team #11214, cyBEARCATS

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: From a plywood start to a plasma cut finish, This team built a unique machine. Their step-by-step process produced a truly “one-of-a-kind” result. There’s nothing underhanded about this sure shooter. The innovation in control award goes to team 9477 Lamda from Suwanee G

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Before the countdown fades, this machine is already in motion. With clear vision through its frames, a front intake that pulls in game pieces without pause, and movement that thrives in controlled chaos, it turns disorder into precision - reading the field, reacting instantly, and executing like it’s already written the outcome. Flowing through every path and powering each move with intent, this team doesn’t wait for the match to begin - they’re running the circuit. The Autonomous Award goes to Team 1002 CircuitRunner Robotics

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: There’s nothing pokey about this team or their bot. We kept our googly eyes on this gang throughout the competition That’s why we are in Clyde to Present the Imagery award to team 3635 The flying legion

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: From their build space here in the Peach State, this team is building more than robots —they are building a movement grounded in access and inclusion. Bringing their entire community along for the journey through innovative and unique solutions, they are building a sustainable and supported STEM community. From students to adults and individuals of all backgrounds to building buddies and brave girls, this team is truly taking their entire community on a long trip after launch while providing a help desk to support them along the way.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This metro Atlanta team is building pathways to opportunity for future generations of innovators and creators. They are making a powerful and lasting impact through hands-on outreach, meaningful mentorship, and programs that bring STEM education to students across their footprint. By leveraging their available resources, their alumni network and all their super powers, this team is forging ahead to spread FIRST and inspire their community in a heroic way.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team inspires more than innovation; they expand access and opportunity in STEM. Through outreach and tutoring, they help young minds rise and believe. They created an intelligent Vantage point, fusing data and strategy to win… Engineering inspiration rises with Team 6925, W.A. Robotics

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Some teams build robots. This team, however, builds an entire ecosystem. They are the architects not just of a machine, but of opportunity, constructing pathways to STEM where none existed before. They are "Bridging the Gap" to launch new teams in rural areas, ensuring the future of FIRST is bright for everyone. Their blueprint for inspiration is undeniable, as they host over 20 teams at their own facility and provide direct technical support to 30 more at FIRST competitions. For proving that they are truly an Oasis of engineering inspiration in the FIRST community, the Engineering Inspiration Award is presented to Team 2974, Walton Robotics!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: We need to talk about the robot in the room. You know the one. The one that had people pulling out their phones in the pit just to take a picture. Somebody on this team clearly lost sleep over every panel, every edge, every detail that didn't score a single point but made every other team in the building jealous. Congratulations to Team 6829, Ignite Robotics, on winning the Industrial Design Award!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team blends a high-performance robot with a broad outreach program. They SPRINT towards opportunities to spread the word about FIRST and STEM. They RUN domestic events at elementary, middle schools, museums, and various online venues. They RACE to host FLL and FTC competitions. Then they DASH across multiple time zones and language barriers to COMPLETE THE CIRCUIT with international partnerships in Libya, Vietnam, and South Africa. Congratulations to Team 1002 Circuit Runners

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team turned their first season into an inspiration both on and off the field. They left pawprints of innovation and teamwork everywhere they went. Competing and helping others with the strength of a bear and the speed of a cat the Rookie All-Star award goes to Team 11214 The cyBEARCATS!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: The growth of the team within the last few years has been remarkable. The challenges of not only gaining new members but to pay it forward to all of those who have yet to come. You might see yourself very soon on this team’s social media holding a bit of fuel. The winner of the Rising Allstars Award is Team 5608 Lassiter Robotics

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team in blue builds a legacy, growing strong and true. With strong sponsor support and a plan built to last, they grow their future strong and true… Through open labs, they train their own, helping new members grow too. Back-to-back sustainability shines again for Team 4112, EagleBots

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team doesn't just display spirit; they embody it in every action they take. These warriors define teamwork not as a strategy for competition, but as a deep commitment to others. They fight with pride on the field and in the stands never yielding. The Team Spirit Award is proudly presented to Team 5109, Gladiator Robotics!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: For this team - simple, reliable design is the goal. The wiring of their “brain pan” is impeccable, their CAD is meticulous, and they use Discord to prevent discord & keep everyone informed. These Outstanding Students REALLY HAVE Created an Awesome Robot! Oi! Oi! Oi! Congratulations to Team 832 O.S.C.A.R.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team stands out for their willingness to help others, share knowledge, and strengthen the FIRST community without hesitation. Though considered a BASIC part of FIRST, this team takes gracious professionalism very seriously. If you look for the beige box at the end of the rainbow and you will find the Gracious Professionalism Award winners Team 6919, The Commodores!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: What just happened out there? This team already knows. . . Their purpose-built app captures, replays, and analyzes match data in immersive 3D. For this team, the final buzzer is just the beginning. Data is sharp . . Vision is clear . . . and their Future is HOT!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: Raise your hand if your robot broke this weekend. Now keep it up if it fixed itself. Yeah, that's what we thought. This team's intake took shots all tournament that would have sent most teams scrambling for zip ties and a prayer. Instead, it just folded up, popped back out, and said 'we good.' You can't break what's designed to bend. Congratulations to Team 1648, G3 Robotics, on winning the Quality Award!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: You ever watch a robot and think, there's no way a human is driving that? That's what it felt like watching this team. The movements were too clean, too precise, too locked in. And when you're hauling around ninety fuel at a time, control isn't optional, it's everything. Here's the kicker: they're only in year two. In math, their name means a constant, and that's exactly what their robot was. Congratulations to Team 9477, Lambda, on winning the Innovation in Control Award!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team doesn't believe in breakthroughs. They believe in one percent. Tweak one thing after every match. Stack enough of those tiny gains together and pretty soon your robot is doing things in auto that other teams are still trying to figure out with a driver behind the wheel. While everyone else is celebrating what just worked, this team is already asking 'what's next?' Congratulations to Team 1833, BEAN, on winning the Autonomous Award!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their imagery is not only consistent—it is intentional. It reflects their values, their journey, and the impact they strive to make both inside and outside of robotics. No matter how you are feeling this team and robot is sure to move you and make you care a little more. It is with great pride that we recognize this year’s Imagery Award winner: Team 9480, the Gear Bears.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: Not just focused on the robot, this team is focused on people. They use a green thumb to sprout FIRST teams like kudzu. Then they launch those people and teams into orbit with comprehensive support programs. They "build brave girls". They mentor younger students with "robo-buddies". They engage the elderly with "Silver Circuits"... And when teams need help, they cover the "Help Desk". Congratulations to team 4188..

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Some teams quietly build robots, while others leave a lasting impact far beyond the competition floor. This team soared beyond expectations, lifting their school and community to new heights of respect for STEM. This award goes to W.A. Robotics, whose outreach and leadership advanced appreciation for engineering everywhere they reached. Congratulations to team 6925!

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: This machine commands attention the moment it moves. With clean lines, intentional design, and mechanisms that flow with precision, this team delivers a robot where performance and style move as one. Sparking opportunity and bringing together students from every path, this team doesn’t just build robots - the “Ignite” them.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: Momentum Award The Team rebuilt from the ground up with student leadership driving every step. They turned setbacks into momentum and proved that grit can generate lift. And when resilience meets a little turbulence, you get a team that knows how to take flight. Congratulations to team 5828 the Flying Riots.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: Some teams start out with more questions than answers, but they keep showing up anyway. This team kept their paws on the problem while turning every setback into power and stayed glowing under pressure. This award goes to the Plutonium Panthers, whose persistence through the challenges of being a young team is nothing short of inspiring. Congratulations to team 10376!

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The speed of this team is almost automatic. They hunted from their burrows in this weekend’s competition. This Cobra killing mob has shown they are at the top of the heap when it comes to increasing and maintaining their pack to bring continued success.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: Some teams cheer and some teams make sure everyone hears. From loud chants to a sign waving high, this crew brought nonstop energy to the stands and a little personality straight out of a certain famous grouch. With spirit you could see and definitely hear, the Team Spirit Award goes to Team 832, O.S.C.A.R.!

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s design flows with purpose where every component works together to create a truly seamless system. Their design moves with grace and precision as it glides across the field. Though under the sea, this gentle giant has climbed to new heights. Congratulations to team 6772 the Marist Manta Rays.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: This team’s sportsmanship and cooperation spread like fire across the event just like their work off season in their community. All weekend long, teams couldn’t stop talking about how this red‑and‑ready crew leapt in to help with anything, pouncing on every problem no matter how Dull‑ton it seemed. Congratulations team 6887 Dalton Catabots!

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Innovation often starts with a simple question: what if we built it smarter the second time. This team turned last year’s lessons into a modular machine with a turret, upside-down electronics, and the ability to shoot on the move with the push of a button. With a design as hot as their name, the Creativity Award goes to Team 1414, IHOT Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: From bolt to code every detail reflects a level of structure and reliability that would pass the toughest inspection. This robot doesn’t just run, it reports for duty executing every task with precision and discipline. With a machine belt like a well drilled unit, we’re pretty sure this team could pass a surprise inspection at 0600. Congratulations to team 7104 The Bot Brothers.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team ran their robot like a well-oiled operation, delivering a machine so smooth on the field that every rapid-fire shot and fuel cycle looked effortless. Their innovative control system blended precision, accuracy, and reliability, allowing them to hold more fuel, score with consistency, and navigate the field with the confidence of a team that truly has everything under control. With unmatched awareness and integration beyond autonomous play, they proved their vision from every angle with four-sight. Congratulations to team 2974 - Walton Robotics

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.script: This “self proclaimed” robotics team operates fully autonomously, making precise decisions without human intervention. They hail from NE Atlanta and have demonstrated exceptional, reliability, adaptability, and efficiency in these complex competition scenarios. This impressive team that ends in 26 had a performance that’s at a new standard for intelligence, self-directed robotic systems.

records.eventName: PCH District Columbus Event presented by Muscogee County School District (CTAE) and Columbus Development Authority
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some teams build robots, but a few create a presence you can’t ignore. Powered entirely by peach power, this squad proved that when you work together, the results are anything but ordinary. Yoshi set the standard for visual excellence and imagination. Congratulations to team 9057!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: This team is a well‑oiled machine, tirelessly championing the values FIRST across their community and beyond. They heroically mentor over a hundred teams, host dozens of events, and volunteer thousands of hours … building a pipeline to the future they show that STEM is everyone. Tony Stark isn’t on this team, but he would be proud! The winners are … The Avengers!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: The Engineering Inspiration Award celebrates outstanding success in advancing respect and appreciation for engineering within a team’s school and community. Through outreach, mentorship, and meaningful engagement with students and their community, they have worked tirelessly to share the excitement of STEM and the impact engineering can have on the world. Their efforts demonstrate a deep commitment to spreading the message of FIRST and creating opportunities for others to explore engineering. This team has gone above and beyond to inspire the next generation of future tech tinkers. The judges are proud to present the Engineering Inspiration Award to Team 2974… Walton Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: This team showed their creative spark by exploring three distinct bot designs to combine into one. Their robot machine features a heavy metal frame that demonstrates why hexagons are the bestagons. This fiery, well-oiled machine sets the competition ablaze, let’s give it up for Team 6829, Ignite Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: The Judges’ Award proudly recognizes this team for their elegant, creative engineering solutions—proving that simple ideas can overcome even the toughest challenges. They embody the spirit of FIRST through meaningful STEM outreach, by inspiring curiosity and opportunity throughout their community. Like their eagle mascot, they spread their wings to mentor younger FIRST LEGO League students, helping the next generation soar to new heights. The Judges Award goes to Team #4112 EagleBots.

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Though this is their very first FRC event, this young team has experienced mentors and have led their local Lego Team to the State Championship. The Cybearcats truly represent the symbolic Bridge, connecting skilled participation from throughout their School and entire extended community. They especially appreciate the support from The Commodores and many other teams embracing FIRST Robotics Gracious Professionalism. Congratulations to the CYBEARCATS team 11214.

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Some robotics teams start the season with experienced members, polished robots, and everything going exactly according to plan. Other teams start with a nearly brand-new roster, a rookie coach, and a robot that might contain a little more wood, duct tape, and determination than anyone expected. But when that team keeps coming back with the persistence of a robot with nine lives, rebuilding their program and tripling their membership, you get Team 6887, the Catabots of Dalton High School — a team that truly embodies the spirit of the Rising All-Star Award in the FIRST Robotics Competition.

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team may be young, but they are up to the challenge. And they are building a talent pipeline that is creating a long-term, sustainable pathway to dominance. They are reusing resources to build the best robot they can, allowing them to swim with OR against the current, if necessary. The Team Sustainability Award goes to the Marist Manta Rays. Congratulations

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: When it comes to Enthusiasm and Spirit this team isn’t just Horsing around Their community outreach is whimsical yet tracked with Precise Business Metrics Today’s team members and alumni are committed to be Trojans for Life. Congratulations team 5608 Lassiter Robotics .

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team stood out by demonstrating their professional approach to the engineering design process. Their design transition from concept to execution mirrors their mission of turning potential energy into kinetic results on the field. This green and black machine can run ci9rcles around the competition. Team 1002 The Circuit Runners.

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: The Gracious Professionalism Award celebrates outstanding demonstration of the FIRST core values—sportsmanship, teamwork, and helping others succeed both on and off the field. Like little Care Bears-This teams positive attitude and willingness to support others proves that when teams work together, everyone moves forward. You could say they helped keep the whole competition turning like a well-oiled gear. The judges are proud to present the Gracious Professionalism Award to Team 9480… the Gear Bears!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The Creativity Award celebrates a robot design that brings an innovative and imaginative solution to the strategy of the game. This team impressed the judges with a feature that was clearly intentional in its design and execution, demonstrating clever engineering and originality. Their creative approach enhances their gameplay strategy and shows how thinking differently can lead to powerful results. If you want to understand their design, you might just need to get on their wavelength. The judges are proud to present the Creativity Award to Team 9477… Lambda Robotics! 🤖🎉

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: The Quality Award celebrates machine robustness in both concept and fabrication. This team impressed the judges with a robot built for consistency and durability. Their innovative design features strong structural elements that show careful planning and craftsmanship. Their innovation shows thoughtful engineering, resulting in a machine that performs under the toughest competition conditions. The judges are proud to present the Quality Award to Team 8866… Innovation Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Speed and precision set this robot ahead of the competition. Their spindexter keeps the fuel spinning smoothly into the turret these mechanics turns great code into great scoring. Congratulations to the Mechanisms - Team 8736

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: This team let their code take full control to rack up high scores. Their programming logic proved as robust as classic 8-bit processors. This legacy computer needs no manual input to command the field, Team 6919, The Commodores!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The Imagery Award celebrates attractiveness in engineering and outstanding visual aesthetic integration of machine and team appearance. Their robot and team presentation feature a striking purple theme, reflecting pride in who they are and the mission they represent. Started by girls and continuing as an all-girl team, they are helping build a powerful girls-in-STEM pipeline, inspiring the next generation of innovators and engineers. Their visual presence is more than just style—it’s a statement about inclusion, opportunity, and the future of engineering. The judges are proud to present the Imagery Award to Team 7514… EVE Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: Impact and sustainability are more than just finances and recycling; they incorporate knowledge, people, and future thinking. Many times, a team will pick an identity that is important to the team. This team picked a hard model to follow: a generation of gods that preceded the Olympians!

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This award goes to a team that has made inclusivity more than a motto — it's the operating principle behind everything they do, from how they recruit to how they resolve conflict. They invest in their people at every level, even challenging their underclassmen to manage all the design changes since the last qualifier. Their reach extends well beyond their school, having hosted FLL tournaments and attended community festivals alongside their mayor and city council. These BULLS are the rare program that is just as intentional about building people as they are about building robots, and that's what makes them exceptional.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: This team didn't just build a robot, they designed a precision instrument. The wide shooter profile and sculpted hood aren't just functional — they are pure scoring artistry. No “bugs” in this elegant design, and it looks as good as it performs. Smooth, deliberate, effective — this team is ready and fully CHARGED!

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: This award goes to a team whose passion for FIRST is matched only by their determination to figure things out - no matter how hard. What started in 2022 with a couple of members has grown twenty-fold. Along the way they've had to learn something many teams take for granted — that "designing" a DROID and "building" one require two very different skill sets, and they've been closing that gap one part at a time. They hustle, they reuse, they adapt, and they show up every day committed to blending the technical with the tactile. When team members say that “FIRST changed our life”, you believe it — and that's exactly what this competition is all about.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: Against every rookie barrier, this team (like their mascot) stands tall and proud. Fueled by relentless curiosity, teamwork, and a passion for FIRST Robotics, they turned late-night learning and bold innovation into real results. With 70% of the team made up of freshmen, the seniors refused to let a single “byte” be taken out of their momentum: they stepped up as mentors, teaching skills, sharing confidence, and ensuring the program’s future. Their robot, Doc, is a proud testament to what mentorship, dedication, and enthusiasm can build.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: Some teams start small—but build something much larger than themselves. This team has quadrupled in size, becoming a cornerstone of STEM in their community while expanding opportunities for girls. As the only team in their area, they are not just building robots—they are building a future. With black and gold pride and a cat’s determination to climb higher, this team continues to rise.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team doesn't just build robots — they build a culture that lasts. Their focus isn't only on winning matches, but on leaving a lasting impact in their community. Fifteen years in the Peachtree District and still going strong, this diverse crew has the fire to keep going — season after season, never burning out.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: Being one of the oldest teams here – with a low team number to prove it, this team showed even “old” teams can bring new energy! They built their robot in 3 weeks and recruited a rookie to build their business plan. They've actively mentored middle school students in their community, hosted spirit nights, and even inspired two of their own graduates to return to mentor them. It may be their 20th anniversary, but this team shows that team spirit never gets old!

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Some teams build machines —but this team builds systems that continue to improve. Their detailed documentation of their robot design and build process reflected a disciplined engineering approach, supported by a clear cycle of reflection and improvement that guided their decisions throughout the season. By embracing a “Reflect and Improve” mindset, they demonstrated true ownership of their engineering process. Like a dragon that grows stronger with every challenge, this team continues to refine and elevate their design.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: This award goes to a team that understands something most engineers only learn on the job — that the best solutions are often the ones built under the tightest constraints. With a dozen active members and a few hundred dollars to build the bot, they revised it multiple times, RAIDED recycled parts, and relied on pure ingenuity to stay competitive in a crowded field where sponsors gravitate toward more established programs. This team has proven that resourcefulness is its own form of excellence, and that doing more with less while exhibiting grace under pressure is a skill worth celebrating.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Order up! This team has been cooking since 2004, serving creative strategies so original, the judges had to ask for the recipe. Coming all the way from an international kitchen in Buckhead, their gameplay approach was intentionally designed, never discovered.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: This next award goes to a team whose robot is so well built that we’re not sure it even needs bumpers. Already no strangers to the big stage, this team floated into Gainesville with a machine that proved when you build it right the first time, you don’t have to REBUILD it.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When the data is flowing and the system is connected, great control becomes possible—and this team took full advantage of that. Their control system used motor RPM and torque monitoring to detect intake jams and automatically eject game pieces without operator input, demonstrating a thoughtful and responsive approach to automation. This seamless integration of sensing and control improved reliability and reduced driver workload. With signals flowing and a wildcat’s instinct, this team stays connected and in control every match.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.script: They planted something new just last season, and it’s already grown into a giant. Undefeated this year, there are no signs of slowing down. Their robot didn’t need any help from the drivers to know exactly where to score, proving that when you put down the right roots, autonomous magic follows.

records.eventName: PCH District Gainesville Event presented by Honeywell
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team brings talent from throughout their school. Realizing that the difference between STEM and STEAM is adding the element of Art to the process. From the floor of their pit to the color of their bot, the consistent theme exhibits purposeful design. Throughout the event wherever you see purple and black you know this team in on a crusade.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: "This team believes STEM should be open to everyone. And they’ve found a way to make that happen. Each summer, they run engineering and computer science camps where students learn CAD, coding, and hands-on design. Through these camps they both inspire the next generation of engineers and fund the future of their own team - eliminating all team dues and travel fees so that every student can participate. But their impact doesn’t stop there. They mentor younger students through FIRST LEGO League, helping strengthen their STEM pipeline using bootcamps and tournaments. Their outreach keeps expanding, bringing robotics to more students across their community especially girls, through holistic and creative events. And if you listen closely… you might hear something coming. A rumble. A stampede. Because when this team gets moving, they charge. The FIRST Impact Award goes to… Team 4509 — the Mechanical Bulls!"

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has “stalked” their way to the top. With a confident display of fundamental engineering principles and a commitment to FIRST values, They’ve “sprouted” through this competition— 1833 Bean

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This prestigious Industrial Award recognizes a team whose robot demonstrates elegant design, efficient performance, and practical functionality. The wiring and component layout are exceptionally well planned and thoughtfully optimized. A creation worthy of legend – crafted with a spark from the God of Fire! Congratulations to the one and only Techno Titans!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This team has “captured” the Judges attention. Through their “burning” passion and cohesive professionalism, they’ve “scaled” their way through the “horde”— 3318 Robo Dragons

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: "Change can be challenging, but this team turned it into opportunity. After major turnover in student leadership, these students stepped up, supported each other, and kept their program moving forward. New leaders rose, new ideas took shape, and their commitment to learning and outreach never slowed down. These Scholars proved that resilience, teamwork, and determination can power any team through change. Please join me in celebrating the Rising All-Star Award winners… Team 3091: 100 Scholars!"

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: We are proud to recognize this team for building a program that thrives year after year—empowering new members, cultivating community partnerships, and inspiring the next generation of innovators through lasting impact. Their thoughtful outreach, knowledge transfer, and commitment to growth ensure that their team and the spirit of STEM will continue to flourish well into the future. Like their robot Syracusia (seer-uh-KOO-zee-uh), engineered to carry big ambitions and steady momentum, this team demonstrates that strong foundations can support incredible journeys. Congratulation to Team 9522 Archimedes.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: "Their infectious enthusiasm turns every challenge into a celebration of teamwork and innovation! Their pit, and their cheering section pulse with unstoppable energy, proving that spirit isn’t just something they show—it’s something they live. From the moment they arrive to the final match, they shine as a unified force of inspiration, reminding everyone that in FIRST, spirit and teamwork drive the ultimate victory! Dacula Droids and their bot Helios have team spirit that shines bright as the First Morning Sun!"

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: "In the wild, a pride is known for strength, coordination, and a leader who knows exactly how to control the hunt. You can see that same big-cat precision in this robot—from a camera-driven autonomous system stalking its targets, to a clever spring-loaded wiring solution that keeps the turret clean and untangled, and a robust spindle design built to launch fuel elements with accuracy. That kind of engineering excellence doesn’t happen by accident — it comes from experience, teamwork, and a team that has been leading the pride for years. Please congratulate the Robo Lions of Peachtree Ridge High School — winners of the Excellence in Engineering Award."

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: "Whether they are serving up STEM activities with a side of fries or providing hydration to local marathon runners, this team is always ""plugged in"" to their coastal community. From cleaning up Georgia beaches to volunteering at Georgia Tech, their outreach efforts span from the local shoreline to the heart of the engineering world. They have truly wired the circuit between service and Gracious Professionalism. Congratulations to Team 4701, Team W.I.R.E., from Savannah, Georgia!"

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: "Every great engineering story starts somewhere, and for this team it began with a growing group of students, a simple idea, and a robot built with the kind of durability you might expect from a very big, very loyal dog. And fittingly, their engineering approach feels a little like something from a small northern European country known for clean design and practical thinking — simple, smart, and built to last. For turning a creatively simple idea into a strong rookie season, please congratulate Team 11174 — the Great Danes from Denmark High School — winners of the Creativity Award."

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: From meticulous construction to elegant integration of mechanical, electrical, and software systems, this team demonstrates a commitment to craftsmanship and reliability at every level. Their attention to detail and pride in workmanship set a high standard for excellence on and off the field and in their pit. These water based mammals have formed a hard working teamwork focuses on helping others succeed. 6340 - Marist Manatees

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Is that a hurricane in the intake or a typhoon at the hopper? No, it's a tornado in Midtown! This team uses cyclonic fingers to feed fuel at EF5 speeds into their turret! Congratulations to...

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: While several teams had good autonomous performance, one stood out from the crowd. Through a flurry of fuel, this blitzing bot scored point after point during the autonomous period. Congratulations to Team 1771 for winning the Autonomous Award!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: All right, everyone we have a team here that clearly understands one very important rule of branding. If you’re going to stand out do it in style! Through the vibrant, branding, powerful message and commitment to bringing more girls into robotics they embody the imagery award to celebrate the team identity that energizes the entire community. When creativity and confidence power a team, robotics looks absolutely fabulous in pink! Please join me in congratulating this year’s imagery award winner team 9057 G.I.R.L!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.awardName: Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team’s countless efforts to advance STEM float them above the rest. The breadth of their outreach spans the country, bridging the gaps between the underserved, overlooked and marginalized, earning the respect of not only their peers, but even national leadership. And, of Judges, of course.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: Demonstrating simplicity with an elegant and efficient design, this team showcases thoughtful engineering where visual appeal and performance optimization come together. They really understand the “Link” between form and function.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: Fully embodying the essence of FIRST, this team took multiple steps to help others. Merging their ideas with other teams, they traveled far and wide as a united force. This team has no problem stepping up to the plate.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: This team has succeeded in creating a culture of connection. Full of purple, they exude the core value of FUN, bringing time, grit and work together. They made the judges’ choice easy.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: This team has come a long way in a short time, despite the mountains in their way. Through an ENORMOUS number of cold calls, they acquired sponsors that brought them to Houston. Like PENGUINS, this team shows that through perseverance anyone can thrive!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team really puts in the leg-work to maintain a fresh, new culture on their team. With a wing span as wide as the Amazon, they make room for everyone on their team, training and retaining knowledge and resources as they go. Don’t forget to check the temp before serving.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: Despite their clawed mascot, this team is warm and welcoming, and willing to offer a LITTLE SPARKLE to everyone. They CERTAINLY passed the VIBE CHECK!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team tuned their intake, conveyor, and shooter to work together flawlessly and pump fuel through at an impressive rate. They applied human factors to the design of their drive station to accommodate a highly focused drive team. With their efficient robot and human engineering, they are burning up the field!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: This team didn’t just compete; they galloped ahead, in lifting others up. When underrepresented groups faced barriers in STEM, this team successfully collaborated with others to rise to the challenge. In a competition full of legends, this team proved that true positivity and kindness is no myth.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creative solutions can go in multiple ways, and we all know that one fuel at a time just isn’t enough. This team reimagined scoring with a system built for volume, precision and redundancy. They kept the action flowing in more than one direction, with built two independent side by side turrets.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Mouser Electronics
records.script: Before this team creates anything, they run the design through its paces. They evaluate every potential failure with a tedious precision. It helps them avoid any preventable failure as if they were on the power play
