By exploring both the past and present, these tinkerers have enhanced their acquisition of knowledge and developed their leadership skills for the benefit of all. With accessible stem camps and a growing student base this team is building an empire to last.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This Indiana team is building their pipeline to the future. They are embracing, empowering, and educating not just their team, but their community as well. There is no need to guess about how precise this team is...
These KIDS rose to the challenge. They had a unique design approach to deploying their intake. They're the GOAT of Pneumatics!

This team has "traveled" far and never forgot the FIRST CORE values that make them great. They have been chosen for what the judges are calling the FIRST CORE values award because of their success, humility, and countless stories of lending a helping hand. They definitely take everything "by the horns".

At the crux of this team's journey, they sunk their CLAWS in to succeed despite challenges. They are dedicated to teaching the next generation. We anticipate them conquering their SUMMIT in the years to come.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: A strong program is not just built for one season, it is rebuilt and strengthened year after year. A single page (or two) maps their mission. A binder hits all Ps…People, Prosperity, and Planet. With a flash of color, seniors graduate and their team keeps running. They live the meaning of sustainability while expanding STEM opportunities with true PRECISION!

This team demonstrated consistent enthusiasm that inspired those around them, and truly embodied the heart and soul of FIRST. Their cheers are the loudest, their support to the community is evident, and this team reminds us that Robotics is as much about people as it is about their machines.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team took their shape to new heights, spinning new solutions to old problems.

This team embodied the spirit of Gracious Professionalism through constant sportsmanship and genuine commitment to lifting others up, their team colors often signaling help had arrived. Judges repeatedly noticed how they moved through the pits like a well-coordinated pack, offering tools, time, and expertise to help fellow teams. Their unwavering teamwork, generous mentorship, and a spirit that proves no team succeeds alone are inspiring.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This purple team created an out-of-the-box solution for their robot. They have a unique way of feeding, eating up twice as much as the competition. They love taking huge bites out of the competition...

This team's robot blends resourcefulness with high quality engineering. Built with precision and creativity, it features a unique pivoting bottom and repurposed components from the past. This thoughtful craftsmanship represents the ingenuity of this team.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This medieval team takes control using their unconventional powers. They will replace any old pie with a custom baked solution.

The best autonomous routines combine careful planning with technology that always knows exactly where it is. With precise algorithms, reliable odometry, and smooth automated driving, this robot delivers a truly super duper performance.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's imagery used student thinking to bring the robot to life. With a strong emphasis on the original Coach, their creative theme remains strong; supporting their mission to spread their wings and the CORE values of FIRST.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This team can't be boxed in. Paddling through challenges to spread their love for STEM. The future is bright with this pack!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has unleashed their full potential to inspire their community. They give students a passport to the world of STEM. This team is the top dog on the track when it comes to engaging the next generation.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This team came into the competition hot. Iterations forged this machine with purpose. Now their robot blazes through the field.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This central Indiana team is a jack of all trades. Their supportive nature and ambition goals fur-real impressed the judges. These pawsome young pups will someday be top dog.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This second year team is pushing themselves to the top of the list. They developed a team culture we usually see in veteran teams, when they redesign their robot between events. They are the prototype, for all FRC teams.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team shows their claws to make sure their team is sustainable on all fronts. After recent team changes, diverse funding sources and enhanced documentation show their commitment to FIRST. With recycled PET, this team is building their legacy.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: From the stands to the field, their energy is relentless and impossible to ignore. This team doesn't just bring spirit - they launch it, rallying the crowds, lifting up their peers, and making every match louder and more fun for everyone.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team hails from a historically significant city. They machined a majority of their components in-house even down to their wheels. Their honeycomb design had the judges buzzing about this team's engineering skills.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This team may be early in their journey, but they already developed a clear understanding of what it means to be part of something bigger than themselves. They understand that Gracious Professionalism isn't about having all the answers - it's about making sure everyone has access to them.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team broke down challenges into manageable pieces. They innovated a novel intake system that was key to their success. They knew their sharp approach wood lead to success.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: This team put some bite into quality engineering this year. Their bright machine was crafted with reliability and durability in mind. This team has successfully stalked and solved engineering issues to make a quality machine.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With all the competition, this bot has to keeping on firing even on the move. This team has ONE eye on the prize at all times. It is truly the gift that keeps on giving. They remember all there past glory, even the parts that are classified.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.script: You're not in a simulation, this team's robot is undercover. You'd never know that their robot's data logging is on the hunt for clues. As they go from code changes to simulated matches, this team goes from Covert to Classified.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota IN & VU CARA
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Imagery is evident throughout their pit, uniforms, machine, and mascot. FIRST core values are demonstrated in all aspects of this team. Their bamboo-tiful panda made us smile.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This LEGENDARY student-led team impacted students of all ages, including children with special needs, and Title-I schools through their after school programs, STEM Nights, STEM Galas, programming camps, and being a student voice to promote STEM access for all. This team attracts and brings together 14 counties, and gives every student THREE A's: "Advocate, Advance & Advise". They're not just BREATHING FIRE; they face every problem with: “YES and…”

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This team shoots for the STARS with their design experimentation and purposeful back spin, to make sure their balls don’t collide in FLIGHT. Sleek as a ROCKET, this team’s robot was able to LAUNCH to the top! With a custom controller and robust navigation system, this team ROCKETED into the stratosphere.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: Today the Judges create the SPREADING STEM award! This team has written a book on their widespread efforts to advance STEM all around them. This team is ACTIVE in their community spreading FIRST to 25% of children across their city with many more to come! Their efforts aren’t confined to their city, they have even spread STEM in Africa.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This team’s POWERFUL “FIRST for Everyone” initiatives reach the far corners of the world. They make sure under-resourced teams in Asia and Europe are INCLUDED in their efforts. This team’s ENERGY for expanding FIRST’s impact shows that, yes, batteries ARE included.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: Even with limited resources, this team leads student-run educational workshops, STEM training, scholarship funding, a model UN hackathon, and they support FLL & FTC programs. Nothing SHAKES this team. Even when their captain's Visa gets declined, they charge-on & roll with it. They may be only 2 years old, but they're more than a PROTOTYPE!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s sponsors don’t just write a check for this team’s BOT, they stay year after year, decade after decade. They are also quietly saving the planet with extensive battery recycling efforts. They needed more space, they made their case, and found a HACK to get it done. These HACKERS will be around for years to come!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: This team is BLUE from traveling from far away. Their REPTILIAN spirit screams FIRST for ALL as they expand the spirit of FIRST through Latin America. Their energy flashes like LIGHTNING!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team utilizes effective geometry and high ouput to RETRIEVE fuel flawlessly. These DOGS lead the PACK, FETCHING in any direction. They defined the problem, created a plan, tested their solution, and UNLEASHED their potential.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: Engineering a blueprint for gracious professionalism, these NERDS love to see the competition succeed. Bumping their way through districts, they assure competitors pass inspection and are ready for the field. When alliances are chosen, they fortify first-timers. And when the final buzzer sounds, their reach extends beyond the field, delivering letters to lift spirits for Wounded Warriors and young patients who need it most. It’s in their NINJA DNA.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had the judges saying HOT DOG! With fuel FLYING flawlessly and 90 degree indexing, their entire HIVE works in perfect harmony. They STING the competition as their robot BUZZES with creativity!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: With robust design and quality standards, this team has been put in motion, and it STAYS IN MOTION. This FORMIDABLE robot withstands the true test of MAGNITUDE in the field. We already know the FORCE is with you!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With their intense level of automation and comprehensive fail safes, this team beats the MEDIAN. With a modified drone controller and VR headset, their drivers don’t just run code, they RAPTOR around the field with precision in both auto and teleop. This team is far from AVERAGE, by not bunting, but hitting the bullseye every time.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.script: From SILENCE to sparks, this team has entered the arena. This TEAM uses distinct technologies in autonomous mode to focus on rapid path planning and specialized vehicle. When their robot comes alive, they don’t WHISPER, they SCREAM!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Johnson Division presented by Gene Haas Foundation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team uses the NUCLEAR option to draw attention to FIRST. Like Superman, they get their power from the ATOMIC yellow sun. They are also ADAMANT about curing cancer by wearing pink and annually participating in Relay for Life.

With a couple of decades of experience, this team has a lot of practice forming an alliance. They are extremely active in their community, with strong growth inside and outside their team. They used extensive research to aim their efforts and form detailed action plans with achievable intermediate steps. With conferences, event hosting, and leading a multi-team effort to transform robotics in their state, this team is truly a FIRST ACT. Sustainability equals success.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This student-built team rose above the competition. They focused this year on improving long-standing team initiatives for global impact. This team’s Robot Built Them.
This team impressed the judges with their unique intake. Their robot has a cohesive design from its rollers to its double shooter. This team proved that anything is Hemi-Possible

This team has done a lot with a little. Moving beyond camps, this student-led team runs a full year-round adventure. Bonding together with other teams, this purple team has created success both on and off the field.
They rode right up to the edge of extinction. Then built a welcoming space and enduring knowledge base. This team is hiding a mighty surprise

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: They rebuilt and grew their team by more than double this year. They keep mentors and middle-schoolers returning to them through presentations and training. This team strong arms funds in their community with a fun arm wrestling fundraiser.

This team entangled the judges with their spirit for FIRST. Their enthusiasm gears up the objectives of FIRST both at competition and throughout their summer camps that are more than STEM. This team put the A in S-T-E-M.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s seamless design has gone the distance. The other teams shed tears at the sight of this cannon. This fiery bird is reborn at every competition.
This small team understands that overcoming chaos takes teamwork. They built a coalition and improved their team by simply building others. When it comes to GP, this team is chef’s K.I.S.S.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team proved that creativity can be inspired by functional purposeful design. From their intentional 3D printed tires to their excellent wire management, their robot is a pillar of stability and field control. Pouncing into the spotlight with a purple spark and magnetic roar.

This team braved the storm both on and off the field. This team’s quality focus on prototyping and testing proved its toughness “frame by frame”. Their spindexer cone generates a typhoon cleaning up fuel on the field.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team kept a bird’s-eye on the prize. While their shots where on point, they showed there is always wiggle room to grow. This team’s juggling with a full wingspan.

It seemed their robot’s eyes allowed them precise control in all zones of the field. Their double trench auto consistently arced the fuel into the hub with great efficiency. The control of this turreted machine allowed these green titans to autonomously rise to the top of the pack.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has the drive to get it done. They are excited to share how they are using their image to make robotics welcoming to all. You can tell these amicable cats by their cool jackets.

This team pours their energy into their school and community — mentoring students of all ages, building excitement for STEM, and creating opportunities that lift kids toward futures they never imagined. When they encounter a barrier, they don’t slow down; they accelerate. Their impact reaches far beyond their own community. When robotics programs across their state began to fade due to unstable funding, this team refused to let the next generation lose access to the inspiration that shaped them. With determination and heart, they stepped into advocacy — meeting with legislators, sharing stories, and helping secure dependable statewide funding for robotics. And because they know real change grows when others join the movement, they created an Advocacy Day to teach students and mentors how to use their voices too, multiplying their impact. Their work doesn’t just support their own team; it strengthens the future of STEM across their entire state and region. Their belief that “Every Kid Can” comes to life through their 6 E’s — Excite, Engage, Equip, Empower, and Expand — they are opening doors for students of all backgrounds. This team lifts others and builds a future where every kid has the chance to shine. They don’t just dream big — they break away from limits. Congratulations, Team 3937, Team Breakaway

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: While this is a newer team, the fruits of their labor have definitely paid off. Recognized for their kindness, assistance, and generosity when they hit the pits, their enthusiasm and impact go far beyond the field of play. Whether providing office hours for those in need, establishing and mentoring over a dozen teams, hosting events or presenting at the National Advocacy Conference, this team hits hard to inspire others and expand STEM far and wide. They don’t just talk the talk, they “waka” the walk. Congratulations, Team 10101, Critical Hit.

In a sea of intricate machines, one team proves that true elegance can be born from masterful simplicity. Guided by this philosophy, they engineered a clean and robust robot with easy access to subcomponents and a design focused on practical performance and seamless execution on the field. Success through intentional and streamlined planning, this team could not have built a “coolah” bot. Congratulations, Team 3753, BulahBots!

The judges want to recognize this team for their dedication, enthusiasm, and the joy they spread throughout the FIRST community, They fully embrace the spirit of FIRST Robotics—through mentoring at all levels of FIRST, exciting robot builds, meaningful community outreach, and high‑energy STEAM days, they spark curiosity far beyond their own team wherever they go. They don’t just promote STEAM; they make it come alive. Whether hosting their unforgettable celebration banquet—or running their crowd‑favorite silent auction—this team brings a fun, positive vibe that’s truly infectious. Congratulations, Team 3616, Team Phenomena

This team is leading the charge as they are just beginning to build their legacy for the future of STEM through FIRST. The judges SAW their accomplishments and passion for FIRST as they rode in with their cohesive community spirit. Working to gain support from their area schools, local industries, and government agencies, they were able to corral the community to keep their local regional competition alive and thriving. Congratulations, Team 10943, WHJ RoboStangs

Though this team had a rough start they realized quickly that meaningful changes happen through the accumulation of small actions. They are proud of their efforts establishing connections with programs in their feeder schools where they serve as mentors to the younger students. Through the efforts of all team members, they hosted STEM competitions, career camps, showcases, and school tours, they reached over 800 kids across multiple schools this year! The members of this team are working their way to the top, one paw at a time! Congratulations, Team 10217, Catahoula Blue Dogs

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Rooted in more than just gears, this team proves sustainability isn’t a bunch of baloney! Cultivating student leaders using their unique leadership development structure & success in student grant writing, this team is building a strong future all while maintaining lasting relationships with sponsors and alumni. Following their mission of having fun and doing cool things that help people, this team and INDI-HAMMA JONES have no problem bringing home the bacon! Congratulations, Team 1902, Exploding Bacon

This team truly embodies what it means to lift each other up. With loud cheers and contagious enthusiasm, whether in the shop, at competition or in the community, their energy level never dips,... they are definitely not a quiet bunch. Through summer camps and partnerships with local governments, they’ve built a spirit of outreach that inspires everyone around them. Starting each day with a mindset check‑in, this team moves together with purpose and passion, like a tornado, leaving a lasting impression wherever they go. Congratulations, Team 2080, Torbotics

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team navigated key game challenges and engineered intricate solutions from initial conception through final completion. Their mastery of an ELEGANT FIX, demonstrated a rare ability to add critical components without creating new points of failure. They proved this by solving problems before sailing onto the field. Congratulations, Team 2992, The S.S. Prometheus

The impact of this team’s commitment to gracious professionalism has been widely recognized -not just during competition, but throughout the year. They have made a meaningful impact by sharing STEM knowledge with students halfway around the world, coaching other teams on how to prepare for judging sessions, and hosting events to raise funds for community organizations that support victims of domestic violence. Their focus on uplifting others and helping improve performance is un-wavering and truly on point! Congratulations, Team 3284, Camdenton Laser

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: These inventive minds have developed a remarkably original robotic solution. They intentionally engineered a unique component that mimics the inertial properties of traditional rubber shooters. With a lighter, more efficient design, their rotating shooter drum allows this team to launch the fuels and STEEL the score. Congratulations, Team 8808, SWLA Tech Pirates

This team really feels at home on the field with a bot that sets a high bar for quality. From the quick disconnect pins to unique vibration rollers, one could say they "shook up" the competition. Yep, this "squad" definitely did not drop the bomb. Congratulations, Team number 16, Bomb Squad

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team stepped onto the field with a level of control that immediately stood out. Their command of their machine was so smooth and deliberate that every movement looked like it was choreographed. Their control system amplified their innovative design, allowing them to shift speeds on the fly while maintaining remarkable accuracy and consistency. When you need a bot that stays locked in, dialed‑in, and laser‑focused on its target… who are you gonna call? Congratulations to Team 4635 — PrepaTec BotBusters!

This team sets a new standard for autonomous performance when their robot springs into action. Their ability to compare simulated gameplay with real-time performance gives their on-field mapping navigation its impressive speed. With deadly accuracy, their shooter sets the field abuzz when it swarms the hub with fuel. Congratulations, Team 8044, Denham Venom.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Embracing their roots with exceptional and attractive visuals, this team set the gold standard for theme and design. Their pit, team gear, and machine all work together to engineer an experience. Stickers, posters, and accents echo the principles of FIRST and create a world where every detail feels intentional. This team didn’t just build a robot — they built a visual story that keeps you coming back for another look. Their outstanding aesthetic integration and creativity will stand the test of time, Congratulations, Team Number 3468

While many teams have influenced their school, community, and region, this team has redefined their school, community, and region, as champions for FIRST and STEM. This team inspired their school to offer more STEM related programs and created pathways from FLL to FRC. Through their sustained outreach, they've built a thriving FIRST community within their district. They have expanded STEM opportunities in their region and advocated for additional STEM education funding statewide. This team's impact reaches deeply at home and across the planet, including Ukraine, Morocco, Rwanda, and Brazil. This team's cosmic story won over the judges.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Engineering Inspiration is about spreading the message of FIRST. The judges found a team that we feel is an outstanding example. They: Spread the message of FIRST through their rookie outreach. Creating a community maker space for everyone to use. Redistributing parts from one team to another. Actively outreaching to STEM adjacent communities such as gamers and anime Promoting STEM education to disadvantaged students. Congratulations to team 10063 SCRAP

This team geared up with a design built for real world reliability. Through rigorous prototyping they delivered an intake with true flex appeal, twin flywheels that stayed perfectly spun up, and an autonomous game that hit its marks. Clean, simple, and anything but platitudinous, this robot shows what thoughtful industrial design can do on the field. The Industrial Design Award goes to… Team 3467 — The Windham Windup!

This team impressed the judges with a trio of speed, simplicity and optimization. Their sweet robot combined three flavors of capabilities in a well layered package. For demonstrating that thoughtful simplicity can produce smooth results, the judges are proud to recognize team 1119 Pup Cups.

In nature a river flows through the landscape changing its nature along the way. A teams journey is often not a straight one. Sometimes things rush along, growing, building robots, and sometimes they hit a dam and it all comes to stop. When a team runs into a dam, if it can overtop the dam, then the team can return to a rising team, that overcomes the challenges and can grow green again. Congratulations team 1735 the Green Reapers.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has focused on making stem accessible to their community. Their business plans and recruitment methods have prepared them for the future. This team endured and stood firm this year; they persevered Congratulations team 5962 perSEVERE

In the deep blue sea of competition, some teams simply swim… But others make waves everywhere they go. With jaws-dropping enthusiasm, fin-tastic costumes, and cheers loud enough to echo across the field, they prove that spirit is more than just noise — it’s about lifting up every team around them. You might even say… when it comes to excitement at this event, this team is at the top of the food chain. Congratulations, Team 663 Power Sharks

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s simplified control of their complicated robot exemplified excellence in engineering. Their ability to reduce controls down to 3 buttons, design a robot with dual spindexers, as well as use vision to adapt to bumps during auto, made this team a particularly NASH-ty alliance member on the field. Congratulations team 1768 Nashoba Robotics!

Gracious Professionalism is fundamental to FIRST. We ask everyone to exhibit Gracious Professionalism all the time. Behaving graciously is easy when things are going your way. It’s a lot less easy to be gracious when things aren’t going your way, when you are not winning, or when your robot is not working. The judges and robot inspectors witnessed a team being gracious when things weren’t going their way. They accepted the guidance from the robot inspectors, were grateful for help that was offered and appreciative of everyone’s effort. For being a great example of being gracious while under pressure. Congratulations to team 9644 NEIA Robotics.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a pride worthy set of original engineering ideas. Their robot blends simple mechanisms with creative twists, showing they aren’t afraid to think beyond the usual lion’s share of designs. From fuel handling to clever wiring solutions and precision shooting, their creativity really roared to life. For demonstrating elegant engineering with bold imagination, the Creativity Award goes to… Team 8013 — The Boston Lions!

This team showcased fabrication with intent. Their transparent robot displayed clear design, attention to detail, and consistent performance on the field. With robustness and iteration at the forefront of their team, they’ve created a perfect ‘storm’ for a quality team. Congratulations team 5422 Stormgears!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The dynamic control system on this robot sets them apart from the competition. This team “Rebuilt” their coordinate system, tracks the fuel they intake, and scores with incredible speed. With seamless control system integration across the board, this team gives their alliance a lot of leverage. Congratulations Team 6328, Mechanical Advantage!

This team's versatile auto races under the trench to the Neutral Zone multiple times for fuel. Their localizing "shoot on the move" 210 degree turret design was proven on their practice bot before ever hitting the field. Give us a minute, to congratulate to the home team - 4909: The Bionics.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: They’re decorated in their spoils of war. The visuals are integrated throughout their robot, pit and team. This team is the hoot of the competition. Congratulations Team 3182 Athena's Warriors

This team has shown recent exponential growth, sparking meaningful change in their community. A long established team, they prove that there is always room to grow; recently doubling their FRC enrollment. They have found new potential in their community starting new FLL teams, hosting many FIRST events and bringing STEM into their schools. This team has received over $1.2 million dollars in grants to help fund stem education to over 22 thousand students. Developing experimental robotics, they brought it to Massachusetts, the United States, Ukraine, Paraguay and beyond. Reminding us that building a better future takes more than a village, it takes a herd.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team will “herald” their success by singing their “own” anthem. Even their newest members share their message, creating unique events, turning useful facts into accessible crafts. This team is “bred” to be a “large” presence in their community.
In terms of design this team soars above the rest. Their cohesive red 3D prints tie everything together. Their next bot surely has big pants to fill.

If the judges had to pick one word to describe this team it would be TOGETHER. Demonstrating the values of first through prioritizing continuous learning. No matter what stands in the way of the next generation this team is sure to persevere.
This team is rebuilding from the basement up. These bucks continue to battle, sparring through any challenge they face. This team’s reset has them solidly on the path to success.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is committed to helping the planet, one bottle at a time. They are expanding their pack, both close to home and abroad. Their pipeline ensures there won’t be a lone wolf.

Whether they're on the field or off, this team makes it loud. With angry eyes and friendly faces, you'll see their mascot proud. By bringing farmlands to the city, they’ll make sure everyone sees that “Somerville Leads the Way”.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: They didn’t need a “charge” to make an impact. They turned their robot into a seamless “chain reaction” of motion, timing, and control. They showed that with a “neutral core” at the heart of the team design process; you never “destabilize” the game field.
Through camps and community STEM volunteering, they are focused and available for all. They will open their heads, hearts and shop for any that have need. Like a “neon” sign this team shines bright.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team sailed the “C” of creativity. From the start, they designed a system that would maximize space while they fish for fuel. With all that extra space, they could reel in a sea monster!

To increase their robustness this team continuously changed and improved. Now, their robot can recover from any challenge. Their philosophy of “only trust where we are scoring” ensures their dreams come true on the field.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team took their robot on a “Quest” through a video game engine. Their unique localization let them score from anywhere on the field. Despite what their name implies, their controls were the opposite of Chaos.

This team showed “exponential” control and consistency over their robot. Their flight paths aren’t “batty” and get to the “root” of the issue by maximizing the time to shoot while moving. This sets them up for success when “squaring” off against any opponent.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team doesn’t just walk the walk, they fly through the competition. From bill to the bot, their cohesive themed branding was polished playful, and flowed seamlessly through every detail of their presence. They make a quack-teastic splash.

This team is very disciplined. They have in-house grants to provide member reinvigoration projects. They had 30+active outreach events inside FIRST, including Robocon and helped start 3 other FRC teams. Their summer camp uses Liger Boxes designed through one of their grants. They helped start 3 other FRC teams. Congratulations Ligerbots, 2877.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: They drive STEM deep into their community to inspire FLL teams, because for this team engineering goes far beyond the robot. This team has taken flight to spread STEM to hunt down every future engineer. They are RUmBLe-ing the world, and for them engineering is a way of life. These raptors don’t just build robots…..they build engineers.

This team's robot is efficient, elegant, and effective. While they look great just sitting in the pit, watching them score fuel is truly a sight to behold. This team may be neutral in charge, but their design is electrifying.

This team shines bright each time they blink across the field with fiery speed. Their consistency and meticulous attention to detail in every aspect of their on-and-off the field design always drew the eye. To the delight and surprise of the judges, this team even incorporated their team number into their iconic yellow color.

This rookie team embodied everything that FIRST is about - a love for science and technology and a solid, fundamental robot. They are heating up the competition with some small but mighty upgrades. They keep it simple, but every modification counts! Even the mightiest creatures start their journey hatching from a single egg - we are excited to see them spread their wings in the future!
This team rebuilt itself from scrap meta. They persevered against challenges, and reconstructed their database as a unified team. This herd will clearly be galloping into a promising future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team strengthens their program with creative fundraising and outreach. Sustainability is practiced every day with car pools, provided hot lunches and bio degradable 3d printed parts. They are following their own yellow brick road toward a sustainable future.

This resilient team demonstrates pride in developing solutions. Throughout the season, they have managed risks and risen from failures. Seen or not seen, this team solves problems and always lands on their feet

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team has charted a course through the ages. Iteration after iteration, they have documented and built upon the lessons of the past. Piloting a practical design, housing four modular cannons, they are blasting their way through the competition.

This team consistently takes the high road both on and off the field with their sportsmanship and teamwork. Even outside the season, they bring the spirit of FIRST to their community, teaching people of all ages to inspire others. Their outreach isn’t just “Fluff”, it’s inspiring the next generation of thinkers.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s shooter has been prowling around the field this weekend. They look at this year’s challenge and turned itn 90 degrees. They served up a solution with the performance of a panther.
This is a team that loves to be in charge. With software that can be used to test individual components, this team is in control. They have a freaky robust Robot that can take a hit and keep moving.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team didn’t just write code; they engineered intelligence. Their solution impressed the judges with a triple-loop control system that allowed their robot to accurately shoot while in motion. When the judges saw their detailed whiteboard filled with the entire mathematical derivation, it was clear this team had merged brains and creativity into one seamless system.

Rumbling across the field, this robot has a mind of its own. When an operator gives the go to score, it’s the machine that decides when to start the storm. As a small team with big dreams, they don’t just keep their head in the clouds.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team brings infectious energy and whimsical fun to everything they do. Their pit, outfits, and, of course, their machine design reflect the fun, form, function and flair of their lovable crustacean mascot.

To the team winning Impact today, the award is 100% a team effort. 100% of the team contributed to the submission and presentation. 100% of the team worked on the impact projects the team undertook. The Girl Scout Gold Award shares the same mission and values as FIRST®. It explores root causes with a sustainable solution to a project. 100% of the team contributed. May the 4th has many different meanings in our FIRST® community. Star Wars Day, May the 4th be with you, is the best known. For this team May the 4th is a day of celebration of STEAM in their multi-town community. On May 4th, this team showcases STEAM in a community that lost an inspirational student at a young age. The team works with these students’ classmates in celebration of hope and inspiration. May the 4th be with Team 173 RAGE Robotics.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Whether it’s their summer camp, STEAM club, or STEAM nights, this team’s commitment to spreading STEAM is unquestionable. It’s no wonder that a team this strong doesn’t just mentor FLL, but also hosts the state championship. Their outreach initiatives are ironclad, their pipeline secure, and it won’t rust away because this team is galvanized.

They're here to CHOMP through the competition. Their fabrication process, prototyping, and maintenance system are an exemplar for how robots should be made. We look forward to seeing more from this lean, mean, GREEN, machine.

This team impressed us with their hardware, heart, and planning for the future. The young team members have learned the skills to both build a robot and give to the community by granting wishes. Technically their dual shooter and very large fuel hopper made the difference.

Being a young team, doesn't mean you can’t already start making an impact on FIRST. With this team building a brand, focusing on skill development, and thinking about next year, the judges expect great things to come from this rookie. Look out for these bandits, Congrats Team 10910, The Outlaws.

Overcoming challenges requires teams to dig deep. Focusing on being less mentor reliant, they have made conscious efforts to build up their new students and fundraising efforts. This team does not rust under pressure,

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The thoroughness of this team’s planning really pulled in the judges. They charged up the year with brand new budgeting systems. They are building a strong team culture through team dinners, skill-building Workshop Wednesdays, and student-run office hours where students help students. This team is attracting success with long lasting structures.
This team is spreading their spirit across the state. Their enthusiasm is always on "display". Just like a unicorn, this team is one of a kind.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team rides to the rescue when challenged. Their thoughtful process and STEM skills save the day. You will know them by their robot in shining armor.

This team soars through the skies. Working together with other FRC teams, they help bring everyone to into the FIRST community by making FIRST more accessible for differently abled individuals. The grace that they use when working with other teams would surely earn them a spot in the Greek pantheon.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This is a team that truly represents their entire school. They have overcome many obstacles with thought, design, research, and creativity. From a custom heat sink to their bumper pin removal tool, watch this triple Sushi shooter go the distance.
This team has unleashed the dog on the competition. With Pride in their work from soldered electrical connections to custom 3D printed mounts and covers. Quality is the Law.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Phonetically speaking this team’s approach to control was anything but ordinary. Their operator control station really impressed the judges. Everything is coming up roses for this team.

This team calculated a path to success using autonomy. The variety and quality of their automation helps them launch balls high into the sky. And when the match starts, they hightail it into the center…

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From their bot to their gear, when it comes to the theme, it’s all here. Their theming fits their mood, and their mascot showcases their history and AGE. Look out for Sandslash, because this team’s imagery catches all of our hearts.

This team proved that even from a small community, you can build an impact that reaches an entire state. They stand out as a role model team with their dedication to each other and their surrounding community. By mentoring and starting teams, leading events, supporting international efforts, advocating for STEM education, and creating a year-round hub for robotics, they expanded access to FIRST in lasting and meaningful ways. Living their motto, “Learn it, Do it, Teach it!”, they continue to uncover potential and build Vermont’s future.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: The thunder of this unique herd is heard near and far. The passion of this vision in purple can be found inspiring at the town parade, leading girl scouts, and mentoring FLL. They bring their message of inspiration and advocacy to audiences from town hall to the State Capitol. Grab your shades, because this team shines bright.

This team knows how to optimize their robot build with spreadsheets and engineering software. Revision control keeps their design process on track and machining tolerances tight. They won’t get wound up if their robot takes a hit on the field, because analysis found they have strength to spare.

The Judges decided to give this award to a team that represents what FIRST is all about. They had a full range of outstanding attributes, from robot performance to spreading the message of FIRST. Few teams can KRAM arts, engineering and STEM outreach into a single program like them.

This team exceeded expectations. Their hands-on approach to learning had them swerving across the field with style. From their basement to MIT, they conducted themselves like veterans. From bot to bumpers, this team stood out amongst the competition. CHOO CHOO, All Aboard the RED LINE.
Focusing on business and STEM, this team has been doubling the team size year after year. They are doing this all while striving to EARN their way to Worlds 3 years running

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team may be mighty red, but through loss and rebuilding, they continue to stand tall. With pen in hand, they pass down knowledge—so watch out for the lessons they leave behind. For them, being giants isn’t the exception… it’s standard operating procedure

With a spirited entrance to the competition, this team brings a warm introduction to STEM. They light the pathway for their journey while having an amazing time. This team creates an environment where people can fail forward and turn a flicker of failure into a spark of success.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This award was chosen to celebrate the design of a robot with flexible and cooperating components. This team's robot is ambidextrous and automatically ducks its head to go under the trench. And even if something went wrong, this robot would be protected with its Hammer Head.

This team embodies STEM for everyone and is committed to demonstrating FIRST core values on their team and in their community. They waltzed into the judges hearts and sashayed before the competition while supporting their most vulnerable denizens. For them, E means everyone despite the challenges their team faces.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s robot was well-rounded. The team was intentional in their creative and unique design. When it comes to intakes, this FLEX-ible robot is ahead of the curve.
When doing pit checks on this bot it will keep them performing at top notch. The quality of this bot is above all else. The clean and neat wiring makes Deadshot a happy bot.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When the day shift is over and precision is still needed, one team proved that innovation never sleeps — delivering control systems that quietly turned complexity into competitive advantage during the “night shift”. Their robot leveraged advanced sensor fusion, dynamic path planning, and seamless driver-assist automation to maintain accuracy, adapt in real-time, and consistently outperform under changing match conditions. That level of intelligent design and controlled execution kept them out of the valley to deliver peak performance.

When the match began and drivers stepped back, this team’s robot took command of the field with confidence, showing that true power can come from wings… and a roar. With consistent, reliable, and high-performance autonomous routines, this robot executed precise movements, delivered game pieces efficiently, and repeatedly set the tone before human control even began. When it comes to soaring over the competition, these birds do so in a royal manner.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has no bones about it — when they need parts for their bot, they’re not afraid to dig them up. From the shop floor to the competition field, they build piece by piece, stronger every time. But beware… because rising above it all is their secret weapon -- the Flying Skeleton.

records.eventName: FCH District Bethesda MD Event presented by Bechtel
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: It is FRIGHTENING how much time this team invests into their community. Increasing their outreach three-fold in the last year, these champions of STEM logged over 1,000 volunteer hours. From multiplying mechanical rabbits to hosting amazing STEM events, this PROJECT is inspiring the future of engineering and robotics.

records.eventName: FCH District Bethesda MD Event presented by Bechtel
records.script: This strong team charged into the ARENA. The Judges loved their high-performing, two-cycle autonomous period and their advanced robot positioning system. The crowd roars with thunderous applause: 8! 8! 8! 8! 8! 8! ...

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: This passionate team dug deep into the unique interests of their community to bridge the gap between robotics and agriculture. records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: These competitors have clearly left their mark on this competition. They have created a highly integrated, practical, and visually-pleasing robot that has been a beast on the field. Just like the apex predator of the jungle, this team has clawed its way to the top of the scoreboard.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: Mistakes were made. But the gears meshed and generated an FRC team. With help from others the Guilford Park Gear Heads were born.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: Despite facing significant hurdles in gaining recognition from their school, this team has proven their resilience. They expanded their reach fivefold this year, and have a rock-solid sustainability plan and a deep commitment to the values of Gracious Professionalism. Leading the way with a fierce spirit, this pack has truly wired themselves for success!

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team was very supportive of both their future and the world around them. They enthusiastically supported their fellow students through numerous environmental and robotics initiatives. Whether they’re fixing broken desks or supporting the FTC community, they bring a rainbow of positivity to every corner of their community.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: This team’s spirit shines bright even in the rain. Their peer mentorship strategy creates a welcoming environment where mutual respect is valued. Besides, who doesn’t love Pear-Bear?

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Robust systems engineering led to a great game. Marvelous mechanics kept the robot in the game. Excellent execution demonstrated they were great engineers. Great gameplay showed they were not cavalier.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: This team really showed the judges’ that they found their role here today. They’re always first to come to the rescue and an OVERALL help to one and all. Between scheduling shuttles and working to fix others’ robots, this team showed their GP. Congratulations to team 888, Robotiators!

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to creativity, this team took it outside the box. Unique design challenges require unique solutions and this team learned from previous years what not to do. LIFE comes at you fast, so why be square when you can be a trapezoid?

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: These competitors have come from above to lead the field. Their robot is robust and reliable, their intake has never broken! When it comes to building a quality robot, this team of hawks has flown above the rest.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team takes pride in their experimental yet robust techniques to support driver function. With a focus on game automation, this team employed techniques to detect herds of fuel and jump them over the moon with physics backed polynomial regression calculations. MOO-ve over teams, we have some cattle on the loose.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.script: This team launches into action with precision and purpose. Their robot’s adaptive autonomous and shoot-on-the-move capability aided their STELLAR performance. They charged forward like a legendary unicorn.

records.eventName: FCH District Pasadena MD Event presented by Plummer Industries
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The judges were impressed with the way this team adapted their theme to this year's game. The team's logo, colors, and theme are consistent throughout their pits, documentation, uniforms, and robot. This powerful rebranding was due remarkably to the work of a freshman.

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team lives their values. Their commitment to genuine assistance is clear from the outstanding outcomes they engender in partner teams from FLL to FRC. This team has soared to the occasion with accessibility efforts, and with more than twenty thousand people reached in person over the last three years. Their novel, unique ROV efforts for data collection in the Chesapeake Bay led to impactful outreach with a local maritime museum and earned them the judges' esteem. Congratulations to team 1111, the Powerhawks!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team brought FIRST at scale to their community. They launched STEM all over their county. They were ready to inspire from thee Geck-go. Congratulations to team 1629 for the Engineering Inspiration Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team exemplifies throughout the competition that they’re anything but slow. Their bot is intentionally designed and thoughtfully presented, executing challenges on the field with precision. When it comes to form and function, this team incorporates everything under the umbrella. Congratulations to team 1719 for the Industrial Design Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team always has a bird’s eye view. Their efforts to engage needy schools with the National Society of Black Engineers are forging powerful professional connections. Like a plane made of plants, these flowers soar. Congratulations to 3714 for the Judges Award for Professional Engagement!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: Though they are young, this team looked thee top. They are growing their impact, bringing the local community to the stands to watch them compete. They are heading to another dimension. Congratulations to team 11211 for the Rookie All Star Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: Integrated like a single circuit, these students are hardwired to rise to any occasion. Judges were impressed with their STEM advocacy, this young team grew rapidly and now possesses the scale and expertise to spread STEM. This pack of students are howling in their community. Congratulations to team 10679 for the Rising All Star Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team sparked inspiration with their sustainability plans. They surged ahead of other teams, embodying the principles of “people, prosperity, and planet.” When it comes to training, community outreach, and recycling, this team is simply electric. Congratulations to team 1389 for the Team Sustainability Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team slices through a crowd. Their enthusiasm and positivity geared up the judges. Recognizable from their Maryland-themed shirts. Congratulations to team 4541 for the Team Spirit Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: There are many building blocks to creating successful systems. Excellence in Engineering includes being able to co-ordinate multiple subsystems to a united plan. This team was able to square their requirements to bring functionality to the competition. Congratulations to team 8592 for the Excellence in Engineering Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: As much as FIRST is about competing, it’s even more about learning and growing. By assisting other teams both at competition and in the offseason, they are employing gracious professionalism everywhere they go. Working for this company means you’ll be surrounded by this positive promotion of learning, just wait and “C.” Congratulations to team 2377 for the Gracious Professionalism Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is taking math to the next level. Their unique pathing solution is guiding them and others to success, crunching numbers on-the-fly faster than ever. They show no mercy to the problems they vanquish. Congratulations to team 1418 for the Creativity Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team’s robustness soared to the occasion. These hawks screech quality planning. They have maximized their materials to allow Madison-proofed chaos. Congratulations to team 614 for the Quality Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.script: This team pounced into the competition. Their robot’s autonomy in accuracy, efficiency, and pathing all contribute to their pride. Few teams could withstand the roar of their competition. Congratulations to team 2199 for the Autonomous Award!

records.eventName: FCH District Severn MD Event presented by Arcfield
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A team’s image is a critical component of any successful endeavor, and this team has a bright future. Whether it’s shirt designs, buttons, or parts on their robot, taking a peek at this team is sure to leave an impression. Cause if it’s orange, and they can afford it, it’s going on the robot. Congratulations to team 339 for the Imagery Award!

This team has worked on developing widespread outreach efforts that serve to rise the tide that floats all boats for regional FIRST robotics and STEM education. With detailed plans for team development, on and off season recruiting, sponsorship fairs, and progressively developing their skills, this team has done more than its "FAIR SHARE" towards FIRST Impact.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team’s community outreach really sparked our interest. They spread the wealth of knowledge to the FIRST community, from First Lego League to training new college mentors, to demoing to the community. When it comes to perpetuating FIRST, this team pulls away from the HERD.

These engineers burst onto the field in vivid color, turning sketches into parametric models and capturing every decision in a complete design binder shaped by the entire team. Their student-driven process flows from concept to robot, building their own app-driven system to manage CAD numbers and keep every part and revision tightly clad. As the design race reaches the CHECKERED FLAG, the Industrial Design Award goes to Team 172 The Northern Force!

This year, the Judges have decided to give an award for simple but effective design. In a competition frequently involving complicated mechanisms and detailed strategies, this team has decided that a simple concept executed well is better than complexity. Like explorers on a legendary quest, they’ve charted their own course, focusing on a simple design optimized for defense. The Judge’s Award for Simplicity in Design goes to Team 8023, The Argonauts.
This team's comeback far exceeded the NORM, with focused efforts on getting back off the ground. These competitors rebuilt from the ground up, rose from the ashes, and hit the mark!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This student led team has put in over 2000 hours to reach more than 10,000 people in four counties. Financially, they sustain themselves with a profitable business, and most impressively, they’ve continued a multi-year initiative to make a science-based case for bumpers made of biodegradable materials.

This team's success stems from their roiling energy. They and their fans exhibit a boisterous spirit that isn't WHITE noise. It's what you get when your energy's wavelength lies BETWEEN yellow and red. Congratulations Team 4564 - Orange Chaos

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse

Give a round of applause to the team that puts GRACIOUS PROFESSIONALISM into overdrive, team 8410.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

records.script: For some, robotics is about building machines. But for one team, it’s about building something far greater. A legacy. A culture. A story that is carried forward far beyond each season. Because when impact is truly meaningful… it doesn’t slow down… it continues to move and ACCELERATE. This team has spent decades shaping not just students, but leaders—creating replicable systems where knowledge is passed forward, voices are found, RESPECT and UNITY are created, and confidence is built. Through a powerful, student leader structure they span every level of FIRST, and have reached thousands—removing barriers, expanding access, and ensuring that every student, no matter their background, has a place to belong and succeed. Their impact is not measured in seasons, but in generations—seen in the HEARTS of students who return as mentors, the teams they have grown, and the teams those teams have grown. They don’t just participate in FIRST… They define and set the standard and SPIRIT of what it means to sustain it, to live it, and to pass it forward. Some might say the GOLD STANDARD.

records.eventName: FIM District West Michigan Event presented by Grand Valley State University

records.eventName: FIM District West Michigan Event presented by Grand Valley State University
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.eventName: FIM District West Michigan Event presented by Grand Valley State University

records.eventName: FIM District West Michigan Event presented by Grand Valley State University

Listen closely and you’ll hear the whistle of this team cutting through the forest and the fog of Duluth for years to come.

They brought the heat all the way from the Pacific

Their outreach continues to crawl across Minnesota and beyond – and they are not slowing down any time soon.

So as they light the torch for the next generation, help us celebrate… the Tiki Techs!
