While most of us struggle with documentation, this team is uploading a variety of policies, guides, charts, videos and reels in multiple languages that have been viewed by thousands worldwide seeking to aid fellow FIRST teams across all points of the compass. These competitive Cats are on the prowl to find a way to sustain and grow their program through living and advocating for FIRST Core Values.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: From camps to comps, both day and night, this team does extensive outreach. Through education, they inspire others to spread their wings and fly. Purple and pink, they assemble, empower, grow, and think. Girls have no limits under the wings of this team.

Their team has everything planned, from robot design to maintenance checklists. Printed parts, belts, high rates of fire; this team has it all. Watch out if you’re on the red sea, those raiders will get ya!

K’nex-ing (connecting) all ages with compassion and care. Their bi-weekly visits bring seniors knowledge and joy. Understanding that STEM never retires, this team enriches the Golden Years with golden gears. The judges award for Compassionate Care goes to...
This team pays it forward in their community. From the bench through the basement, they have risen to the stars. This team truly rocks – something that would make Dr. Jones proud.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: From mentoring FIRST teams, to recruiting in the classroom, this team actively feeds their future. They’d rather ride the bus while picking up new students along the way. Brick by brick, they build across borders – giving their community a reason to recycle.

This team may not take up too much space, but their little engine will take them to the moon. Their energy and positivity are truly out of this world. Watch out because their genuine spirit is lightning in a bottle!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team demonstrated excellence on the field. Galloping, delivering, advancing excellence in engineering. They are electromechanical and a little diabolical with engineering solutions that are never unreliable.
You see them everywhere, like pebbles in a stream. Consistently fueling the Co-Opertition dream. Rockstars in real life, making everyone feel like part of their team.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: These students showed immense passion for their design process, specifically in how they identified and tackled a critical vulnerability on the field. To ensure their machine could survive the toughest matches, they engineered a custom auto-protection bar that was as intentional as it was effective. You can tell this team’s gears are always turning.

This team’s turret lights the way to the target. They built their robot to be reliable and flexible, allowing their team to be successful through the competition. These pups can take the hits and keep going!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is a high-tech powerhouse driven to find success. Armed with a precision navigation device, they move around the field with efficiency. This Hungry Hippo is chomping their way to victory.

Descended from an ancient dynasty, this team's robot punches ABOVE ITS WEIGHT. Evolved after countless iterations, it sweeps across the field and lights up the skies with perfect accuracy every time. Never disoriented, the twin turrets always focused on their goal - this team's performance is one for the history books.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team honors their roots - each member a unique flower in the bouquet. Their pit tells a story, standing like ancient ruins in the jungle.

This team covers the full STEAM pipeline from FLL Explore, to FLL Challenge and FTC teams. As a bedrock in their community they partner with local businesses from industrial shops to the local pizza and ice cream store. Their influence has created new classes at their school covering topics like astrophysics and ballooning where the team builds sensors to support classroom experiments and maintains a hydroponic garden. Hi-ho, hi-ho, it's off to work we go.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: The judges are over the moon with this team's outreach efforts, domestic and international. Working day and knight, they helped to develop their school's STEM curriculum, teaching their teachers. The judges are u-knighted in their excitement for this team.

Some robots catch your eye before they even move. This robot stood out with a clever brush designed to flex safely inside the trench, protecting both the robot and the field while still getting the job done. It had amazing speed of a sonic boom to blast past the competition.

Tackling the problem of FLL teams disbanding, this team stepped in to keep young innovators in the game. With teamwork, spirit and a playbook, they're building momentum for FIRST in their community. For putting FIRST first,

This team might be new, but their attitude and enthusiasm rivals the oldest teams in the league. They are excited to learn and grow, with other teams recognizing their clear understanding of Gracious Professionalism. Over the course of the event, their robot has risen like a phoenix, ready to play.
This team set out to discover new possibilities. From finding a new space to building their own robot from the ground up. They tackled every challenge like an archeologist uncovering a lost relic.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: It's no mystery how this team is consistently impressive and competitive. They focus on internal growth, external education and overall community development. If you throw this team a bone, they won't waste time chasing their tails.
This team knows the importance of perseverance. When it comes to sink or swim, this team doesn't get weighed down. Their determination and work ethic is as hard as iron.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team built a robot where every subsystem is pulled together and the details are dialed in. They assured performance with a flexible intake and a well organized spare part strategy. Like a mountain goat scaling a steep cliff, this team built a robot that climbs challenges with confidence—strong, balanced, and built to last.

This team's philosophy is to create bonds within their team and in their community. They practice Gracious Professionalism in their shop so it's second nature at the competition. They started as a team and they'll end as a team.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot was carefully crafted, where creativity and function work side by side. They were wise to choose a distinct mechanism that brings both style and function together. The robot was an absolute hoot—able to shake us out of a jam

Great robots don’t just perform well in one moment—they’re built with care, precision, and attention to the little details that make the whole machine strong from start to finish. Like a mighty moose forged from steel, this team’s robot stands tall—strong, resilient, and built to weather anything the field throws at it.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Innovative control and precision drives this design. They are hard to miss and even harder to beat - watch out for blue and yellow. The competition never saw it coming - it's pure sabotage.

This team dug through their data to let the past inform the future. They showed continuous improvement in their autonomous performance throughout the matches. They shook up this competition like an earthquake.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team really dug deep to match this year's theme. Their green and purple flags were easy to spot in the jungle. This team would look great, even in a parallel universe.
To prepare for this year’s robotics season, this team GEARED up for DUEL. They developed ADAPTIVE solutions in their community. This CRAZY team wowed the judges with their inclusive culture.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Uncovering this team’s number when fossils were discovered. Mining the path for future growth, their success can be seen in all levels of FIRST. Global reach can be seen across the map.
This team learned how to get over the hump. We’re all fired up about their design. Orange, Black, and Yellow! Where did you get those nice pants fellow?!
From Newark, New Jersey born and raised. Prototyping is the language they use every day. The judges give them “dos” thumbs up.
This rookie team checks all the boxes. This school embraces their community is ‘soaring’ to new heights. This team’s future ‘Rocks’
This team turned their community into a family. Amigos y amigas, this team breaks barriers with STEM. They are a pack ahead of the rest.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Their plan is comprehensive from recruiting, risks, and the environment. From recycling to rebuilding, this team reaches into their community. Give me liberty or give me science.
Bouncy like Tigger. We always see this team shining bright In the crowd. They’re Grrrrreat!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: When it comes to excellence, being first is nothing new to this team. From streamline design to double turrets, for double trouble, they make challenges look easy. When things get tough, this team really puts the Peddie to the metal.
This team provides “bands” and a “vice”. They keep track of who’s naughty and nice. This team was graciously “rocking”.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot created a swirl. Their design swept us away. Spinning fuel like “Fruit Loops”.

This team’s machine wasn’t just powerful – It was built with precision and grit. From blueprint to build, their aluminum beast showed craftsmanship and smart design. Armored up and stoppable, this bot might just make ‘The Doctor’ reach for his screwdriver.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has taken total control of their robot With buttons, slides and toggles, this robot made it easy to play the game. They don’t shoot air balls.
This team is First in more than one way. Hand in hand their autonomous mode had a mind of it’s own. This robot may resemble Swiss cheese but it’s clearly a gem.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This standout team cannot be missed. Their trivia is insightful not spooky. Pink Rover, Pink Rover, let the Robo-Rovers come over.

Previously, curiosity and creativity were not being nourished in the education system so this team took BOLD steps to challenge cultural norms. Then, the first contact with the Department of Education led to widespread policy change, encouraging RADICAL openness and pivoting from rote learning. So, this team recognized a significant underserved population and decided to recruit students, PASTORS and others to lead STEM transformation with FIRST! They reached thousands of young people, and expanded to multiple countries, demonstrating the IMPACT of “ZERO”. Congratulations to team 4253 Raid Zero from Taipei, Taiwan! The winner of the Impact Award goes to Team 4253 RAID Zero

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team embodied a new hand, a new plan, and with the same swagger. When things got dicey, they rolled a natural 20. The Regional Engineering Inspiration award goes to team 7426, PAIR OF DICE ROBOTICS!

This team's robot has distinct shine with all of the aluminum framework and unique front loader. Clean lines... Bold design... Every detail refined. Built with purpose, engineered ahead of its time. Sharp shooters on the scene, living the cowboy dream. Congratulations, the award for industrial design goes to Team 991, BroncoBots from Phoenix Arizona!

At this competition the judges are recognizing a team with the "CONNECTION" award. When considering the judges award, this team's compassion put them at the top of the pyramid. This team brings community and engineering awareness to multiple empowerment groups. The judges award goes to the warriors who are putting FIRSIT's core values into action. Congratulations Team 6479 AZTECH Robotics

This team generates energy within their northern Nevada community. Their talented robot would be a MVP for any All-Star game. They aced their outreach by continuing to support First Nevada in and around the Nevada's biggest little city. Congratulations Team 10903, The Ionizerz.

This team brought a whole new light to their STEM community. Their luminous display made them stand out in the crowd. Between mayoral visits and their work in schools, hospitals, and disaster relief they shined bright through it all. The rising all-star award goes to: 9233 Luminous Robotics team from Turkey!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is working hard to have robotics recognized as a SPORT in every school. They use recycling as a tool to minimize their carbon footprint. Honored for their commitment to sustainability, they demonstrate lasting impact through outreach, strong partnerships and inspiring the next generation of innovators. they continually strengthen their future through mentorship and environmental consciousness. Building a true "pillar of sustainability" ...Congratulations, Team 3990 Tech for Kids, from Montreal, Canada!

If a wave of roaring cheers and synchronized chants seems to follow every match they touch, you might already know who we’re talking about. They are being recognized for extraordinary enthusiasm and spirit, lifting every team and volunteer they encounter with contagious energy, constant support, and a joy for the game that never fades. You could say their presence feels like a fearless crew of northern warriors who arrive loud, proud, and always ready to strike with unstoppable team spirit. Congratulations Team 5851 the Striking Vikings!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team is definitely wired for success. They did not duck the opportunity to help others, nor did they "quack" under pressure. They take "owning who you are" to a whole new degree. Congratulations Team 6413 Degrees of Freedom.

From across the ocean, they "lei'd" gracious professionalism on every team they met, increasing the morale of all their peers. Their crusading efforts EXEMPLIFY the core values of FIRST Robotics Congratulations team 4270 Crusaders, from Honolulu, Hawaii!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team KNOWS how to design a creative component. They found ways to "climb" over the competition to achieve new heights. The Creativity Award goes to... Team 987 HIGHROLLERS from Las Vegas!

This team really brings the heat during the competition. The quality of their intake sets a very high standard. When it comes to meeting the rigors of competition this Mega team does not "horse around". Congratulations, Team 8005, Mega Meadowbots, from Las Vegas!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Some teams whined about the challenges presented by this year's game. But this team looked at the problem with a new set of eyes. They doggedly pursued a solution by rethinking what the problem was ...and succeeded! They even added their own set of eyes!! The award for Innovation in Control goes to 10183 ARC, from Las Vegas, NV!

This team's autonomous brought FIRE down on the competition. After their autonomous, their chips were seldom down. Even a blacksmith couldn't forge a better solution. The autonomous award goes to team 4421 Forge Robotics, from Calgary, Alberta, Canada!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team dug into the archaeology of past competitions. They boldly branded themselves with imagery that stretches brilliantly across banners, bots, and beyond. Whether at school, within the community or representing at competition, their fresh branding, engages EVERYONE, young and old alike! From Phoenix, Arizona, the winner of the 2026 FIRST Robotics Imagery Award goes to a true “Spitfire” of a team—Dragon Robotics, Team 2375, Bioscience High School!

Heart, Adaptation, Respect, Love, Excellence, Mobility - This team embodies all of these. The team takes their role as innovators and engineers to another level. Stepping up and stepping out into their community, this team is determined to level the field for all, partnering with local groups and building systems that last. For this team, good enough for competition is not enough. They are creating a sanctuary in their community. Each one- Teach one. Congratulations team 1880- The Warriors of East Harlem

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has built a complete sanctuary for STEM, ensuring that from hatchlings to fledglings, every student has a place to fly. Through engineering nights and their STEAM craft studio, they’ve created a migratory path that guides K through 12 students towards success. For providing the wings that lift their entire community toward the future, the engineering inspiration award goes to team 353, the Pobots!

The judges were impressed with this team’s very clean and efficient design. Their expanding intake and hopper system can hold a large number of fuel balls, and can score from a 3 point range. The color scheme accentuates the machines beauty, and the colors match the robots namesake. The industrial design award goes to “Lebot James” and team 287 Floyd Robotics!

This team brings STEM to life through their Stem outreach, inspiring students across their community. They keep the community informed with their weekly newsletter This team is a consistent bedrock within the FIRST community but never take them for granite. With creativity and spirit please join me in celebrating Team 810, the Mechanical Bulls of Smithtown!

This team may be brand new, but they are preparing for a solid future. They may be small, but they are working to recruit and train incoming student, and they have already gotten some hard hitting sponsors on board. And they are so proud of their first robot. As was said earlier today, this is a rookie team that does not play like a rookie! Team 11030 the Bonac Bots!

This team is STEADILY BUILDING its culture of growth, leadership, and inclusion. It is committed to PULLING EVERYONE IN through outreach to younger students and spreading the mission and spirit of FIRST. All team members get hands on experience after getting their FEET WET. This team is becoming a force to be reckoned with. They SWEPT THE JUDGES AWAY. Team 8267 RIPTIDE!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: After a year of low enrollment, this team took the initiative to assess their risks and came up with a comprehensive plan to promote growth. They used a creative fundraising structure with a predictive budget, and created a mentorship program to give younger students hands on leadership experience. Pulling in 100% of a community FLL team, the team members impressed the judges with their passion to sustain their program through future generations. Congratulations Team 5016 Huntington Robotics!

A surge of red, black, and gold fills the arena as this ream brings unstoppable energy to the stands. This small school brings big whale energy evident in their entire organization from team inclusion, school spirit nights, to competition day. Rising as the Beast from the East with unmatched spirit is Team 28, the Pierson Whalers!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This year’s winner put their own spin on comprehensive robot design. Each aspect of their robot reflects intentional application of engineering principles. Why use off the shelf? Build your own parts, be a rebel! The excellence in engineering award goes to team 2638, rebel robotics!

While others may rush, this team knows that a steady shell, strong with a steady and strong foundation is the surest way to win. From inviting all Long Island teams to pre-season events, any LI senior to apply for STEM scholarship and creating steminars for women, they have built a protective habitat of support for all. For proving that true progress happens when you carry your community on your back like a turtle, the gracious professionalism award goes to team 3624, the Soring Colts!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to creativity, this team doesn’t just think outside the box — they psyche out the competition entirely. Their 3D printed rack and pinion system and precision-crafted tpu rollers had our judges doing a double-take, and frankly, left them a little unhinged in the best way possible. Under pressure — and this team clearly knows a thing or two about PSI — they engineered a feeder design so clever and clean that it was enough to make our judges question their own sanity. We were completely psych-ed out by the ingenuity on display, and presenting this Creativity Award to team 533 - The PSIchotics is the only rational response.

This team knew how to “roll with the punches” and iterate and refine their designs. Their clean execution, thought out elements - intentional or unintentional- were impressive. Every panel had a purpose and every wire had a home. This robot doesn’t need the judges to say he’s quality, Chuck Norris already knows it!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: For this team, timing is everything. Their masterful control of their machine sent waves through the competition. No one is shocked that the Innovation in Control Award goes to team 263, Aftershock!
This team is a force to be reckoned with. Their machine's autonomous performance was fit for a king. The Autonomous Award goes to team 5736, Kingsmen Robotics!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A blaze of creativity ignites every detail, from a striking logo to bold banners and a robot that radiates their fiery spirit. With glowing intensity, their inferno inspired design leaves a lasting impression. Fueling the competition with visual imagery is team 4458, The Infernobotix!

Under chaotic environments, this team excelled in creating technical, social, and emotional impact. As one of the oldest teams outside of North America, they have mentored numerous FIRST teams and advanced numerous initiatives both locally and globally. From flood-ravaged streets to favelas, this team, no matter the crisis, no matter the barrier, kept everything UNDER CONTROL.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team is the heartbeat of connection, extending STEM Education into communities often out of reach. Through a powerful outreach mechanism, this team engages leaders and bridges schools as an organism of change. Their inspiring commitment to being strategic ambassadors of Science and Technology rises to extreme heights. Together they can climb any mountain.

records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team
records.script: This team has a very “Stealthy” look for the design of their robot. They doubled their fun with independent turrets while ensuring the fuel cells don’t collide. One could say they really applied their “brain” trust while also making the “giant” strides in their performance.

First & Forever Footprint Award: This team’s footprint will outlast their final season. As graduating seniors from a school closing its doors, they chose to plant lasting seeds in their community and at every regional they touched. They shared their culture and volce of FIRST in a way that will carry their community forward.

This all-girls team traveled from Taiwan and stood out for their extraordinary interpersonal dynamics, uplifting and supporting one another at every turn. They’ve demonstrated resourcefulness by working with other teams from their country, strengthening the FIRST community. They believe that “gender should not define who gets to build the future,” and even their butterfly logo reflects thoughtful design by integrating their team number.

The judges were blown away by these stars. Starting with only 10 members in their first year, they created and FLL and FTC pipeline to expand their team to over 60 members. Through their trendy social media, they have grown in sponsors by over 400% in just 2 years. This team stands strong in the face of challenges by inspiring new trends in their community.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Don’t mind the waste, all 145 lbs is accounted for. This team is destined to Prosper, all while playing ultimate frisbee, eating hot pot and BBQing at the beach. If you’re heading downtown, be sure to check out the Knights of BK Tech!

This team brings energy, resilience and joy to every part of the event. Despite travel challenges, a partial team, and damaged robot, they showed up cheering, collaborating across language barriers and captured fun photos with everyone to remember the experience. From stray cats, they carry their culture and love of FIRST everywhere they go.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team impressed judges wiht the way they logged their design process this season. Their progress was clear, data-driven, and intuitive to anyone from rookie members to judges. With their logs and data, they always had their finger on the PULSE!

This Team’s willingness to support others truly stood out. From creating an app to assisting others to generously donating parts, they consistently prioritized the success of the broader community. Like a seamless fusion of innovation and teamwork, these borgs not only lead the way but ensure that everyone has the opportunity to reach the finish.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their agitator, while not being easily agitated during the competition. The intentionality in their fixed pivot point and the design of their mechanisms were a stand out. When it comes to creativity, they were DEAD CENTRE!!!
This team readily demonstrated a commitment to quality. The strength of their intake allowed them to easily stalk their opponent . This team’s robot could survive even an encounter in the jungle.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team used software to give their drive team every advantage. Shift-synced controls, vision location and velocity interpolation kept this bot locked-in to score even while on the move. This team was SO in control of their BOT
This team started each match with a strong autonomous. They made sure to train and prep for any obstacle. Their double turrets made sure to spot each other in flexing their mind.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a cohesive and distinctive identity that soars from their pit to their robot, uniforms, and more. They took us through the ears of both their team history and journey through FIRST. This team flew the temple of impact over 400 miles to build a nest of artifacts here at the armory.

This team laid the foundation for what FIRST could become, transforming a single team into a nationwide ecosystem of innovation, starting teams across their region to empowering young women through initiatives in STEM, their impact is both measurable and deeply personal. Through partnerships and the integration of robotics into schools, their work doesn’t end with inspiration, it continues through sustainable programs, global collaboration, and resources that reach far beyond their borders. They didn’t just find the formula for impact, they became the R Factor.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team blew the judges away with their diverse outreach initiatives at home and spreading their wings overseas. Shifting the focus onto underserved communities, their dedication to STEM education is a game changer. Helping hundreds of students find their home, through workshops on CAD, circuits, and FIRST Lego League, this team STEELS the show.

Their robot is clean, compact, and intentional from the timing belt feeding system to the angled shooter that saves precious chassis space. Tight modular packaging, a seamless autonomous positioning system, and steady accurate shooting show what happens when form and function work together. This is industrial design done right

The Rebuilt Award With a new leadership structure emphasizing merit based participation, they aim to connect generations. This team went from seeking help to expanding their program and inspiring the youth within the community. If you want to catch this team after a match, give these rams 5 minutes to relax.
This team had a long commute to today's regional. Yet, they come ready with ambitious plans, big dreams, and a steel will to get it done. These masters of time are ready to get to work.

This team is on a mission, reaching beyond limits and bringing others along for the journey. Like a well planned launch, they explore exponentially while overcoming the hurdles of space. Through their electrified board game, they reach the horizon.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The ability to break down barriers has created momentous opportunities in this journey of inclusion. Working with ambassadors has made this team prosperous. Sign in and have a cup of water with this team that is committed to therapeutic diverse collaboration.

Seeding FIRST throughout the land, from FLL to FRC, Their enthusiasm knows no borders — it’s clear for all to see. With motivation, you never lose; their energy fills the room, Spot those big blue numbers from afar — you feel the spirit boom

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team's sleek and cohesive design allowed them to soar through the competition. Using their 4 limelights, they're able to watch like a hawk and shoot like a hunter; their unique cable management system and efficient integration provides constant contact and ensures that nothing slips through the cracks. For the team that dives beak-first into challenges, we say: No Hopper... No Problem!

This team leaves no stone unturned as they swoop in to support others. Their open doors create a culture of continuous collaboration, working side by side so every team can take flight. And they do it all not like a chicken, but like a hawk!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's unique approach to this year's game hooked the judge's attention as they climbed their way to the top. By utilizing custom vision, python scripts, and projectile motion calculations they ensured that no matter how high they pounce, they always land on their feet. This team's creative design approach me-wowed the judges!

This team's eyes lit up when asked about their pre-match checklist! They were prepared for all risks with their secure braided wiring and impressive, quick access to the "belly of the beast, plus there was extra added safety with their battery logger. They have the most powerful jaws in the competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team came out with a bang... bang... and wowed judges by reducing 200 brownouts per match to zero. The judges loved seeing the software behind the vision and odometry in github, line by line code and comparative graphs on different "shooting-on-the-move" algorithms. They left the choreo behind to focus on improv!

This team demonstrated exceptional consistency and precision in autonomous operation match after match. They earned this award through reliable multi-path routines, consistent two cycles of shooting, and adapt to changing circumstances on the field. When the red crowd is watching a shocking autonomous performance of 6 to 70 balls, you know the team name. It is...

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team demonstrates a powerful brand energy. Their colors and mascot energize their whole program, from their bright blue shirts, to green intake rollers, and even features their mascot's face on their robot's launcher. These "sparky"-ologists have unearthed an outstanding team identity

This team’s journey is defined by a commitment to transforming their community, continuously paving the road for a better future through their unwavering dedication to STEM. By starting and supporting many FIRST teams over the past three years, they have built a sustainable network that fuels the passions of young innovators. This team’s influence creates a rumbling momentum through a cycle of advocacy and leadership that strengthens the entire FIRST community which truly changed the regional culture. They have laid their own camo brick road, easing the path for others to follow. Their impact continues to grow until the thunder is heard by all, please join us in celebrating Team 1511, Rolling Thunder

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team can't help but make sure all can compete. Creating lesson plans for all in any language you need. Their pulse can be felt no matter how far you may be.
This team strikes balance with their compact design. 700 degrees lifts them from the competition. These circuits do take flight.

This team, despite their sharp corners, are very well rounded. They keep everything spinning between their unique indexer and being a pillar for FIRST in their region. If you find yourself talking to this team, don’t be surprised if they RAID all your time.

When you and your friends want to have a student run team, you will want to talk to this team's members, This team's members even sought out a mentor to help start their team. Just be prepared to buy a plane ticket to work with team face-to-face.
No matter who you talk to, this team is sure to make you enthusiastic. Their creative juices flow at dinner time, like soda through a straw. They “Live, Laugh,Love” FIRST

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has developed a comprehensive, year-round approach to sustainability. Despite being just thirty members strong, their outreach programs reach millions of people in a major second-city market. While their well-organized pipeline of programs ensures a steady flow of students progressing through the grades and into FRC.
This team can be heard cheering non-stop. With frills and lights, they are not only recognized here but also in their community. They’re loud, they’re proud, they’re conspicuously pink

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Design is the word of the day. Their requirements paved the whole way. 4 sixty degrees makes shooting a breeze And their process is on display.

This team is a shining beacon of Core Values, but a true champion for Inclusion. Where a gap in robotics education existed, they saw the opening and took the SHOT This all lead to a totally UNIFIED team that incudes people of different abilities and of different minds

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Winning the creativity award is a massive achievement for this team. Your ability to think outside the box allowed you to climb over every technical hurdle with an original ingenious approach. This victory is as sweet as honey, reflecting all the hard work and passion these cats poured into their robot.
Limerick: A robot built strong in two halves Each System aligned on their paths They tune every part Like a well-practiced art Blue and Yellow cast magic with staffs

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: These competitors had their horns at the READY and a torrent aimed and STEADY Haptic feedback gave them a symbiotic approach with man and machine that got it done. Their bot was built with changing parameters ready to run and gun!
This team's autonomous routine was robust and reliable. They consistently make two trips into the neutral zone to collect and launch fuel. They always know the RANGE to target.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is made of adventurous cats. Their theme this season belongs in a museum. For this team, X marks the spot.

From school board meetings to the halls of Congress and classrooms in Guatemala, this team is a powerhouse of STEM advocacy and global citizenship! Whether presenting engineering in Spanish or mentoring the next generation of innovators, they are truly forging a future where every student has a seat at the table! Exhibiting FIRST Core Values that are truly O-Mazing, and O-So-Wonderful throughout.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has built a powerful pipeline into STEM, starting with their youngest learners and continuing through sustained mentorship, hands-on programs, and global partnerships From launching and mentoring elementary robotics teams to developing curriculum with educators and supporting international programs that reach competition-level success, their impact is SO deep and far-reaching. They don’t just build robots, they Shift Outlooks, Spark Optimism, and Shape Opportunities.

Emerging from the pits is a machine that commands attention before it even takes a bite. With sleek lines, exceptional craftsmanship, and a design where every detail feels purposeful. This team's design is a powerful presence born from the sea but winning on the field.

Faced with numerous challenges, this team never stopped chugging forward. Blasting through barriers of language, finance and resources, they cannot be held back. Like the imspirational children's story, this group exemplifies the "Little Train That Could"

From the Northern region of their island, this team is reaching for the stars. Pushing beyond limited resources with determination and purpose, each achievement has only fueled their momentum. Victory is celebrated one pizza party at a time.

Persisting through significant challenges, this team has shown remarkable resilience. Charging out of the past they are now rebuilding their program from the ground up. This team didn’t just survive the fight, they’re back, and they’re ready to bark.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is sounding the alarm—making more than robots, they’re building a future fueled by opportunity. With a structured STEM pipeline to open doors for the next generation of innovators, they don’t just talk—they take action; recycling and reusing parts they reduce waste while maximizing their impact. They answer the call for innovation, outreach, and environmental responsibility.

This team is impossible to miss ! Lighting up the field in neon green with unmatched energy and contagious enthusiasm, their spirit goes beyond appearance. Whether on the field, in the pits or in the stands,this team doesn’t just compete… they Drift.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team designed systems for success with plenty of spares on hand. Documenting every step of the way supports their excellence. Spinning better and better and better, they continue to shoot for the stars.

This team fully embraces the FIRST cores values on and off the field. With a JV team designed for inclusivity and outreach that extends a half a world away. Teamwork keeps them volunteering and supporting participants through the entire FIRST ecosystem.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When this bot is on the field, it is sure to stir up a storm. Even without a hopper, they can keep a steady stream of fuel flowing. This team can certainly "Keep Calm and Unwind" knowing that their design is unique and effective!

This robotics competition has seen a lot of robots go down. To make it, takes a machine that is robust, effective and can meet any challenge. This team built an impenetrable fortress and is not afraid when things go South.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Seeing the field through a new lens, this design brings vision and precision into perfect focus. By integrating a unique control system this team achieves positional accuracy and shooting success. Shaking the competition to a new reality…with virtual reality.
This teams autonomous routine dominated the competition. Masterfully shooting with speed and precision. For 20 seconds no one ROARED louder.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This feathered team shows the importanc of FIRST core values. They built a nest in the FIRST community and welcome others to their flock. From seed to spark and flame to flight, this team displays their commitment, pride and success everywhere.

This team relentlessly drives their efforts to spread the mission of FIRST near and far. They PAY it forward by providing STEM access to students in disadvantaged regions with initial training, continued mentoring, and an underlying goal of self-replicating sustainability. By building ecosystems on seven symbolic pillars, this team honors the history of its mascot by looking towards the future and courageously advancing STEM opportunities and the mission of FIRST in some of the most challenging regions on earth.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: A commitment to science and technology is at the core of this team’s culture. By promoting STEM in every corner of their school, running an off-season competition, and raising funds for children fighting pediatric cancer, this team is truly golden. Whether it’s kimchi or Koshar on a Friday night, this team soars to new heights.

All the teams here faced constraints in their robot design: size… weight… time. But then again, most of the teams here didn’t need to fit their robot into 4 pieces of checked luggage. This high performing machine wow’d the judges with its clean design, beautiful machining, and "high volume" scoring. After visiting one of New York’s most notable landmarks, this team aptly named their robot that “scores like a waterfall" Niagara.

This team dives into their community and its youth by demonstrating their robot at the local Museum, engaging home schoolers into their team, and providing mobility for those in need. The team demonstrated learning from other teams by using advanced materials to improve their performance. They also showed falcon-like focus on fun and developing a team for the future.

Every rookie experience is unique… that said, some may be more unique than others: Most rookie teams don’t document their entire season or host the most viewed build blog in their country. Most rookie teams didn’t need to redesign and rebuild their entire robot just so they could come here and share their story. For their local impact, their team spirit, and the way they repeatedly demonstrate a passion for FIRST in the face of adversity, they are Rookie All Stars!.

This bright new star has already built a strong foundation to inspire future engineers. They create artifacts to help children, the visually impaired, the elderly, and animals. They are one team, with one heart and big dreams.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Primary colors don’t just start the picture—they make it possible. This team has painted a self-portrait of a future bursting with potential. Their wild red palette isn’t just on display—it’s ready to leave its mark on the whole gallery.

The spirit of FIRST is alive and well in this team. Whether it’s lending a hand in the pits, teaching coding in the community, or bringing STEM kits to elementary school students, this team sparkles with enthusiasm. At home and away, this herd proves that you really can ‘catch ‘em all’.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team dominated the field, intaking heaps of fuel effortlessly and depositing it with pinpoint accuracy. They grew together and “SPROUT”-ed an elegant and uniquely engineered carwash-inspired design. Though they may be from Queens, they’re undoubtedly the Kings of Engineering Excellence!

When teams are sidelined by broken components, they stop by the pit of this opponent. Our winners didn’t wait to be asked, their printing service was widely broadcast. In a game that can be chaotic, they helped other teams from going psycho!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: How do you get out of a jam? Just don't get stuck! This team's clever mechanism allows them to capture fuel and always be on the go. They don't worry about getting stuffed due to their passive overflow.

This team’s robot design and build processes Screamed quality and had the judges SINGING their praises. The team analyzed failure modes from previous competitions to ensure their robot had the quality to stand up to this weekend’s competitors. OHHHH-my did it work!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: In a well choreographed dance, this team’s robot lights the way to locate game pieces. With a few button pushes they IGNITE and control innovation.

This team autonomously cruised around the field and was able to easily navigate all obstacles. They “upgraded their ride” to increase the amount of fuel they could carry. We are here to give them their autonomous crown!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s visuals extend as far as the eye can SEA. Their theme unites their school and sponsors with a love of the ocean and the sky. Otto the Octopus really makes a splash!

records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team
records.script: Like blue skies, this team’s blue shirts can inspire one to reach for great heights. This team’s impact reached far beyond their own state’s, and even own country’s, borders. Their commitment to expanding the accessibility of technology to those who need it exemplified the values of First. Their creativity is displayed not only in their robotic designs, but in their medical innovations for those in need. This team really uses their BRAIN to support STEM. Congratulations to team 8393, The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team!

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: By placing STEM at the heart of their mission, this team achieved a staggering reach of 55,000 people over 30 diverse events and media. Their strategic outreach and infectious passion left a mark on their community that even a ROGUE FLUKE couldn't slow them down. They proved they had NO DIFFICULTIES, inspiring judges with their commitment to the FIRST mission. Congratulations, Team number 4085, Technical Difficulties

This team was in attack mode from start to finish. Many nights were spent prototyping and optimizing their turret to make it the “Top Gun” on the field. The entire machine fused efficiency with practicality into an industrial design that was as bold as a WILD ANIMAL on the great plains! Congratulations, Team number 2252 The Mavericks

This team isn’t in a HURRY, they’ve already arrived. They show up to help in person or virtually anytime or anywhere. Keep up the great work sharing lessons learned from sustained performance over 30 years. Congratulations, Team number 27, Rush

Over half of their team graduated last year, but they didn’t just grin and BEAR it. They began a summer camp and FTC team to teach STEM to CUBS. They avoided a grizzly extinction, doubled their team size, and are BEAR-elling towards the future. Congratulations, Team number 6964 BearBots

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has built a model of sustainability that ensures long-term impact through planning and strong leadership. By using their equipment to CRAFT items that fund their team, they are WALKING towards the future, with technology leading the way. This team RAMMED their way to success from the other side of the state! Congratulations, Team number 3201 Ross Rambotics

The judges were inspired that this team defined themselves by their UNITY and perseverance. The bring enthusiasm and pride to all their initiatives, from their partnership with a local hospital, to their incorporation of all their team members’ ideas. They are a model of how a team can REBUILD, even when BAD things happen. Congratulations, Team number 1014 Bad Robots

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team wowed the judges with the ABCs of their design and development, resulting in a simple yet highly effective robot. Unlike a shy and elusive mythical creature, the results of this team’s iterative and flexible design process resulted in a robot that won’t be missed. The judges felt that this team MUST, SHOULD, and COULD be recognized for their achievement. Congratulations, Team number 2399 The Fighting Unicorns

This team makes sure no one in the HERD gets left behind. Their scouting data doesn’t just be-HOOVE them, they share it with other teams. Like BISON roaming the plains, their scouts sweep the field and send help to struggling robots. Congratulations, Team number 695 Bison Robotics!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Sometimes you need to REBUILD old solutions to solve new problems. When the PRESSURE is on, they expanded to maximize fuel collection, while making WAVES to never get in a JAM. Meteors are not the only thing to shoot through the air this week! Congratulations, Team number 5413 Stellar Robotics

Building the robot is only part of their success and the judges recognize them as a quality example to others. This team has kept their competition sturdy and clean with a robot that has OODLES of personality and robust quality. When it comes to building a robot that avoids all obstacles in their path, these competitors are CLOUDS above the rest. Congratulations, Team number 4611 Ozone

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team pursued an intense journey to find new ways of navigation. They always know where to go, even when FLYING through the air. Scoring in Rebuilt is never VIRTUAL, even when their robot Parmesan is wearing GOGGLES. Congratulations, Team number 1507, Warlocks

This team took early command of the BATTLEFIELDS neutral zone during the auto period. They distinguished themselves with their automatic targeting and shooting- even while ON THE MOVE! Their calculation velocity makes them WORthy of this award! Congratulations, Team number 4145 The Worbots

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The winner of this award has mastered the skill of rebuilding the ANCIENT PAST, transforming every part of their team. This team has an impressive array of RELICS from FRC history, adding to the HALL OF LEGACY with their dusty, weathered robot and their team info cards. Soaring above the competition by creating their own ANCIENT TEMPLE of impact. Congratulations, Team number 3193 FalcoTech!

This team’s passion for spreading the FIRST mission through establishing FIRST programs & volunteering is no MYTH. They galloped through the process of expanding the STEM curriculum with their school. No barrier can contain these MYSTICAL creatures. Congratulations, Team Number 2399: The Fighting Unicorns

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team is known for turning hardships into a POT of GOLD! They promote respect and appreciation for engineering within their school and community, and even got the Board ON BOARD. This team is really GOOD – not BAD – at collaborating! Congratulations, Team number 1014 Bad Robots

This team was ABOVE AND BEYOND able to talk their design and maintenance plan with the judges. A very high percentage of their bot parts are fabricated IN-HOUSE. Their turret’s cable chain made the judges hearts FLY HIGH. Congratulations, Team number 1787 The Flying Circuits

This TRUSTY STEED stands out from the herd. Leading the CHARGE in a much-needed conversation, this team has become a hub for the community to receive support for and discuss mental health. We thank this team for being at the forefront of a long overdue subject and making a bold statement for change. Congratulations, Team number 2252 The Mavericks

In the Bluegrass State, this team’s impact is already becoming legendary. They’ve MARCHED through the season recruiting partners to join their growing ranks. Spartacus leads the way with a unified FORCE that cannot be conquered. The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to: 10987 The Legion

This team became a community-based team after losing their support structure, and are now working across the state to protect the future of other FIRST teams. Bursting out of their coach’s basement, this team is taking advantage of an opportunity to start anew. Fresh out of the oven, this team is coming FULL CIRCLE. Congratulations, Team number 3814 Pi-Botics

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This community-based team demonstrates sustainability by turning compassion into action, spreading HOPE all around. This team empowers the next generation by hosting FLL summer camps and TRY-IT DAYS at their STEM center. They inspire their local community through efforts such as planting initiatives and a clothing drive. Tie-dye preferred, but not required. Congratulations, Team number 1038 Lakota Robotics

This team purrs with the spirit of FIRST through their outreach and team communication. They attack their community, support for fellow students, and competitors with obvious enthusiasm. Their cat spirit is part of their team and apparent in everything they do! Congratulations, Team number 451 Cat Attack Robotics

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The energy around this team simply BUZZES with excitement. They impressed the judges with intentionality around design choices, including both positives and NEGATIVES OF ALL of the features. The sting of challenges didn’t STICK with this team as they had planned for future improvement, sometimes made overnight. Congratulations, Team number 2603 Steel Stingers

This interplanetary team takes the initiative to offer help to others in need. This team, which comes from a place of rich heritage, is mentioned regularly by other teams as being truly joyful in their graciousness. This team focuses on one thing each season, but unlike their namesake their focus unifies the team instead of creating war. Congratulations, Team number 2614 Mountaineer Area Robotics MARS

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team prioritized this unique feature over other subsystems, keeping other teams on their PAWS. They calculated gear ratios like the great GREEK mathematicians. This robot FLIPS the competition on their heads. Congratulations, Team number 2228 Cougar Tech

This team knows where they are in this competition with home-made precision programming. Their 3D printing skills, modular design, and maintenance thinking is NO SECRET. Using simulation to determine variable sensitivity make their quality A SURE SHOT. Congratulations, Team number 5811, The Bonds

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With sharp vision, this team’s robot directs and clears the way, always facing forward. It swerves across the field, hungry for yellow dots, eyes locked on the goal. Like Pac-Man, it clears obstacles, devouring every challenge in its path. Congratulations, Team number 695 Bison Robotics

This team did not take any SHORTCUTS when addressing the challenges with time-based pathfinding. Their machine uses 3 cameras to maintain robot POSE to KEY IN their sequence shooter and one-button lock-on. They improved consistency in autonomous by UNDOING jamming issues with their hopper feed. Congratulations, Team number 4096 Ctrl-Z

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s culture is one where they BUILD each other up. Through their mascot, pit area, and robot, this team’s COLORS RUN DEEP. When it comes to BRANDING, this team is a TRUE GEM Congratulations, Team number 10011 Gridrunners

Addressing root causes is a passion of this team. Their years of effort led to enduring funding for future teams statewide, and STEM kits for military brats nationally. These cats show how to make an impact that lasts an entire nine lives.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: The surprise of this award might make this team fall over dead. Their STEM outreach is exemplary. One might even say it’s Museum Quality.
This team rolled in with a robot bold and supreme! Junior warriors built this machine with power and a SCREAM!
Although nothing rhymes with the color purple, the Judges hear the crowing call of this team as they DOMINATE the principles of FIRST.

This team has really turned up the heat and proven that they aren’t just winging it. By spreading the spirit of FIRST through incredible outreach, they have shown that their commitment to the community is truly enlightening. After a blazing start to their journey, it’s clear this team is destined to keep soaring as they rise from the ashes.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This community team brings five high schools together under one roof. They may be spread out, but they still impressed the Judges with their pipeline. Despite how it sounds, you won’t find them on the Value Menu.

This team is obviously enthusiastic about their team, showing off their contagious spirit. The students on this team ignite enthusiasm throughout the surrounding community with STEM related camps and workshops. The fire spreads wherever the serape lands.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: On the field or with their home state, this team excels in showcasing key principles for engineering. When you are born to be wild, who you gonna call?

These competitors have mastered the art of stealthy support by slicing through technical troubles whenever a neighbor is in need. Through their Assist Program, they have kicked it up a notch by constantly helping others in the pits and proving that teamwork is their greatest weapon. With a black belt in sportsmanship and a heart for service, these Ninjas are truly a cut above the rest.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has creatively integrated all the features of their robot into a cohesive package. From their shooter to their hopper on the field, their success shows that this robot is no ordinary rabbit. The Creativity award goes to the Holders of the Holy Hand-grenade!

You don’t need a particle accelerator to open up this bot. This team impressed us with their focus on ease of repair with their expertly designed collection of components, allowing them to focus on ease of repair. Let’s pop open the hood and take a look!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team stands out for their consistent accuracy and smooth control operation. They were as powerful as an 80’s rock ballad, and as slick as a blues riff, scoring fuel like a sweet melody. They deserve a Grammy for their performance at this competition.

Scoring 2 tanks of fuel and filling up for a 3rd pushed this robot to the top before firing it off in a streak of yellow into the hub. The judges found that teams consistently SCREAMED to be paired up with them during the event.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s flashy style make them standout on the field. Their robot’s STRIKING color scheme cannot be missed. They matched everything down to the last golden ziptie.

This team wants to be seen for everything they do in FIRST. When they are not traveling the length and breadth of the state, people visit them in their 'shop in passels. They are not lying down afraid; instead they are daily making an IMPACT.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team's robot stands above the rest as a large mass of stone, a mountain; a strong, sturdy, force to be reckoned with on the field. This team embodies the spirit of FIRST with their design, team focus, and processes like a well in the desert. This team shines brightly like a star, set lit in order so that they may find their own. El tiempo que perdiste por tu rosa!

This team's robot tears through the traffic of competition with an elegant, efficient and practical design. All the components of this team's robot are worthy of this recognition. Traveling the highway of form, function and aesthetics, they are a clean, clear and competent classic team!

This team buzzes above the rest. They pierce everyone, including the judges, with their stinger of gracious professionalism. Congrats to the team that made it from the land of 10,000 ER's and 1,000,000 mosquitos to Tulsa, OK.
This team has a bright future ahead. They started in a garage, and still managed to set up for their future years. They're BOLTING forward so fast, you might clock them at 140Hz.
This team has come far in a short amount of time. Their reach has been broader than their travel. They've reached for the stars, and become rockstars!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: It's important to create systems that keep teams thriving, which is not a challenge for this group...they won't burn out! As the most abundant matter in the universe, they spread their outreach to recruit new members and provide their existing ones with life skills to sustain their future.
This team is jacketed with the prestige of an energetic spirit. Compassion, leadership, teamwork and friendship define them to the core. A TIGER of a team, watch out for the energy of their BYTES!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: Engineering principles COMMAND this team's approach to organization and design. They utilize CAD to design modular subsystems and clean wiring plans to make HISSSSSSSSTORICALLY effective gameplay. This team's overall execution puts them into position to strike like a COBRA.

This team has been heavily involved with their FTC teams around the clock. They opened the doors to their shop to multiple international teams when it was needed. You don't have to look TOE-FAR to find this team.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: These competitors have traveled far to be here. Their robot is a creative example on never giving up. This team believes in themselves and flourishes in the shade.
Even when taking a hit, the quality of this team's bot shines through with its black & gold parts, all they way down to the golden zip ties neatly holding everything in place.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The judges net has pulled in this catch, which is tough because the controls keep their robot from being caught. These fish could make it all the way to the moon.
Back and forth, to a fro. Even with no one at the helm, these ducks automatically know where they go!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In the stands you'll spot a rowdy crowd, with hats as shiny as their robot. When these competitors gallop into play, they can't be mistaken. If you free them from their corral, they'll show you what they're made of. Let's give a bit YEEHAW to OmegaFactor!

Not limited by their geographic location, this team took every opportunity to spread FIRST’s mission across their close-knit community. This year, they’ve expanded their reach by developing a STEM network supported by a unique funding model and newly introduced grants, ensuring sustainability. Their initiatives, partnerships, and outreach activities locally and abroad could fill a book. For the judges, this team exemplified the essence of FIRST, its mission, and STEM. They have been some very Busy Bees!

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team’s STEM outreach represents Canada on the world stage with their themed robots. The judges were impressed with the team’s commitment to build outreach robots using FRC parts, culminating in their most ambitious robot, a hockey goalie. This team might “Banter” but we look forward to their next robot to join Goalia.

The robot stood out with a strategic and elegant design, demonstrating effective performance on the field. The team has used a robust engineering process and has built a high quality machine that includes a smart, clever shooting mechanism. Like a perfect stream, Team Laminar glides on top for Industrial Design.

This team leads with confidence and conviction—championing girls in STEM and setting a bold example for what’s possible. They embed FIRST values into their everyday school culture, applying FIRST Robotics practices and applications into their school curriculum and actively inspire young women across their community and around the world to step into STEM with strength and ambition. This team is creating the next generation of STEM role models. Let’s Go Girls!

From the shadows, a young team shines bright — lighting their path like explorers uncovering something extraordinary. They REBUILT after half their team graduated, recharged, and surged forward with relentless energy—recruiting new talent, refining their machine, and proving that grit and passion power true progress. With neon glow and unstoppable momentum, this second-year team rises again.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team engineered a flawless knowledge pipeline building process that empowers the next generation across FTC, FRC and the wider STEM field. Driven by their EDIT labs and DARTS organizational structure, they ensure long term continuity by educating younger students and providing unparalleled machine shop and mentorship support to the teams from the Northern Region. Securing the future of STEM, one student at a time.

From centre stage to centre field, this team connects their love of art, STEM and the FIRST experience. These robo-performers show off their creativity by wearing their spirit on their sleeves. Doubters aside, they stand like Titans at every competition.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team demonstrated a thorough engineering design process. The judges were impressed by their systematic plans & end-to-end flow charts, which translated into an effective robot on the field of play. They stayed cool under pressure, freezing out the competition – just like an ice cube.

The judges were amazed at the depth and breadth of this team’s outreach initiatives. With an abundance of intelligence, creativity, and empathy, the winning team introduced STEM to members of their community with special needs. When it comes to being a force for promoting STEM, these CATS are WIRED!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Even with a budget that barely covered snacks, they rolled in with a “glass half full” attitude… and probably a half tank of gas. No sponsors? No problem. Since they had few spares, their creatively designed “custom” dashboard was coded to prevent their motors from burning out in the heat of competition. Surrounded by roaring Harleys and polished Hondas… in putters a Vespa saying “alright y’all, let’s see what you got”

Their all-rounded robot snuggles multiple balls smoothly with their white silicone rollers, distributes them evenly with a spiral design, and then rains the balls into the hoop in a flawless cascade. Their robust design creatively includes Bounce sheets to protect their circuitry from electrostatic discharge, and this team "shuts down” all active opponents.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team was on a quest to prove they have the metal to win. By cleverly using sensors to calibrate the swivel and spin in tandem, their turret launched a relentless volley where every shot hit its mark. For a performance that was truly hoot worthy, put your talons together.

This team has been scoring a flurry of points during the autonomous mode. They’ve planned and employed a smart route, and mixed various sensor data well to keep the robot on track. A storm on the field, Blizzard takes the Autonomous Award.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This community-based team proves that an outstanding visual aesthetic can unite students no matter how far apart they are. Bringing together more than 10 schools and several school boards under one colourful banner, they flawlessly combine a unified style guide with a sheep Mascot that takes safety seriously. Setting the standard for community branding, and painting the competition purple, Congratulations to Team 2706!

This team really sank their TEETH into making an impact on more than just the FIRST community. They made sure that everyone felt included and were provided with a safe space to participate in STEM. They are a hub of support for many FIRST teams with reach spanning the globe. The breadth of their recycling program shows that they're not HORSING around. This team has perfected the formula for making the competition better so that everyone can participate. When asked 'WHO,' this team made sure no one was left behind.

This team GOES THE DISTANCE to spread impact to their entire community. By hosting decentralized workshops, they have enabled equal access to education, reducing barriers and promoting equity. They created a supply chain of FIRST teams, forging connections to reduce material costs for rural teams. They have worked to build a technology HIVE in a remote region, generating a lot of BUZZ about STEM. Defying all known laws of aviation, this team went BEE-yond all others.

records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team truly ESCAPES the mundane. They effectively PULL new members into their team and have LAUNCHED many initiatives in their community. Where others go round in CIRCLES, they have LANDED on a winning strategy.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team is a SHINING example of starting off with a BANG. They have brought a BLAST of energy to their first season that can already be felt across the globe. They demonstrate that even a rookie team can LIGHT UP THE NIGHT.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: Science experiments dictate that gases rise. This robot has gone through some serious iterations, and has a distinctive look, built from simple components and materials. Clean design decisions makes it a strong contender. This team aspires to rise to the top.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: With a fiery passion for data, this team charged onto the field. Their youngest locked heads to envelope a code to analyze their opponents and fuel their strategy. This team is always ready to bring the heat.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team has earned its stripes not once, but twice. Despite an extended hiatus, a small but mighty streak restored a strong foundation and continues to inspire young cubs. This team is roaring with pride and truly rose to the occasion.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Building a lasting program requires laying an unshakable foundation for the next generation. Functioning as a perfectly structured organization, this team engineered a knowledge pipeline that acts as a powerful catalyst. They effortlessly transition younger students into FLL, FTC, FRC and the wider STEM universe, all while extending vital machine shop support across the north. Securing the future of stem, one student at a time.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team stood out with a unique colour. They’re young, exciting and bring joy to the field of play and to their community. The kitchen staff keep trying to kidnap their mascot to clean up.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team inspires and elevates the level of the game. Their robot is an example of simplicity in engineering. Do not be deceived as on the field it is a master of competitions. Anyone playing against this team will be up the creek.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: It’s no mystery why this team was chosen. Rather than holding their resources and knowledge close to their chest, they asked one question, How can we help? This team competes hard and helps harder. It is agreed there is no contradiction.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s unique mechanism Attracted the Judges from the start. They identified and designed a creative approach to scoring Rarely claimed points. By Sticking to their concept, this robot climbs above the competition

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This robot sure looked real to the judges. The design seems simple but, like Canada’s Coffee Shop, it delivers time and again, no matter how tough the competition. This team made the most of their home field advantage.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This green machine sure can score. Performing better than Limelight, their custom camera solution became "SENTRAL" to shooting consistently and reliably anywhere on the field. Their shots are definitely better than THAT green basketball team.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team approaches each match with crisp efficiency. They give their drivers a break, and fast reconfiguration makes the auto a breeze. Having ironed out all the measurement errors their robot performance is sweet.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team prepared the field for our competition. They celebrate and engage their members by representing their community through cultural understanding. This team uses hand painted imagery and artwork to reflect their heritage.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team’s double-turret design is well laid out and squeaky clean. Everything is essential on their bot, including agitating the balls like a washing machine. They optimized space for agility, from their wire handling down to the PANTS.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: By joining this team, you will have minstrels singing your praises. This team is building bridges over moats that connect members to future employers. These bold knights are preparing students to come to the employers’ round table.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team is still young, but fierce in its enthusiasm for FIRST. Even as they prowl to find rare sponsors, everyone is welcome to join and grow their robotics summer camp. Cette équipe est souple, agile, et ira loin, comme leur mascotte, la panthère noire!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has been turning everyone’s trash into their treasure chest. They’ve recycled their way through cardboard prototypes, and created an explosive STEM impact in their small town community. They are absolutely dynamite when it comes to making the planet and their community better.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: Despite facing setbacks, this team’s voice remains loud and proud. This team uses their contagiously positive energy in ratcheting up enthusiasm in others and their robots. This favorite manufacturing tool is never lacking in good cheer.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team went aROUND the design cycle of engineering with an unusual solution to this year’s challenge. Their robot eats fuel like a hungry hippo and seamlessly spins the balls into the hopper with little effort. From the depth of Madagascar, the features of their robot all work together in harmony.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team plants the seeds for other teams to grow by lending others their knowledge and wisdom. They help foster a thriving robotics rhizosphere. This team deserves the Oscar in Gracious Professionalism.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team made others green with envy with their robot climbing ability. They created a ducky solution for integrating an efficient and reliable climb mechanism into their autonomous and end-game strategies. By refusing to back down from the challenge, this team showed they had the strength to topple their climbing Goliath.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
