records.script: Témoin de l’harmonie entre la technologie et la nature, ils ont su intégrer le thème de cette année à leur équipe. Leur décor représente l’évolution sous plusieurs formes. Ce loup alpha a conquis les terrains techniques et esthétiques de la robotique.

Access to STEM education is not always equitable or affordable, yet this team proves that FIRST means STEM for everyone. They design inclusive learning experiences that ensure innovation is accessible to all learners, regardless of ability. By hosting STEM events in local libraries, they transform familiar spaces into hubs where curiosity and engineering thrive. Leveraging accessible technology and web-based tools, they remove barriers while building confidence in the next generation. As they reach for the top of the stacks, they lift their entire community with them, creating lasting pathways into STEM. This team is truly humble, heroic, honorable, and here to make a lasting impact on the world.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has brought stem to students of all ages. They gently rammed their stem initiatives into multiple schools. and They managed to do this without butting heads.

This team has command and control to override every control. Their robot moves with precision and power, sending their fuel flying into the hub. With an elegant design, this team had hammered their way to the top.

The judges adamantly agree that this team has achieved greatness and made positive impacts on and off the field. From "Women in STEM" to "Men in HEALS" this team has many unique programs to spread their message and support others. Threading a course through the canals, they ferry towards top-tier destinations.

This grass roots team is small in numbers but large in enthusiastic spirit. In their short existence, with a limited budget, they've managed to strategize, design, and build their robot to attack the game's challenges. Their team members have utilized student driven CAD as part of their design process. This 3 mentor and 5 student team have exhibited a great beginning and we're sure to see them on the "seas" for years to come.
This team hatched not not too long ago. They are still growing, but already are flying high. For Rising All Star, this team takes the crown.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Whether it be from businesses or beaches, this team ensure no scrap is put to waste. With this team's sustainable practices they were able to field a 'jumbo" robot. We feel confident that this scrapy team is on the path for continued success.

This team demonstrates why sowing the seeds of team spirit is so important. From carrying on tradition through their robot's aesthetic to resurrecting old traditions forgotten to time, they will not back down letting you know who they are. While their opening pitch is impressive, they continue to reap the spirit of competition.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team continues to rain success rain success from above. Their robust engineering solutions allowed them to persistently overcome obstacles at terminal velocity. Their detailed design process is why this soaring competitor earned this award.

This team exhibits Gracious Professionalism both at events and throughout the year. Demonstrated through volunteering at events, teaming up for beach cleanup, assisting rookies, hosting an impact exchange, and even providing a kitbot to a team in need, their GP may "cure the blues" at their public co-hosted full practice field. While printing parts for other teams, the "devil" is in the details.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Hailing from Vacationland, this team's creative design has set them apart on the field. Their machined roller can shoot 4 balls at once, proving both unique and effective. As their name implies, this team thinks outside the box and stands apart.

This team had the most robust "cat" in the game. This solid robot could always land on its feet despite the challenges of match play. This team spent weeks "Bacon" up a quality machine, that had even "Stacy" and "Carl" beat.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team integrates control systems internally between robot subsystems and also dynamically with their strategy. With eyes looking both forward and back, they can repeatedly traverse the trench and score tons of fuel. Their control system aint just for "show-bro".

In a field where precision meets intelligence, one team's machine moved with the confidence of an Egyptian god. This team's consistently flawless pathing, rapid and accurate decision making, and level of sensor integration allow their robot to adapt in real time and dominate during both autonomous and teleop modes. This team demonstrated their success whether lone or with their alliance pack.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team branched out to become recognizable from a distance. They change flavors every year, and this year's flavor added layers to their brand. "Tim-Brrr' these pups are cool!

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: Some teams inspire with a single moment—but this team builds inspiration like a rising tide. Their programs reach students across the entire K–12 journey, ensuring that basic needs are met first so that learning can truly take root—because “a child is not going to learn if they’re hungry.” Their impact is backed by thoughtful documentation, meaningful statistics, and initiatives like providing sensory stimulation that support student success at every level. From the first drops of rain to the powerful winds of a thunderstorm, this team remains focused, driven, and firmly in the eye of the hurricane of inspiration.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Most teams come here to generate some buzz — but this team has been building a charge long before they ever touched this field. And we're not just talking about robots. They've been conducting energy into the corners of their community that others forget to wire up — bringing STEAM education to students in special education programs who too often get left off the circuit entirely. That current doesn't stop here. They built a foundation, and they've been transmitting that signal outward ever since. Because for this team, that's always been the point. Their motto says it all — "Take the message farther."

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: Some robots move fast—but the best ones move with intention. This team’s design featured an extended hopper that increased fuel capacity while maintaining structural balance, paired with autonomous routines that showed thoughtful coordination between hardware and software. Their ability to machine their own components demonstrated craftsmanship and ownership of their engineering process. Like a patient viper waiting for the perfect moment, this team delivers precision every time Snake Eyes takes the field.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: Some teams build robots—but this team builds momentum. Their conversations with judges showed a program that is always evolving, constantly finding new ways to improve through creativity, persistence, and teamwork. Their thoughtful discussion and maturity made the judging experience feel like a conversation among equals, demonstrating the depth of their understanding and commitment to growth. With ideas that keep expanding and a team culture that never stands still, this program proves that the best teams are always getting better.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: For exemplifying the spirit of a "FIRST Impact Award team in the making," they have shown they truly understand that technical challenges offer a bright future. This new crew has emerged from the depths and is already circling the top of the leaderboard. They have taken a massive BYTE out of the competition by building a robot that tackles every game challenge while forming a powerful partnership between their school and sponsors.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: From the frozen strength of polar bears to the rugged resilience of the grizzly, bears have long symbolized power, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in changing environments. This team has shown that same spirit - learning quickly, growing boldly, and not quitting! They are rebuilding their program and its future to stand out in black and white, just like the bear that represents them, bridging strength with curiosity and charm.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has built a sustainment plan so strong, it doesn’t just hold water — it channels it into a future proof pipeline of student leaders. Their long-term strategy keeps new members flowing in like a renewable energy source, ensuring their program never runs dry. This team "surges" to the front, regardless of the storm.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: From their vibrant presence in the pits to their unwavering support for every competitor on the field, this group defines what it means to be a unified force. Their enthusiasm is deeply rooted in their school, their community, and every partnership they build. They have proven that a high-performing robot is even more powerful when backed by a team with heart. This team has shown true team spirit where their bark is just as impressive as their bite.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team impressed the judges not just with their performance on the field, but with the meticulous documentation of their journey. From their first design ideas to their integrated chassis architecture, every bolt and line of code had a clear purpose. They showed us that true excellence comes from iteration. For a machine that has literally been unearthed and a team that has truly risen from the fire.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: In every handshake, every helping hand, and every hard-fought match, this team showed what true character looks like. They stepped in to help other teams troubleshoot issues — offering time, tools, and encouragement without hesitation. This team doesn't just spark success on the field… they ignite Gracious Professionalism everywhere they go.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When others followed the crowd, this team went their own way. This robot’s expandable hopper and dual-shooter system demonstrated a creative approach that balanced capacity, flexibility, and storing potential in a unique way. By embracing a design that breaks from tradition. These ideas don’t just cut through the challenge… they carve their own path.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: Some machines are flashy, but the best ones are simply built right. This team demonstrated exceptional craftsmanship with a robot designed for reliability and consistency throughout the competition. Their attention to build quality and disciplined engineering ensured their machine performed exactly as intended every time it took the field. From a garage built on old-school mechanical pride to a machine ready to roll, this crew proves that quality always stands the test of time.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When every movement matters, this team’s robot responds with precision and confidence. This team came down out of the mountains to compete this week. With camera controls and performance that feels effortless, they turned control into a competitive advantage. When it comes to controls, every connection counts.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.script: When the match begins and drivers step back, this team's robot steps forward, thinking fast, moving with purpose, and proving that preparation meets precision in those critical first seconds. With a consistent, routine their autonomous mode sets the tone every time. This robot gives a G3 performance that's truly Great, Gritty and Game-changing.

records.eventName: FSC District North Charleston Event presented by SCDE & City of North Charleston Recreation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some teams build robots—but this team builds an identity that people recognize. Through thoughtful branding and dedicated public relations work, they refreshed their image within their school and local community, strengthening their presence while promoting the mission of FIRST. With warriors at heart and circuits running strong, this team proves that a powerful image can inspire an entire community.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: The Impact Award recognizes a team whose efforts create meaningful, lasting change—and this team has done exactly that by building a powerful legacy of STEM access in their rural community. They have inspired hundreds of students with coding workshops, launched new FIRST teams, and celebrated herds of young innovators. Their outreach extends far beyond classrooms, engaging thousands at public events and amplifying their message through widespread media coverage. By forging strong partnerships and advocating at the state level, they have secured significant funding to expand opportunities for future generations. Their vision for a Technology Center promises to elevate STEM education across the region for years to come. Clearly, when it comes to making an impact, this team didn’t just head west—they went Due West.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This award celebrates a team that has made a powerful impact in advancing respect and appreciation for engineering in their community as this team has done. Through outreach, mentorship, and a commitment to growing STEM opportunities, they have energized those around them and created a whirlwind far beyond their team. Charging forward and leaving a trail of inspiration in their wake, this team proves they are a storm you can’t ignore.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: The design of this robot impressed the judges with their efficient and elegant design. The team’s extensive use of prototypes culminated in a multi-shooter robot capable of outscoring their opponents. With their unique indexer design, this team was able to assault the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: This team truly understands what it means to give back to the community. Sowing their roots in both body in mind, they reap the rewards of their bounty. It’s a goodness that’s sure to even spread to the stars above. The winner of the “Keep on Jammin’ Award” is Team 9315.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: Despite getting a late start ahead of the season, these rookies came out strong with strong partnerships, dedicated mentors, and colorful branding. While they look to veteran teams as “father figures,” it is clear they are preparing to lead the pack.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: Despite the challenges faced by this team, they have risen high above it all. The judges were impressed by their spirit and drive and how they have incorporated the FIRST Core Values into their team’s culture. With their motto of “making it fun to make it last,” this team strikes like there is blood in the water.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In the world of competitive teamwork, technical skills are only half the battle. The true test of a team is their ability to build a foundation that lasts beyond their graduation with the community integration to become a local institution. Through financial self-reliance and unwavering commitment to their neighbors this “flash flood” has proven that they are a permanent force of nature.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: This team brings unmatched energy to every moment, showing up “always hyped” and ready to lift the spirit of everyone around them. Known for their bubbly personalities, love of pink, and unforgettable team moments—like showing up to a bowling outing in full costume (yes, even a chicken!)—they make every activity more fun. This group of young ladies spreads excitement while growing skills in themselves and others.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: By planning their game strategy in advance and focusing on a robot that could reliably collect fuel, move them smoothly through the intake, and shoot them accurately without interruption, this teams has designed a robot that consistently “makes magic” on the field.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: This team brings a spark of positivity wherever they go, always ready with a smile and a helping hand. You may have noticed their energy lighting up the pits, forming friendships across teams, and proudly wearing a name that shines—maybe even spelled out on their shirts. From their motto “building great robots by building great students” to their unforgettable robot Bottomless Potamus, please congratulate Team FLASH!

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed judges with a creative design that kept their eyes on their competitors. Using a unique pneumatic intake system in addition to a dual turret, this team was able to slither past the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a robot built on precision, durability, and attention to detail. Their robot’s reinforced steel intake and innovative vision system ensured they were able to speed past the competition. The robust design allowed the robot to spend less time in the garage.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Control is more than just movement—it’s about being accurate, focused, and consistent. With a name that points to perfect aim, this robot moves with steady precision, locking onto its targets like it doesn’t miss. Every movement is planned and smooth, showing a system built to follow, aim, and act without delay. The Innovation in Control Award goes to Team 281, the Green Villains, with their robot Dead Eye!

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.script: In the spirit of REBUILT™, some things may rest for a long time - but when they rise again, they move with purpose. When the match begins, this robot awakens with autonomous control that feels almost ancient - calm, calculated, and unstoppable in its path. Like something unearthed and restored to full strength, this robot shows control and reliability from the very first second. Wrapped in precision and built with focus, it shows strong and reliable performance every time.

records.eventName: FIRST South Carolina State Championship presented by Magna
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team presents a cohesive identity that is consistently carried across every detail, truly taking flight with their blue, black, and yellow branding. Their powerful symbol of resilience tells a clear and compelling story—one of overcoming challenges and continuously growing stronger. “Rising from the ashes,” this team brings their brand to life in every space they enter—please congratulate the team represented by the Phoenix!

You can measure a team’s impact by how they help others grow. By hosting events, starting new teams, and implementing STEM recognition in classrooms, they are working to promote inclusion, STEAM, and FIRST. Their advocacy on behalf of themselves and FIRST South Carolina is proof that “legacy is like a tree” and the seeds are planted even in the most rural parts of our state.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Engineering Inspiration celebrates a team that demonstrates an undeniable impact in their school, organization, and community. With a project they’ve affectionately dedicated to their “father,” they inspire others to embrace the winds of change. This team is flooding their community with inspiration and making a huge splash like a powerful storm.

From the moment this machine rolled onto the field, it was clear that something polished, purposeful, and impossibly sleek had entered the arena. Their striking black cube design turned heads in the pits and on the field, proving that form and function can coexist in spectacular fashion. With a build this sharp, elegant, and battle-ready from every angle, "should be fine" might just be the understatement of the season.

When a team of mostly freshmen walks in running job interviews, writing grants, crowdfunding, and volunteering as FLL referees, you know a storm is brewing — and this team is absolutely one to watch. They didn't just join FIRST; they built an entire professional ecosystem from the ground up, proving that age is no barrier to ambition when you've got the drive to match. The judges couldn't help but take notice — this team is a force of nature, and the FIRST community is better for having them in it.

This team may be new to the field, but they've arrived with the vision and hunger of a team destined for greatness — matching every student to their passion, building a true partnership, and already planning school demos to spread the FIRST mission far and wide. They know that even the mightiest titans didn't become legends overnight, humbly learning from veteran teams around them and setting their sights on growing from a kit bot today to a fully bespoke machine tomorrow. With that kind of self-awareness, heart, and drive, the FIRST community better make room because Titan is just getting started.

This award recognizes a team that is growing, building momentum, and leaving a lasting impression on their community. From a small but determined group, they have expanded into a team united across cultures, proving that diversity is their strength and collaboration is a strength. With six native languages spoken across their now 20-strong team, this team is ready to thrive because whether they bring it home a winner or bring it home broke, their rise is nothing short of magic.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Some teams don’t just build for today, but this team builds for the future, investing in growth that lasts far beyond a single season. Through intentional outreach, a commitment to welcoming new students, and a focus on sustaining both skills and passion, they continue to expand their impact year after year. Together with FIRST, they don’t just build robots… they truly make magic happen.

This team doesn't just compete, they electrify the entire arena. With unmatched energy, enthusiasm, and a presence that lifts everyone around them, this team brings spirit to every moment of the event.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: There's a rare kind of team that looks at a finished robot and has the courage to ask — what if we started over? This team came back from their first competition, stripped things down, re-engineered almost every aspect, and discovered that simplicity done right is its own form of brilliance. It turns out the most dangerous move in their arsenal wasn't complexity — it was knowing exactly when to shed their skin and strike!

This team rises from every challenge like the mythical creature that inspired them. When their robot breaks, there's no finger-pointing, only resilience and a team rallying together with positivity. They understand that Gracious Professionalism starts from within, openly acknowledging that stress is real and supporting every member who needs a lift. By sharing their programming Wiki and engineering notebook with the world and rotating all students through the drive team, they don't just build robots — they build each other up, and the entire FIRST community along with them. Congratulations to Team 4533 Phoenix!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Every once in a while, a machine shows up on the field that makes everyone stop and ask — wait, how did they think of that? This team turned heads with a one-of-a-kind three-wide shooter, a flywheel keeping momentum humming, and a modular design so intentional and practical they could swap parts fast as lightning. When your philosophy is building great students first, it turns out the robots tend to be pretty electrifying too.

Some robots look like they were built with care — this one looks like it was crafted with obsession. Almost Every gear, sub-assembly, and other components on this robot was custom 3D printed with a level of precision and intentionality that left judges speechless. When your entire machine is built from the ground up with that kind of dedication, you're not just building a robot — you're building a constellation of quality, a robot named ursa major.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team came in with a master plan, and every match made it clearer that something brilliantly sneaky was at work behind the scenes. Their auxiliary control panel delivered a level of precision and reliability that left the judges thoroughly impressed. with eight preprogrammed functions for instant response, other teams are surely green with envy.
This team had awesome autonomous scoring. Some teams sit and shoot, while others move and prove. After filling with fuel in the neutral zone, this team was dead set and ready to release the mummy!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team knows that in robotics, you can never stop moving — just like the predators that inspire them! Their fin-tastic spirit fills every corner of their pit, their shirts, and even the stands, where a certain sharky student has been making quite the splash. Their jaws-dropping commitment to gracious professionalism proves that even the ocean's fiercest creatures know how to play nice. These sharks truly embody the heart of FIRST, one chomp at a time. Give it up for 11398, Shark Bytes!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: The weather could not stop this team from supporting all things FIRST in their community. From social media to sustaining a variety of formats to grow their pipeline. This team’s impact is not out of the blue, they are creating an intentional chain reaction. The impact award goes to 2815 Blue Devil Mechanics.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has worked tirelessly to promote engineering, helping others see the creativity, opportunity, and impact that STEM can bring to their school and community. Through outreach, mentorship, and leadership, they’ve inspired many to develop a deeper respect and appreciation for engineering. It’s clear their community has become a hub for innovation—because when inspiration starts in Robotz Garage, it doesn’t stay in the garage for long.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: This team struggled with location changes and weather. With their resilience and strong family connection to each other, they put together an amazing machine with hidden icons in their parts. This neat and tidy bot makes them more like “Good Villains”.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: In the spirit of REBUILT™, great discoveries often come from those willing to guide others through unfamiliar terrain. When a rookie team faced challenges, this group stepped in with steady leadership, sharing their knowledge, tools, and encouragement to help a new team build confidence and momentum—and a working robot.. Their support showed the strength that comes when a team moves together like a pack, protecting and lifting those around them to get over the hump or around the bend. The Above and Beyond Award goes to Team 5484… the Wolf Pack from South Bend, Indiana! 🐺🤖

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: This team of Rookies demonstrates the FIRST core principles both in the PITS and on the field of play. Committed to collaboration in the design, fabrication, and most importantly in overcoming unexpected challenges together, they strive to “keep the negative out and the positive in.” Their commitment to competitive excellence is not just thunder and lightning from Mount Olympus, Qualifying to compete for the Rookie All-Star Award at the District Championship is team number 11368 Zetabots and their robot Zeus.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: This team brought unstoppable Curiosity and an infectious desire to learn. They’re a first of their kind and have quickly become a community favorite because of the joy they bring to others. You better get used to these fierce competitors, because hot pink is in!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Some teams build robots for a season — others build programs that last for years. Through long-term outreach, strong partnerships, and a commitment to growing STEM in their community, this team ensures their impact continues well beyond competition. This team's program has the power to keep the buzz going year after year.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: This team’s spirit is evident in the level of collaboration and inclusion they demonstrate on their team and in their community. A very high frequency pace of innovation moves them to build better and compete together. Get on their wavelength, because this Team Spirit award is not a mathematical function but a human one. Congratulations to team 9477 Lambda from Sewannee GA!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team took engineering to another level through their level of imagination. Building a robot that demonstrates engineering excellence by incorporating a double shooter was no easy feat for this team, but was designed through resilience and skill. Also, they’ve demonstrated that Pac-Man is definitely a show stopper!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: Throughout the event, this team showed that success isn’t just measured in points on the field. They divided and conquered to help another team build a robot from scratch and even supported their first-time drivers with guidance and encouragement. This team proved that when teams leap to help others, Gracious Professionalism always hops to the top.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the spirit of Rebuilt, sometimes the future is forged from the scraps of the past, where imagination turns raw metal into unstoppable machines. This robot looks ready to charge across a wasteland, a roaring creation of steel grit, and fearless engineering that proves creativity can thrive even in the toughest environments. This team shows how bold design and wild ideas can be built into something powerful!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: Artifacts from the past often reveal the care, craftsmanship, and attention to detail of the builders who created them. In the spirit of REBUILT™, this team demonstrated that their robot was no illusion and with the same dedication—carefully refining every component until their robot performed with consistency, reliability, and precision. Like master artisans restoring something remarkable, they turned design and execution into something that feels almost magical. The Quality Control Award goes to Team Makin’ Magic with their robot Dune! ✨🤖

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: In the spirit of REBUILT™, innovation often comes from those who refuse to accept the limits of yesterday’s designs. This team engineered a solution that moves with lightning-fast precision, channeling creative energy like a surge through a circuit and turning bold ideas into a powerful performance. Their design crackles with ingenuity, proving that when inspiration strikes, great engineering can harness it and deliver results in a flash. If you haven’t guessed it by now……The Innovation Award goes to Team 1319… Team Flash!

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.script: This growth minded rural team emphasizes inclusion requiring each team member to work on their machine. With a passive intake, cameras for aim, and four consistent autonomous modes. This team will likely do great things at “ The Pit”.

records.eventName: FSC District Richland Event presented by Aflac & RCSD1
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From pit to playing field, this team created a presence that was impossible to miss. With bold colors, coordinated design, and a machine that looked as sharp as it performed, their identity was reflected in every detail. They proved their style is as strong and polished as aluminum itself.

This community based club impressed the Judges with their success in growing STEM for everyone; removing obstacles for members participation; and advocating for their team, the community and their state. This team truly is using Engineering for Good--the Pioneers.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team shares their space with neighboring teams and has secured an impressive amount of funding aimed at expanding access to engineering for their community. Their social media captures widespread attention by showcasing the impressive tools and opportunities they provide. From a city shaped by classified information comes a team committed to open access.

Don’t tell anyone this well-designed, rugged robot refuses to be moved when it matters most. With a locked-in X-mode stance and fiber-reinforced construction, it stays planted while delivering a ridiculously high balls-per-second. Its tightly integrated system, capable of sending four shots wide in quick succession, shows that precision and durability can work as one.

Some teams build robots; this team is building an international franchise. By creating a second FRC team and dominating social media from Turkey to China, they’ve proven that their 'web' of influence is everywhere. For this team, leadership has no time zones.

Starting with a standard kit and a mountain of fabrication challenges, this team didn't just build a robot—they built a powerhouse. By swiftly turning early obstacles into on-field results, they’ve shown the poise of a veteran squad. They proved that rookie status is no barrier to excellence.

This team embraced a true new beginning this year, quite literally rising from the ashes. With grit and determination, they rallied support, raised funds, and collaborated under intense time constraints to get back to the competition.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Weaving themselves into the community, this team threads together recruitment, fundraising, and sustainability with ease. They reduce event waste by upcycling collected plastic bags and inspire the next generation by providing children with pollinating plants to grow at home.

With a look that’s as vibrant as their energy, this team proves that you don't need a monochrome uniform to have a unified mission. Their spirit is so bright, it's practically tie-dyed into their DNA.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team braved a long drive to compete at the highest level in the cold mountain air. These nerds engineered a machine as precise and powerful as the hunters of the sky.

This team believes sharing is caring. Through open alliance, they welcomed the robotics community into their process by sharing code, designs, and insights while learning from others along the way. After a full rebrand, they leaned into collaboration, showing what it really means to be a team player.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While some robots struggle with a jam, this team decided to 'twist' things up. By adapting a marble sorting mechanism into a dual-screw powerhouse, they’ve ensured their scoring is always on a roll. Their design is truly the cat’s pajamas.
Prayers alone can't build a quality robot that can withstand a competition with hard knocks. It takes a lot of planning, precise machining, and shamrocks.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: A team whose control left the judges in awe, Their turret is the finest that anyone saw. Precision's their claim. Tomorrow's their name. Who are we?! [Team 2783]

This team has clawed their way to the top to unleash their mighty roar. Climbing high every match to pounce on their opponents below, they would not accept defeat. Keep an eye out for this jungle prowler.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's aesthetic is certainly ‘geared’ for success. They’ve got the gears, the goggles, and even their own personal physician. We're tipping our hats to them for proving that high-tech and high-fashion aren't mutually exclusive.

This team has built more than a program, they’ve built a home for STEM where students belong. Serving over 360 students locally while reaching thousands more through outreach across their community, state lines, and even globally, they create opportunities for STEM learning where it’s needed most. The judges think this team’s impact is black, red, and spreading fast… you might even say it’s turning into full-on *panda-monium*

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team moves forward with their “eye” on the prize. With unmatched professionalism, their community involvement in a small town ““sowes the seeds” of FIRST values. Let’s hear the “roar”…“From this point forward, there will be Tigers”.

With a presence that feels like it’s circling overhead, this team brings a robot to the field that looks as sharp as it performs. With a sleek design and strong performance, they’ve seamlessly integrated their red and black aesthetic into every detail. The judges think this design really soars above the rest.

This team impressed the judges with their strong commitment to unity and their unwavering commitment to the ideals of FIRST. Nothing limits their community as they work to create a unified HERD within their city and across the border that leaves no one behind.

This team is really heating up. With rising support from their school and community, they have real potential as they continue to gain experience with FIRST. When it comes to rookies, this team is on fire.

They learned to run with the pack before finding their stride. Through funding delays and a wave of new members, they stayed focused, overcame critical obstacles, and brought their strengths to this year’s competition while already building momentum for the next. From the Land of Enchantment, their howl is only just beginning to rise.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Out in the “West” this team had a wild idea. These members thought outside the box while involving the FIRST community in their build. A part here and a part there made their bot as strong as an “Iron Cowboy”

This team’s ability to collaborate effectively, both within their own team and with others, set them apart. Even when faced with challenges, they remained positive, supportive, and focused on helping the entire community succeed. They actively reached out to other teams, shared knowledge, and contributed to a strong sense of unity across the event. They ride enthusiasm, professionalism, and willingness to lift others embody the core values of FIRST.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team rolls onto the field with a robot that looks *ready for battle* and built for control. A masterclass in precision and performance, this robot showcases a refined integration of mechanical reliability and thoughtful design choices that elevate both efficiency and consistency. The judges think this team and their wingman *goose* are *ready for takeoff*.

Even when things didn’t go as planned, this team stayed focused on what really matters. Through a challenging event, they continued to support other teams and volunteers with kindness, patience, and a willingness to help. The judges think this team showed that real strength isn’t just in machines… sometimes it’s in the talons that lift others up.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team came ready to rumble. Through flexible design, their hopper enhanced their robot’s capacity for fuel collection. When it comes to creativity, this team weaved their way to top dog.

These competitors have been a true predator on and off the field. Their robot is a champion of versatility with a perrrr-fect balance of style and functionality. The sharp design of this machine was SPOT ON!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Theres no “fluff” with this team. When it comes to programming, their bot could almost navigate the “matrix” on its own. They show their spirit when they light up ‘Zia” every time they run.

This colorful robot bounces into action the moment the match begins, showing precision right out of the gate. With accurate targeting and the ability to score twice during autonomous, their robot sweeps the competition. The judges think this team really knows how to hop their way to the top.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s robot and team aesthetic is no mystery. Their visual story is wrapped throughout their robot, their pit, their uniforms, and their team spirit. In the end, the puzzle was already solved, just seen in a whole new shade of green

When it comes to promoting the culture of STEM, this team does just participate-- they go absolutely bananas for outreach! By creating innovative community interactions, encouraging mentorship programs, and working countless volunteer hours, they have turned their mission into a marquee event that shines as a beacon of purges for the entire region. When it comes to bridging the gender gap in engineering and inspiring the next generation of innovators, this thinks pink and shows that ladies can!

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Giving new members an immersive training experience in the off-season is key to ensuring this team is ready for build season. Add in team bonding events, strong partnerships, and fun, effective outreach, and you have a recipe that promotes respect and appreciation for engineering and for FIRST throughout the their community. And when you add in their efforts to reduce waste in their manufacturing processes, it is clear that this team is an inspiration for all.

A robot’s design unites precise mechanics and smart control, proving that when every part works together, the whole team really clicks into place. By focusing on efficient use of volume, the design ensures that every component pulls its weight—no wasted space, just a well-packed roster ready for action. And when it’s time to perform, this lineup is always ready to fuel the hub with energy—swinging for maximum efficiency with every hopper.

This team exemplifies a positive attitude in the face of adversity. Perseverance means rising above setbacks—because even when the journey gets turbulent, you’ve got to keep your wings level and aim for new heights. After pushing the limits and soaring past every obstacle, the team claimed victory with true Maverick spirit—proving they’ve got the need for speed and the skill to fly above the rest.
This team of newcomers shined bright with a joyful spirit. Other teams flocked to their playful, energetic, vibe. This team’s potential and heart truly REVEAL firsts core values.

This team is easily recognizable in the pits and the field with their themed headwear. They have persevered through new designs and mechanical challenges and added an engineering request form to attract changes. We're excited to see this team explode in the future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has proven they are truly outstanding in their field by cultivating a program that will yield success for seasons to come. They didn’t just plant the seeds for engineering education in their community, they’ve ensured the program will sow a bumper crop of innovation that will reap rewards for years to come. While others might feel they are plowing through challenges alone, this team works with others to create long term continuity - there is no moo-ving backwards for this team.
This team keeps their image, nice and sharp. They make sure everyone has a Gouda time with their cheesy presence. Their sprit is unified like warm and gooey bowl of mac and cheese.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The shape of our discussion gradually revealed a framework that made the final decision feel inevitable. A passing remark about cowboys sketching trapezoids in the dust made the process simple. Ultimately, it was as easy for us to decide as it is for this robot to wrangle fuel.

This team is known for helping other teams, including FLL & FTC. They embrace the core value of fun by playing hide and seek at competitions. All members are cross trained, and all seniors create their own unique guide books to pass down to underclassman.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team used creative solutions for resolving problems to overcome on the filed. Their 2 stage shooter sent fuel flying constantly even on the move. Their cassette style spindexer was hardly weak and it stood strong during competition.

records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

Their efforts to include every team is very appreciated.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division

Responding with uncanny coordination, they executed complex actions with the kind of reliability that hints at something deeper beneath the surface. Like a watchful guardian at the gates, their design demonstrated power, awareness, and control in perfect balance.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: From the very first seconds of the match, this team demonstrated that preparation meets excellence in autonomous performance. Every movement was deliberate, every action impactful, showcasing a deep understanding of both strategy and control. They deliver a true TRIPLE THREAT in autonomy—accuracy, reliability, and innovation.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team draws its strength from a legacy of world augmenting elite values of FIRST. Focusing on building stronger communities, hosting outreach events, powered by “Y”, and building more.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team truly inspired the judges. Their dedication to providing new and sustainable opportunities to their area is changing the course of so many futures. records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX

They didn't give up blending their culture, love of STEM, and teamwork into creating an organization that will continue for many years.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team pulls in members beyond the HORIZON. For such a young team, their efforts to maintain themselves really impressed us. This team IGNITEs a passion for STEM in Frisco.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse

This team is like a drink of clean water quenching a thirst while embracing diversity and empowering others in their school. records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

A backup plan for auto shoot, change to planned driver set way points, and changing to steel intake axles, this is a quality robot that we can appreciate.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

Whether it is starting new teams across the world or sharing their resources online with others, they are growing their global footprint with purpose. Through providing mentorship and assistance to 75 FIRST teams, running multiple STEM summer camps, and hosting and volunteering at FIRST events, they provide the continual, sustainable support necessary for others to thrive. This team performs with excellence in spreading STEM both locally and internationally!

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX

Defense may be their aim, but adapting is their game! Their bot prowls just beyond the trenches. This team earned their stripes with their strategic play all day!

This team galloped back stronger than ever. After facing massive turnover and funding challenges that kept them from competing, the team rebuilt and secured the resources to return. This team proves that when horsepower meets heart, a comeback is always possible!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team checked ALL the boxes - sustaining people, prosperity, AND planet. They didn't just build bots, they built a whole alumni network with their 5 to 6 year plans. Like savvy farmers, they didn’t just plant ideas - they continually cultivate and harvest STEM futures.
This team shines with easily recognizable uniforms and face paint. Their extraordinary enthusiasm makes FIRST loud. With mascot lore worthy of a feature film, they're out of this world.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team soars through the sky with their turret mounted flywheel. They showed extensive knowledge about their engineering process with an excellent technical binder. This team drives through their competition like a ghost rider.

Rising high in the FIRST community, this team helps everyone around them. Whether opening their field for others, helping anyone in need, or handing out safety glasses, they show the true spirit of Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creativity shows they were thinking outside the bot. The angle of their double barrel flywheels were just too radical! We’re green with envy about this team’s creativity.
From the get-go, this team had a clear vision for a quality build by isolating electronics from mechanical components. They could lift the hood and get those engines running. No wild guesses here!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is on the search for control. Their innovative technology allowed them to wrangle their robot throughout the competition. On the quest for success and keeping it simple, you might say their robot runs smoother than a tumbleweed on the western frontier.

This team simulated various scenarios so that they knew where and when to be despite the hurdles. All we had to say was "3, 2, 1, go," and they could finish the game with a graceful breeze. These girls showed they CAN!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

Outreach sparked a school board meeting leading to FLL implementation in elementary schools and building the future brick by brick. Being more than Robots, they are actively advocating for a district event in their area. This team rebuilt their membership from the ground up. They worked with the materials they had on hand. This team really shows us how to get things done ‘JUST IN’ time.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has demonstrated sustainability through being a focal point in their school community. They have collaborated with various organizations school-wide by hosting interactive events and drives. They believe that to maintain sustainability, it comes from community outreach and awareness. This team is a BEAST from the EAST!
Their spirit makes everyone green with envy. This team is radical in the stands. These CUBS let everyone know they are loud and proud of their team.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This winner did not just build a robot; they built a system. With an iPad-integrated shooting process and a robust autonomous driving suite, their engineering workflow was nothing short of excellent. Their attention to detail and process-driven design GRILLED the competition!
This team graciously provides support to other teams by lending them not just a hand but other tools and materials. Roses are red, violets are blue, this team is always there to support you.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
