This team reminds us that 'the details matter.' Their robot was built with precision and durability in mind, highlighted by their impressive spin indexer featuring a modular center piece. This design allows for easy maintenance and consistent performance and is a BASTION against the stresses of competition!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Most teams think a perfect shot requires standing still, but this team prefers a large amount of fuel delivery with more speed. Their control system computes complex trajectories on the fly ensuring the whole robot does the aim, it was hungry and keeps coming back for more. This FAST-FOOD delivery control system will certainly SPICE things up.

While many teams impressed with strong autonomous openings, this team stood out by sustaining a consistent, reliable performance from start to finish. Through the use of advanced look-up tables and seamless, precise cycles, their robot demonstrated that it does not just act—it thinks ahead and charges into action.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team showed us why a focus on themes is so visually impactful. They made it a PROJECT to make all aspects of their team cohesive. Their bot ‘J. Robot Oppenheimer’ pays tribute to their hometown.

While most teams measure their success in points and placements, one extraordinary team has decided to measure it by something far greater. From answering urgent needs in their community during difficult times to investing thousands of hours mentoring the next generation of engineers... ...this powerhouse has built an expanded high-tech workspace, created STEM publications distributed internationally in numerous languages, and delivered critical support to teams across the globe at the World Championships. So let’s give it up for the team that shows us all how to *PEAR UP* and lift everyone higher

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has a rich history of continuous recruitment which is reflected this season across the FIRST community. Aiming high and going higher - they set the bar for other teams to emulate and then they flip over it.
This team’s robot is out of this world. Their sleek machine shines on the field and in the pits. They’re primed to takeoff and conquer the competition and beyond!

This team’s infectious, positive attitude was impossible for the judges to miss! Obstacles? Not a problem for these Gear-Heads. With a modified Everybot based design and a helping hand for everyone else the judges are happy to recognize their achievement!

This team took the competition by storm in their very first season. Arriving with the poise and organization of a veteran, they have not just joined the FIRST community, they are leading it. Soaring high in the skies on golden wings, they are already a force to be reckoned with!

This team raided the competition, descending on the field with tenacity and a never-say-die attitude. While a robot called ‘Scrappy’ might imply an underdog – it’s a powerhouse of grit and clever engineering. Soar to the skies with this team!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s focus on reusable resources and building kits is medal worthy. Their application process casts a wide net, and they doubled their team size. They’re going up, up, up—it’s their moment!

With a little spark and a lot of magic, this team quickly cast a spell over the competition. In their rookie season, they showed extraordinary enthusiasm - helping other teams and bringing positive energy everywhere they went. Their magic is impossible to miss.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s design iterations have made all the difference, and they’ve got the data to prove it! Their field simulations help their design shoot for the stars. Tip your top hat to this team.

This team was a bright presence all weekend, moving at the speed of kindness. We all noticed how they continuously reflected positivity and stepped in to help wherever needed. This team truly lights up the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Standard? Out of the box? Not good enough for this team, who floored the judges with a mechanical solution that marched to a different drum, as clever as it was effective. It’s a percussive powerhouse that left the competition in total shock!

Bear with this team, because their quality is next level. This sturdy bot zips around with a modular design. Gravity may be fast, but this team is faster! If you’re not yet one of their minions … just wait!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team doesn’t just bring energy – they surge through the field. They masterfully leverage the right programming tool for the job, combining a mastery of multiple programming systems with precision and creativity to achieve exceptional control of their robot.

Carving effortlessly through the field, this team shows no weakness. They wowed the judges with the ability to collect and shoot autonomously over and over again. Guided by three limelights, this bot always points to the emerald city.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team can scratch the competition with their sharp claws. No matter where you are on the field, their eyes are watching you! These CATS don’t stick to the status quo.

Teamwork creates strong bonds within a team and throughout their community. Each activity strengthens the team, from hosting summer camps to connecting with industry professionals. But this year's team took bonds a step further, gaining support for a bond issue that will increase STEM opportunities through their district by providing over $55 million for a CTE center and additional funding for STEM across campuses.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Community and commitment go hand-in-hand, and this team is proof. In addition to fundraising, recruiting members and mentors, and developing skills, they clean up after natural disasters and help by building ride-on robots for mobility-challenged youth. For this team, it's Go, Baby, Go!

At first glance, this team’s robot stands out with a layout so clean and organized, everything just falls into place. Looking closer, their pneumatic system and thoughtful design really take shape, creating a machine that’s easy to follow and built with clear intent. And when design and function line up this well, this team proves they’re not just winging it—they’ve truly honed their craft.

This team has a recipe for success that impressed the judges in multiple areas. They partner with public library branches to provide workshops in low-income areas, host camps, and even do workshops specifically for mentors. Their name came up frequently when other teams talked about who has helped them at this event. They even take time to cook dinner together to create a strong family atmosphere.

This team of 1st year robotic students impressed us with their accomplishments as a brand new team from a brand new school. With only 2 years of experience across over 20 students, they were able to hold their own against high performing veteran teams at the competition. It's clear that this team wrangles each challenge with a calm and collaborative mindset.

This young team is rebuilding with grit, purpose, and a vision far bigger than themselves. After needing to give away their resources, they had to start over over with nothing but heart. They knocked on every sponsor’s door, spread FIRST into their own Construction Academy, and showed up to every expo and STEM summit in town. This team did not just rise, but they pulled everyone up with them.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Sustainability requires addressing people, funding, and thoughtful use of resources. This year's winner takes a multi-faceted approach to attracting new members and have developed a steady funding stream. Their drive to reduce their environmental impact was inspired by a lack of HVAC in their original workspace and includes repurposing off-cuts into souvenirs, recycling aluminum shavings, and optimizing cut sheets.
This team has spirit, yes they do! They've got energy, this is true! In the stands you will hear! They are the HEROs of the cheer!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team didn’t just bounce back, they engineered their comeback, rebuilding in just two weeks with a design that’s anything but half-baked. With a reliable rack-and-pinion intake and a turret that stays on target even while moving, their robot doesn’t just perform, it tracks success. When it comes to consistent scoring and systems that truly click, this team has all the right gears in motion.

This team extends their "victory-mindset" philosophy to include helping all those around them succeed. Their positive attitude and willingness to share their resources make them a go-to team for those having problems.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Using 3D printed hardware, nets, and metal, this team uses readily available materials and can open doors quickly to replace components. When their spindexer needed improvements, they found inspiration for spinning stars and washable denim to create the best flow. This robot woke up feeling the cheesiest.

This team’s attention to detail starts with a simple but effective turret support that keeps their system steady under pressure. From there, their robust turret design really turns heads, using a retractable badge reel to keep wiring clean and controlled as it rotates. And with a unique CNC-inspired brush spindexer that keeps game pieces flowing, this team truly sweeps the competition away.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: It doesn’t matter if you collide with this sturdy metal, as the feedback system keeps track of trajectory calculations. A variable climber can quickly align to the tower and invert the bot to the top. The Go / No Go poll is shimmering green across the board for Artemis.

This team climbed the ranks through their robust and modular auto modes. Their robot magnetically zeroes their mechanism automatically to enable consistent auto points. Their thumper won’t let stuck fuel rain on their scoring parade.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team truly stood out from the crowd. Their pit was shiny and gleaming like the Emerald City. When they took the field, they demonstrated professionalism and precision while still reflecting true Texas hospitality.

Spreading STEM is the foundation for this team, creating the next generation of STEM stars. Hosting tournaments has become a natural sustainable hobby bringing unity to the area. Only 35% of STEM degrees are earned by women, leading this team to create girl-inspired initiatives. EVERY body who wants to participate in FIRST should have the opportunity, so this team inspired FIRST to create the kit bot. This team has truly risen to Woodie’s challenge to change the world.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Creating a commitment to STEM and FIRST, this team supports the full pipeline - FLL, FTC, and FRC. Building relationships with community leaders for funding, mentors, and guest speakers are part of the core of this team. Let’s join these vaqueros riding in the beautiful sunsets of McAllen and look forward to the green team hosting again in the coming seasons.

This team has potential as wide as a clear, blue summer sky. They were driven by an ambitious plan to build a turret of their own. They headed downtown on the foe-foe unleashing their 3D-printed fuel launcher.

This team has built a buzzing culture of collaboration and commitment since 2021. They foster deep camaraderie among teammates while recruiting and mentoring new students. Their teamwork, community engagement, and family camaraderie truly sting in the best way.

This young team is built on resilience and heart, growing strong and breaking through every challenge they face together. They compete not only to strengthen their engineering skills but to develop professionalism, leadership, and teamwork. Creating a program that participates in community events, works with local schools, and applies for grants proving that even a young team can break through barriers in a community.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team believes that knowledge should be shared by everyone, everywhere. Through a sustainable system built by their students, they ensure valuable robotics knowledge continues to reach new communities year after year. By translating robot documentation into multiple languages and publishing it for teams around the world, they are making robotics more accessible for all.

Energy can change an entire arena, and this team brings it wherever they go. From the stands to the field, their bright colors, loud cheers, and constant support for teams around them create an atmosphere of excitement and unity. If you see a wave of orange in the stands, you know this team is leading the charge.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team brought a bright spark of engineering to the field with a clever yellow design. At the heart of their machine is an impressive 270 degree rotating fuel launcher, giving them flexibility, precision, and control from nearly any angle. This team showed us engineering that truly turns heads and shines bright.

While some teams might focus only on their own success, others make the entire event better for everyone around them. Throughout the competition, these cats could be found lending their time, tools, and expertise wherever help was needed. Whether assisting teams behind the scenes or helping them get competition-ready, they truly embody the spirit of Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: High above the competition field, a shadow circles with patient, steady wings, and steely eyes locked. Their robot unleashes independent double launchers while a gyro-guided system keeps every move balanced and controlled. With adaptive programming, proven components from past robots build a smarter machine to inspire the younger generations.

These competitors show that success in robotics isn’t about flashy tricks. Their robot reflects thoughtful design, robust craftsmanship, and consistent performance. This team has proven that the best tricks are the ones built with true quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team brings explosive precision to the field. Their design of an innovative hopper system controlled accuracy and consistency through the match. This team combined creative engineering with precise performance.

These team's mission is to be consistent in EVERY match. Their high performing and accessible astronaut fuels the engine persistently and frequently during the autonomous period. You can count on them to climb to the moon and back.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some teams make their presence known the moment you see them. With a theme that carries through their entire team presentation, their creativity and attention to detail make them stand out wherever they go. Their vibrant green branding and powerful lion mascot make their identity truly roar.

This team refuses to “CLOSE” its doors to anyone; their impact knows no boundaries. Building global libraries one keystroke at a time, this team will support you in both the dark of night and the ORANGE light of day. They are as fierce and unstoppable as a bucking Bronco. Congratulations team 3481 - BroncBotz

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Clad in black and red, this team has built more than robots, they’ve built opportunity. From creating STEAM kits for underserved schools, expanding their program to welcome students from multiple school districts, the growth of their program is inspirational. What started small has grown with just a little bit of “panda-monium.” Congratulation to team 6369 Mercenary Robotics

This team’s 25 years of experience shows in every punch of their performance. Drawing inspiration from Robot in 3 Days, they engineered a robust machine with a polished design that keeps their ground intake running smooth and steady. This team’s creativity and consistency prove that elegance and grit can swing hand in hand! Congratulations team 457 - the Grease Monkeys

This team exemplifies the large impact a small group can make on its community. Raiding the field, this close-knit team of 6 succeeds through simplicity and cooperation with their peers. Rising from the ashes, their bot claims the Judges' Award in San Antonio. Congratulations to Taft High School RoboRaiders, Team 3561.

This team believes every great robot starts with a great plan. Using CAD to design and iterate before building each part of their robot, they brought strong engineering discipline from their previous FTC experience. For their thoughtful design process and outstanding first season, the judges believe a new “ERA” is dawning for this rookie team. Congratulations to team 11169 ERA- Delta

When this team lost their school support, these “scouts” didn’t pack up their gear, they found a new trail. Meeting in libraries and community centers, they continue to serve their community by mentoring local FLL and FTC teams. Their program shows that with the right leadership and community spirit, success can be built anywhere… and sometimes it even comes “with cookies”. Congratulations team 9419 Vulcan

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team believes sustainability grows strongest when the whole “HERD” moves together. Through their outreach initiatives, they extend robotics learning far beyond their own community, even crossing borders to share the FIRST mission . With programs built to grow and endure, this “excellent” team is easy to spot, just look for the sombreros. Congratulation to team 9136 Rampage Team

Bursting to the surface with a joyful splash, this team makes its presence known with energy that’s impossible to miss. They bring enthusiasm that erupts from the stands, rallying their alliance partners, and keeping the entire event smiling. This team sends a powerful wave of team pride and positivity across the whole competition. Congratulaltiosn to team 9034 - the Space Dolphins

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The sparkled both off and on the field with their solid programming, “brilliant” robot design and community outreach. This team never “pauses”; they are fierce on excellence. Congratulations team 2582 - Pantherbots

This team creates a “maelstrom” of positive energy that draws others in and lifts the entire competition. They create a powerful “current” of collaboration and kindness that strengthens our whole community. Congratulations to team 3735 - Team VORTX.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team blended innovation and precision like a pineapple pen of engineering flair and function. With tap and go presets, a brushed 3D printed spin dexer, and vision tracking that adjusts seamlessly on the move, their solutions redefine creative control. There is no hiding their creativity. Congratulations Team 5572 - Robots
In the past year, this team has soared to new heights. Their meticulous approach to research and design has proven them the “Champions” of quality. Congratulations Team 8114 - Rocketeers

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This “wild” team bucked onto the field with unwavering resolve. Their autonomous technology was truly “in a different world”. When it comes to leading the way in innovation, these competitors are riding boldly into the sunset. Congratulations to team 4717 - Westerner Robotics
Scoring the balls within a “Blink” of an eye. Their robot control moved with purpose and “Red” the field. Fast decisions, quick execution, and no hesitation. Congratulations to team 4219 - Team RED!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Judges had to PAWS at this pit. Something about the display made them stop and look again. Strong colors. Clear design across the whole station. The design showed pride and a clear identity. There was so much to take in that the judges couldn’t BEAR to leave. Congratulations to team 4610 - BearTecs
Bridging gaps leads to strong teams and strong communities. One good turn leads to better outcomes for all. Your impact award winners are team 1477, Texas Torque!

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team turns passion into power with Big Energy and often has us asking—Who can? They can. From pit to field, they show up helping every team, supporting every moment, and lifting others as they rise. Through outreach, mentorship, and heart, they make engineering feel possible, personal, and within reach for everyone they touch. For turning inspiration into action, building community everywhere they go, and proving every time that when you ask “Who can? "the answer is always Lady Cans! 💖

This year's recipient impressed judges with a remarkably refined and efficient build that turned heads throughout the competition. Inspired by the poised, watchful grace of an ancient protector this team's sleek machine fused striking visual symmetry with championship-caliber engineering precision. Team 4295 the Hudson Stingers

This team shows their “stripes” as mentors to grade schools, middle schools and high schools alike. Helping the community through food drives, Christmas donations, drone competitions and school events. With the graduating class leaving a gap in upper leadership they have stepped up and moved forward, never looking back, “roaring” back into the spotlight. “From this point forward, there will be Tigers”.

These “cats” took on every challenge, stared it in the face and said “Bring on the next one” even though it seemed like the challenges were outnumbering the accomplishments. But through all the ups and downs of the build season and even their first competition, the smiles, commoradary and belief in themselves never went away. The “friendships” created in “big cat country” are hard to duplicate and as strong as a “pyramid”.

After losing their workshop, this team *weathered the storm* and kept building. Working out of a small garage, the team of five built their robot in just four days to make it here to Waco, all while continuing to mentor two younger teams in their community. With resilience, grit, and a commitment to lifting others up, the judges think these *underdogs* really know how to bring the *thunder* to the competition.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is mission-focused on building a sustainable pipeline where everyone can thrive. Welcoming students to innovate and be inspired while working together. Soaring towards a positive team environment that will last, congratulations team 5788, Eagle Spec Ops.

Crossing the western border of Texas to compete here in Waco, this first-year New Mexico team brings energy and enthusiasm to every moment of competition. Whether it’s a small success or a big victory, they celebrate it all with the same excitement and pride. With a presence that lifts those around them and energy that never quits, the judges agree that this team’s spirit is truly *phenom-enal.*

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team’s robot shows thoughtful engineering from end to end—where mechanical design, programming, and strategy come together seamlessly. With precision, power, and a strike that’s hard to miss, this team proved that when the Rattlers move, the competition takes notice. Congratulations to Team 3679 — Rattlers for winning the Engineering Excellence Award! 🐍⚙️

This team knows how to bring people together, mixing teamwork, kindness, and support into everything they do. They embody what it means to compete with respect while uplifting teams around them. They are cooking up a culture of encouragement and kindness. Congratulations, team 9418, Pasta Bots!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team puts creativity into overdrive. Designing their robot with game elements from last year, this robot stands out with innovative and smart solutions. Fueled with a passion to include everyone in the creative design process, congratulations team 7492, Turbo Torque.

This robot runs like a well-oiled machine—clean construction, thoughtful design, and components working together smoothly from start to finish. When the gears turn for this team, everything just works. Congratulations to Team GORTS for earning the Quality Award!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team navigates every match with strategy, control, and focus. With color-coordinated lights guiding their performance, they communicate clearly with precision. Leading the field with clarity and coordination, congratulations Team 2848, Rangers

When the match begins, this team’s robot strikes fast and true—bold in red and black and executing its routine with confidence and control. Their programming and preparation put them at the front of the field from the very first second. Leading the charge at the vanguard, mission accomplished. Congratulations to Team 6369 — Mercenary Robotics for winning the Autonomous Award!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team brings a whole vibe wherever they go: bright, colorful, and “glowing”. Their pit’s rainbow mascot hangs around, adding more colorful spirit, matching their fun energy. Add in how they hype each other up, and the judges think this team is the best at “getting in the flow” of competition

This team created a significant impact by integrating FIRST programs into their school curriculum and expanded access through camps, community partnerships, and mentorship of other teams. They achieved financial support from their government that has created more STEM opportunities for students and helped rebuild their regional FIRST community. Through their leadership and impact, they spark lasting enthusiasm and opportunity in STEM for future generations.

records.awardName: Regional Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: It's inspiring the way this team spreads STEM initiatives throughout their rural community and country Their vehicle of engagement is remote control vehicles and water rockets These grounded birds certainly appear ready to take flight

This team’s persistence and adaptability was elemental in succeeding on the field. Their use of color coordination and custom machined parts was methodically documented from incubation to creation. This small team proved their scrappy spirit through EGG-cellent resilience in each iteration until the final design was hatched.

This team surged in from nowhere with the fierce force of a Sirocco (suh·row·kow). They gathered many resources from the community, crafting a network of mentors, sponsors, and team members—carving a structure as strong and enduring as red rock canyons. An whirlwind straight out of the desert.

This small team started themselves, and their optimized execution is impressive. The team website pops in yellow and black, and they are standardizing their processes for continued success. Their name may be arbitrarily small, but they can indeed "Do a great job."

This team pays homage to their heritage while building a strong foundation for their future Through mentoring and workshops supporting FLL, FTC and their community, they are rising above the rest. Encouraging young women in STEM makes this team a Sparkling example of FIRST ideals.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: These competitors strike with precision and plan for their future needs. They preserve every lesson learned to strengthen their team, and repurpose old parts to turn past builds into future success. Like a scorpion in the desert, this team is built to endure. Demonstrating sustainability in every sense.

This team's colors light up their pits like their team lights up the community. Whether in a parade or launching things into the nosebleed section at a basketball game. Their enthusiasm for robotics is commenda-BULL, and mooooving.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team did not show up in tatters. They definitely have it all together. They did not teeter totter over the hump. Choosing simplicity over triplicity was the key to their drum shooter. They really dig engineering.

This electric team impressed the judges with their current connections, which they used to help their fellow teams prepare for the season. With their consistent sharing and collaboration, this team isn’t just playing around - even if they’re known for their games.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Ambitious to a fault, they demonstrated skill in drafting, design, and prototyping. With their solid build, they are sure to withstand a crash test. Folded 1000 times from a single sheet of aluminum, tried, tig welded, tied, and dyed, give it up for team!

This robot’s exceptional durability, craftsmanship, and attention to every detail is what excellence in engineering and craftsmanship looks like. Their robot stood out with exceptional durability, thoughtful design, and meticulous workmanship. With every part and wire wound perfectly, never missing a beat, and built with the kind of meticulous quality that keeps everything running like a fine watch.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This season, one robot took a daring roll with its controls and turned chance into mastery. Delivering an innovative control system so clever and precise that it consistently beat the odds and performed exactly as intended, no matter how the field played out.

This team's emphasis on precise autonomy brought them much success on the field. You won't find their rebuilt high-performing anywhere else, but they say the old model is still in stock. Their autonomous climb in particular will help them hang loose while surfing the wave to victory.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Everyone has surely noticed the positive image of these Buckaroos. Roping FIRST values into everything they do, they are riding their horse high and proud. But don’t let their name fool you, this team’s future is as bright as their colors.

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Delivering IMPACT felt both at home and internationally. This team flies to bring FIRST to the underserved. Striving to ensure No Robot Left Behind: Robotica Para Todos!

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team embodies a crazy passion for STEM education. This year, they were dedicated to the mission of building sustainable school-based teams. For starting & celebrating new FIRST teams, our judges went simply LoCo for these LEMONS

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: The judges were impressed with what they HERD from this team. They stood out with noteworthy features in turret design, snapback capability & component accessibility. They have proven to be MOOOO-vers & shakers in design, on the field & in the VALLEY

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: For four years, this team has been forging a new identity. They even created commemorative buttons to celebrate their first-ever graduating class. The cat's out of the bag now… Presenting the Judges' Award for Senior Legacy

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team really took their opportunity to shine. They mentored students and adults alike, introducing them to FIRST & how to run a team. In 3 STELLAR years, this team has really proved that they are all made of STARSTUFF

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team was a cut above the rest in their dedication to sustainability. With a robust student-to-student mentoring program & extensive legacy documentation. It’s easy to see this team grow well into the future, alongside their beards.

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team's fantastically punny robot has the judges REELING over. The team’s swag and style are a show stopper, and they exude constant energy with their school spirit. The judges are excited to celebrate these robot a-FISH-ionados

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: These swift engineers embody the full process, from goal planning & CADing to executing design. They test with wood before building the final bot. In signature dark feathers & gold highlights, these birds strike with precision excellence

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team strives to ensure that everyone they encounter experiences the FIRST Core Values and is welcomed to join the FIRST community. Their STRIDES cover vast territory STRETCHING over 5 countries. These JUNGLE CATS are the epitome of Gracious Professionalism

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They STREAKED to success with their unique design. The effective & reliable double turret set this team apart from the PACK. Their unique approach to this year's challenge proves they really earned their creativity STRIPES.

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team is small but mighty. Using an iterative design cycle, they built a reliable and low-maintenance subsystem You’ll find this team chilling down the shore

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The UNIVERSE knows which team reigns supreme. With pre-calculations & accuracy in shooting, their innovations really shined This STELLAR team blew the judges away in a COSMIC EXPLOSION

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.script: You may not see this team coming, but their robot certainly knows what to do. This team has embraced the definition of Automation Engineering. Their complex routines & custom button array make the drivers like ghosts.

records.eventName: FCH District Alexandria VA Event presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's imagery is iconic, with the quality you might see in a Hollywood movie. Their branding was everywhere: the robot, the pit, their swag & their iconic headwear. Hats off to the team whose image is distinctive enough to overcome a fear of snakes

records.eventName: FCH District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Ball
records.script: True leadership in the community is defined by a commitment to spreading knowledge and building a sustainable future for the next generation. By launching initiatives like a summer outreach program for elementary students and maintaining a consistent, monthly presence to raise STEM awareness, we are doing more than just building robots; we are advocating for a world where technical literacy is accessible to everyone. This dedication was on full display during the recent presentations, where a clear passion for the mission and meticulous preparation set a standard for excellence. Because of this unwavering drive to inspire others and the potential to scale these outreach efforts even further, it is a distinct honor to announce Copperhead Robotics Team 401 as the winner of the Impact Award.

records.eventName: FCH District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Ball
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: Try that in a small town; they did. Despite small town recourses, their dedication to spreading STEM is second-to-none. They're a COMET FLYING through the sky spreading STEM everywhere they go.

records.eventName: FCH District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Ball
records.script: This team earned a feather in their cap for their industrial robot design. They focus on simplicity, ensuring easily switchable parts and ease of access. There was nothing cavalier about their build process or robot.

records.eventName: FCH District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Ball
records.script: Just because you're new doesn't mean you don't have a story to tell. This young team knows the importance of documenting their successes. These SCARABS are about to scurry back to tell their friends all of the cool things they did.

records.eventName: FCH District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Ball

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s robot not only saw the future; it communicated it. They seamlessly choreographed their routine of eating up fuel and hoarding it away for the opportune time. When THEIR lights go red, be prepared for them to RAID the field.

With solid automation, this robot nearly THINKS. Even if fuel gets stuck, it automatically unjams before anyone BLINKS. With a press of a button, fuel feeds through the robot, and into the hub it SINKS.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: As soon as we entered the shop, we were welcomed by a greatly cohesive theme, from pit, to robot, and their chefs. 5 out of 5 stars for aesthetics across their dishes. If you’re ordering here, don’t miss the Tempura!

For this team’s well-established outreach events to ensure STEM inclusivity in their community, they ATE and left NO CRUMBS. They were OUTREACH-MAXXING over the last 3 years, expanding their FLL curriculum to include kindergarten, first, and second grade. Along with their 3 FTC teams, this team started 4 new FLL teams this year. They also began 5 workshops at a senior living community, bringing FIRST to the older generation and bringing the older generation to FIRST. Cumulatively, this team brought STEM to six-seven—I mean 67—events since 2023. The team is also COOKING with their inclusion efforts, expanding Unified Robotics to Türkiye and Mexico and formed three GEARS conventions to spread the program to more FIRST teams. Finally, they FORGED their new FLL mock competition, “Liberty SKIBIDI.” And it’s high-key FIRE.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: We’ve had a FIELD DAY digging through this team’s outreach. From disability aids to FTC & FLL scrimmages, this team FETCHES STEM Education for everyone with summer engineering camps & free library workshops. If we need to be more PACIFIC, we’ll just have to tell you:
This team’s design was out of pocket. With their number suspended in the branches of their design. The judges were Inspired by their use of unique software.

This team is committed to REMOVING barriers in their community. As part of their annual STEM camps, they intentionally select a school using a variety of considerations, WEIGHING how to best REACH marginalized students. This team is taking the CHARGE to RESHAPE STEM learning, as the judges present the “Mindful Matrix” award.

This team of students is on their ASCENT and are far from their APOGEE. Their membership has SOARED and they have FLOWN to the top of the rankings. They are raising the bar for other young teams through forming strong alliances, locally and internationally. These archers are forming traditions that will last long past their second year and POINTS to a bright future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team helps FLL and FTC teams get started and then helps them stand on their own FEET. The team members STICK TOGETHER beyond the seasons and borders, showing their pride in BLUE. This team UNPACKED sustainability issues to give younger students the PARTS they need for the future.

This team’s enthusiasm hit us like a TIDAL WAVE. From fairs and festivals to door-to-door outreach, it’s clear as day this team is ALL HANDS-ON DECK to share FIRST. This team’s spirit makes a SPLASH at competitions and in their community. SURF’S UP!

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: From Seattle comes a team whose engineering instincts are sharp. Multiple sensors keep the robot aware. Shots land even on the move. Prototype. Test. Measure. Improve. Something tells us this machine was built by a very cyber-savvy creature.

We’re PAWS-itive you’ve seen lots of purple in the pits. Whether it’s helping teams at the competition or going FERAL for advocacy, these COOL CATS have it down to a science. You would never want to vote this team off the island.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s compact robot is full of surprises. When competition winds up, they SPRING into action! Their unique serpentine design has them BLITZING the hub.

This team achieved strength by bending material to their will. Their rectangular shape relied on a rebuilt part that was previously shattered. You may not have even seen this team since they known to move undetected, but their quality cannot be concealed.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team left our heads spinning with their precision engineered turret and multi-camera system. All to support their iterative ballistics model to throw fuel like JAVELINS. This team’s code base is anything but SPARTAN.

This team really CLIMBED to the top of the field in autonomous. Multiple cameras guide every move around the field, keeping their turret firing non-stop. Even while they HANG, their shots still land; these QUEEN BEES have brought a whole new meaning to HANGTIME.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Yesterday, this team was BACK in BLACK and Brought a cold BLAST from the PAST to the PITS. Presently they are repping blue and are PRESENTING PROFESSIONALISM coins to PEERS. These PENGUINS must have broken lots of gears in the last 20 YEARS.

This team’s approach to advocacy for FIRST and STEAM has been anything but quiet. They’ve traveled the country talking to leaders for and wide and certainly haven’t been operating on the down-low. We are CONFIDENT this team is making an Impact on the future.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team ignites excitement for FIRST values and STEM. Their commitment to their love of engineering is inspiring. Sparks fly when this team shows up for their community.

This team's design is both elegant and practical, with a lot of smart material choices backed by keen engineering judgement and experimentation. Their numerous coatings to improve cleaning for lower friction gears and higher friction bumpers really impressed the judges. Every time they play, this team's snowblower brings pure Chaos to the field.

The judges couldn't ignore this team's challenges and ability to rise stronger together. Fueled by pink, powered by union, this team showed up ready for anything. And if that wasn't enough, the Robocats kept the energy high and the chili feed kept everyone fed- because nothing says resilience like robots and chili.

Always leading the pack, this team has navigated big changes with grace. From relocating tools to building a new shop, they adjusted and grew. This team didn't just stand up for what's right, they led the Crusade.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's love for their STEM community is obvious. Sending old parts and helping across the globe shows their metal. These patriots don't skip arm day!
Their tight knit community is something every team should strive for. Team spirit won't leave you blue. Their goal to never quit is right on target.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team's unique game strategy allowed them to quickly and efficiently deliver fuel to the hub. Their ability to rapidly hunt down fuel will save them from extinction. Their team's raptor machine clawed its way to the top.

The Judges saw many PARTS of this team around the PIT. Their outreach in and outside of the competition makes a difference to many. This team’s gracious professionalism shows that helping others is “working hard and having fun.”

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Starting with boxes of parts, this team set out to bend ideas, maximizing their throughput and flipping their world. We love the creativity of these droids!

The team’s robot was built for easy replacement of critical components. Their smart use of silicone and teflon on their robot contributes to their success on the field. Despite their name, this robot breathes balls, not fire.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The judges thought this team took risks out of the blue. Their innovative use of technology stood out like thunder. This team's collaboration ensures they have a clear vision through any rolling storm.
This will only take 20 seconds. 8 years ago, you were in grade school, 5 years ago, you were competing in FLL, 3 years ago you started FTC. Just 2 more seconds and we won’t leave you…hanging!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Touching down from another planet and looking suspiciously prepared. This team has serious robotics skills, galaxy level teamwork and absolutely no plans of leaving empty handed. Keep your eyes to the sky and watching for these martians!

This team ignites the community from FLL to career pathways and they have the data! With intentional reach into their community and the surrounding area, Working with Hope, creating alignments from robots to advocacy, this team is redefining what is possible Changing the minds of people around us, one paradigm shift at a time.

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team has a range of STEM outreach opportunities as wide as the OCEAN.. Don’t worry, they don’t bite! They engage everyone in STEM. With continuous inspiration and robot readings that are more than periodic, they have SINES of a bright future!

This team’s robot looks like it rolled out of a design studio—sleek, intentional, and ready to hunt points. From their no-fuss spring deployed hopper and simple, effective shooter to their bold matte black and red styling. Every choice balances aesthetics with performance. When it’s time to claw past the competition and prove that clean design can still hit hard, this machine is pure badger energy.

Close knit and engaged, this team has built a community around FIRST that’s as solid as iron. Their confidence and trust in each other are evident in their collaboration and process. The team is forging the tracks that lead the way to empowerment. This team ensures all team members have the FREEDOM to Engineer their own future.

This team started their rookie year with a steep learning curve and navigating to find their fit. They have leveraged their resources and they are setting up systems to cut through future challenges. From middle school to drive courses, this team chose the hard-core STEM option.

This team’s STEM comes alive in the halls of their high school with all hands on deck. They SQUEEZE out knowledge through training, collaboration, and engagement in FIRST and their community. When the pressure is high, they kick it into OVERDRIVE.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is always willing to lend a helping hand. Focusing on team growth, sharing knowledge with future team leaders, hosting women in STEM nights, and volunteering they ensure the future of FIRST advances throughout their school. This team soars high, inspiring others to follow in their footsteps.

records.teamName: Robo Remedy @ Manitowoc Lutheran High School
records.script: This team is enthusiastic, energetic, and engaging. Dropping positivity throughout the competition. This team encourages and elevates more than their hair.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team had a solid design strategy. Their “pull out hopper” gave more space for fuel, while their VR googles told them where they are. This isn’t’ the Big Apple, but there is no place like home.
This team exemplifies fairness, humility, positivity, and respect. Their creation of a safe space helps teams near and far. Across land and sea, their fire is a beacon to teams in need of help.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has minimized their hopper to move it up and out of the way. When it is time for them to climb, they are bars above the rest. They have not forgotten their roots floating up and away in their balloon.

Modular design and their robot’s ESP has made quality job #1 for this team. They succeeds by knowing what is happening before it happens. Every component in their robot fits together like a perfect hex.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team SPUN UP a unique shooter design for this competition. While always staying in motion, this team exhibits their mastery of robot control from ROUND to ROUND. Known for being in control of the spheres, Atlas leads the pack in innovation.
This team’s autonomous glides back and forth through the trench. Their turret effortlessly tracks as they shoot on the move. Spinning up from the depths they don’t forget the AT in COMP@CT.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has included fun into their colorfully patterned theme. They have discovered innovative ways to leverage the “classics” to level up their numbers. On the field, you may have to look closely because their climber can be difficult to see in 8-bit.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team SURGED ahead with their initiatives to SHIFT students into being more well-RED. Looking to the future, they inspire students of all abilities and cultures to continue and sustain the FIRST Mission. Their TSUNAMI is sure to impact the horizon as they ride the wave to the FIRST Championship.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: District Championship Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: 1 Year! 14 students! 2 seniors! 5 rookies! 73% rookies! 40 events! 2 FLL Teams started! 20,000 inspired! With their outreach, code sharing, event hosting, summer camps, and advocacy, this team is SPARKING a FIRE in their district and community.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team’s robot can hold 40 pieces of fuel and has a turret with a full 360° of rotation. They embraced the physics and calculations needed to build an accurate launcher. Their COMP@CT cable snake kept the fuel flowing.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team has really earned its stripes at this event. Their apprenticeship program ensures student opportunities, mentors and sponsorship. Step aside Tony; there’s a new tiger in town and his name is GREG.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team started with SHARPENED focus to build their FIRST mission. They used their communication skills to get mentors, robot parts and connections to other teams all to cut a path through the woods. Clearly, this team EDGED out their competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team really revved the judges’ engines. They prioritized resourcefulness over resources, embodied core values as they paved the way forward for themselves and other teams. Once they PEELED off their inexperience, they raced to the finish line of a successful season.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This bird of prey is creating a sustainable nest. Their WING SPAN reached from FLL elementary school to local universities. These HAWKS soared through the competition with their pink ribbons flying.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team knows how to bring a BUNCH of energy. They PEELED away boundaries spreading their contagious spirit across the states. Join their RAID by promoting the vision of FIRST in a FRUITFUL Way.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: The team clearly takes pride in every aspect of it’s identity. By utilizing AGILE principles, they brought their stories to life with an efficient design. You won’t lose sight of this team through the steam, because excellence is what they scream.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team’s fierce professionalism was no fairytale. They hosted, they shared, they documented, and they cared . Their events weren’t too hot or too cold. They were just RIGHT.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This rectangular bot was SUPER at plowing through the field. The core structure of the robot allows for easy access to all elements. Their COOKIES don’t crumble even when agitated.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team has a double wide launcher, reinforced plates and a “Bendable” intake bar. They focus on having modular parts that can quickly be replaced. With their replaceable MEG-BAR, they survived aggressive game play with competing at a higher level.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a unique control strategy. Thanks to an innovative spirit, their robot flew across the field while scoring fuel in one fluid motion. Their STATE of the art control system gave them the MOMENTUM to ROLL past the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: From the start of the match, their robot is in full control, navigating the field with confidence. Utilizing robot vision and computations to continuously transform their path to success. By FENCING in their paths, they are able to stay off the ROCKY path.

records.eventName: FIRST Wisconsin State Championship presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is nature-focused with a twist. They demonstrated continuity with colors, creativity and collaboration. TAG! You're it.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: This year's Impact Award winner bubbled to the top of some very good teams. The incredible amount of outreach drowned the judges in information. Somehow, they even found the time to add a 3rd robot class into their school curriculum, bringing waves of change. Congratulations, Team 2826, Wave Robotics.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team is seeing the current year's feeder system really crank. Sponsors provide mentors, alums become mentors. The team joins sponsor volunteer events that feed community outreach. With 73% of the team's 73 members being rookies, the average age of the team is dropping as their impact is rising. Congratulations, team 2194, Fondy Fire.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: This team unleashed a tornado of elegant design on the competition. Huge capacity. Huge range. Huge wins. All made possible by smart material choices and picking the perfect parts for the job. Congratulations, team 930 and their robot Cyclone.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: With every answer, this team plowed us over. Powered by a team of three, working with little - these defensive specialists have been lifting weights to the top. Congrats, team 6732.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: Although a rookie team, they understand Gracious Professionalism as they receive help AND give help to other teams. These rookie team members are clearly early "bloomers". Congratulations, team 11139, Blackhawk Robotics.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: This tight-knit team with strong documentation has kept their young team going. Starting the season with 2 students, a successful recruiting strategy of FTC STEM fairs and sponsor demos helped them to get new students from far and wide. Even though we see a STORM brewing, this team's forecast is bright. Congrats, team 10264.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: From a small town themselves, this team has newer members from an even smaller neighbor. Their gift of gab is great, getting a sponsor on the spot at an event. Recycling is their gig, partnering with the high school octagon club to shape the environmental cleanliness of Two Rivers. Congrats, team 4531.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: It is safe to say this team's unified intro knocked our socks off. Team work, positive energy, and quality alliances make them shine. Their enthusiasm is all the Rage. Congrats team 3381.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This team began with a spin-dex that ROCKED the competition. This was just one PIZZA of the puzzle. Their 2 robots allowed them to excel in engineering. Congratulations, team 1259.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: This team's dedication to the cordial principals of gracious professionalism stands out on and off the field. Always jumping to help, they reach many teams through their generosity. Their collaborative approach is the epitomy of Midwest nice. Congrats team 5826.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They don't just put on shows on the field, but also in their pit. Their robot has a big mouth to eat up every technician's nightmare. They are wired to serve well. Congratulations, team 8700.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: This team's robot is strong enough to hold the world on their shoulders. Perfecting their design with 75 iterations, they really earned a seat at the table. Congratulations, team 1792.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Their virtual view of the field gives them eagle-like precision. Their ad hoc auto controls to cover all blind spots, while use of quest-mapping technology, allows for auto-shooting while in motion. They swoop down, never blind to their target. Congrats, team 706.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.script: During autonomous, this team shines the brightest in the darkest of nights. By offloading vision to an onboard Mac Mini, they used simulations to develop a Pathfinder that constantly checks for states so it can adapt to its surroundings. This team brings the trouble, and makes it double. Congratulations to team 135, Black Knights.

records.eventName: WIN District Seven Rivers Event presented by Mathy Construction Company
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's image reflects their commitment to teamwork and inclusion. Sending those who dare into an adventure of glypns and codes, their light at the end of the tunnel guides the bravest. Rolling out the welcome mat, they invite others to join their secret society. Congrats team 7619.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: This team's innovation, passion and DOCUMENTATION electrified the judges. They transformed elementary STEM education by providing hands-on, fun curriculum, CATAPULTING them to the top of our list. Let's reveal the ELEPHANT in the room.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This dedicated team not only continues to invent hard automation for competition-- they’ve reached out to nearly 10,00 people to convey the importance of the FIRST Ethos. Providing middle school learning opportunities, they grow interest in STEAM in their community with a locomotive force. Join forces with other teams, they help all to move with AGILITY and fiercely LEAN down the RAINBOW ROAD.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: As a LONG-RUNNING TEAM, their experience shows in every detail. Their UNIQUE AGITATOR keeps everything moving reliably. Like an OREO, the CORE of their robot is the crème of the crop.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: Laying down the foundation to rebuild bridges, this team races forward while opening their doors to the next step. Documentation and determination is what has kept this team solid. Their ROCK’N tunes did not miss a beat to keep the rhythm going.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: This team crosses borders and bridges to gain experience, sustain relationships and build skills to be contributing members of the FIRST community. Their forward-thinking focus and their collaborative drive across student organizations, to both recruit and develop membership and sponsorships, will lead to a SUPERIOR future.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: Lets introduce this traditional team. Like many teams, this team has had ups and downs. Keeping their traditions, they are nothing but MONOCHROMATIC, celebrating together with their alum and sponsors. Through all of their tribulations, they are LIGHTING UP the night.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is building a following, sharing the knowledge, maintaining relationships, and establishing GREEN focused ingenuity. They are not AFRAID to be creative in addressing the challenges of today and into the future. This team is leading us OUT OF THE HAZE in a sustainable way.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: This team’s spirit LIGHTENS up any community they are a part of. Beyond showing their energy on their robot, this team has left their TAG on a repaired community RC vehicle. You may have even added your own MASTERPIECE to their collection.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: This veteran team didn’t SLACK OFF when they designed a complete robot which combined QuestNav pathfinding, a circular indexer and an impressive autonomous performance. With an expandable hopper and a turret for shooting fuel, it was no surprise their robot, MORT, climbed to THE TOP this weekend.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: The CEREBRAL POWER of this team doesn’t MISREPRESENT anyone. There isn’t a switch or button in a toy that can’t be empowered. Down to their orange coverings, this BEAST of a team gets it done.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.teamName: Robo Remedy @ Manitowoc Lutheran High School
records.script: This team REQUIRED A CURE for their space constraint. Thinking INSIDE THE BOX, this team’s turret cascaded success. This team REAPED the reward of designing a creative bot.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: This team’s robot DELIVERS consistent performance on the field. Their improvements to their feeding mechanism PROTECTED them from jams. They are a team that exhibits the ULTIMATE in quality.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When this team RUMBLES in, everyone’s HAIR STANDS ON END. Their variable autonomous sets the tone with precision and speed. Their innovative switchboard lets them harness their robot like THOR COMMANDS LIGHTNING.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.script: This teams autonomous looks effortless as they Glide back in forth through the trench. Their auto align shooter, dual cameras, and simplified button layout gave them a leg up on the competition. With their robot as TOUGH AS A ROCK be careful not to hit them, it might create a SPARK.

records.eventName: WIN District Mukwonago Event presented by Regal Rexnord
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: On and off the field, from rookies to seniors, you can SEE FOR yourself this team spreading their image. From their shirts to the pits and their robot down to the zips, their cohesive image is really what hits. With EXPLOSIVE energy, they celebrate with a BANG!

This team impressed the judges as great hosts across many FIRST programs and area groups. Whether they are cooking up alliances with a Saffron like spice, leading gracious SHOWDOWNS between teams, or hosting legislative leaders, this team welcomes all to experience FIRST. And while Raiders may be Bananas for trouble, this team cleary causes Good Trouble across FIRST in Wisconsin

records.awardName: District Engineering Inspiration Award sponsored by SpaceX
records.script: This team believes deeply in both engineering and inspiration. No matter what time of day, this team keeps busy mentoring four LEGO League teams, running summer camps, supporting National Night Out, and hosting a valuable online robotics forum. They also invest an unBEARable amount of energy into FRC, including hosting everything from Regionals to popular off-season events. It is hard to hibernate when your schedule is year round, and you have lofty 1, 3, and 5 year goals.

This team’s design process is a mathematical dream, utilizing the Chinese Remainder Theorem as their guide, they have “Everything working Together” with pride. With a CNC machined spindexer and custom foam rollers in tow, their robot’s high-speed precision is always on show. It’s time to celebrate the robot known as MORT!

With around 20 students and dedicated mentors, this team takes on multiple roles and solving challenges together. They inspire others through Lava Lamps and STEAM Camps and a massive social media presence all to bring fresh members to the club. Some teams do good work, some team do great work, This team always asks for MORE.

This team sure knows how to grow their team thru fundraising, grant writing and even getting a building. The future of this team is Sunny and open like a Praire, so Scrappy is not how we would describe their team’s process.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has a way of reaching out to gather new team members. Their student led organization involves an ORIENTATION which helps rookies open up and find their VOICE! Whether you’re a P.U.G. or a BADGER, they are not afraid to take a breath of fresh air.

This team presented the judges with statistics galore, telling the story of where they started and how they’ve become more. A Bold color scheme fills their community with pride, making them recognizable from far and wide. Through socials media "fits", their feathered mascot is working towards more friends in the pits.

records.awardName: Excellence in Engineering Award sponsored by Littelfuse
records.script: With a clear goal from the season start, they knew they needed to maximize space. Armed with a documented engineering process, they had a robot archetype in mind. They have displayed their Primary Shooter on the field, while opening up their robot Core to the Judges.

This bright and energetic team shows positivity both on and off the field. They support one another by giving shout out, contributing feedback cards and recognizing the efforts of others. This team was Knighted for their outstanding achievements and for their making of a positive impact on everyone around them.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team put carbon fiber to the test with floors and ladders. They lit the way with a spindexer that skipped the fins and brushed their way to success. It flashes, it climbs, it spins, it sweeps, no one can ignore Tubathee Chalamet.

Quality is a product of excellent design, strong construction, and careful maintenance. This team created a sturdy, lightweight frame with extra protection for their wiring. Armed with a thorough post-match checklist and comprehensive spares, they keep their robot in top performance throughout the entire event!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team designed a robot that would dig in to the challenge. They planned controls that can do more than just a push of the robot’s buttons. While normally clad in iron armor, today this team gets to wear a teensy crown.

This team had a vision for a robot with a mind of its own and two-pass collection. With an eyeful of protons, they worked hard and hid from the limelight. With a robot that is shorter than it is long, Gimli knows how to rack up auto points!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some teams find themselves at a crossroads when it comes to team identity. When East meet West, a rebrand was in the paws of this team. Now instead of their school name, their team name is an acronym for STEM & Technology Education.

scope: team judged awards with a published official script
